## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the implementation of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in TGI. VLMs extend text-only language models by accepting both text and image inputs, enabling multimodal understanding and generation capabilities.

For text-only causal language model implementation details, see [Causal Language Models](#3.2). For custom model implementations and optimizations, see [Custom Model Implementations](#3.4).

## Overview

VLMs in TGI inherit from the Flash Causal LM architecture while extending it to handle image inputs. The system supports multiple VLM architectures through a unified interface that handles image preprocessing, token embedding fusion, and attention mechanisms across both text and visual modalities.

**Supported VLM Architectures:**

| Model Type | Model Name | Config Key | Multimodal Token Strategy |
|------------|------------|------------|---------------------------|
| Idefics2 | Idefics 2 | `idefics2` | Fixed 64-token patches with splitting |
| Idefics3 | Idefics 3 | `idefics3` | Dynamic row/col grid tokens |
| LlavaNext | Llava Next (1.6) | `llava_next` | Anyres grid-based features |
| PaliGemma | PaliGemma | `paligemma` | Fixed `num_image_tokens` from config |
| Qwen2VL | Qwen 2 VL | `qwen2_vl` | Vision pad tokens with grid_thw |
| Qwen2_5VL | Qwen 2.5 VL | `qwen2_5_vl` | Vision pad tokens with grid_thw |
| Gemma3 | Gemma3 | `gemma3` | Image soft tokens (256) |
| Llama4 | Llama4 | `llama4` | Aspect-ratio based patches |
| Mllama | Mllama | `mllama` | Cross-attention states |

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/__init__.py:228-417](), [docs/source/supported_models.md:8-44]()

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "VLM Request Flow"
        Request["generate_pb2.Request<br/>text + image chunks"]
        Tokenizer["Tokenizer"]
        ImageProcessor["Image Processor<br/>processor.image_processor()"]
        
        Request --> |"text chunks"| Tokenizer
        Request --> |"image chunks"| ImageProcessor
        
        Tokenizer --> TextTokens["Text Token IDs"]
        ImageProcessor --> ImageInputs["Image Inputs<br/>pixel_values, aspect_ratios"]
        
        TextTokens --> Replacement["image_text_replacement()<br/>Insert image placeholder tokens"]
        ImageInputs --> Replacement
        
        Replacement --> MergedTokens["Merged Token Sequence<br/>with image placeholders"]
    end
    
    subgraph "VlmCausalLMBatch"
        MergedTokens --> Batch["VlmCausalLMBatch"]
        Batch --> BatchFields["- input_ids<br/>- image_inputs<br/>- image_positions<br/>- encoder_cache"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Forward"
        BatchFields --> EmbedLayer["Embedding Layer"]
        ImageInputs --> VisionEncoder["Vision Encoder"]
        
        VisionEncoder --> ImageEmbeds["Image Embeddings"]
        EmbedLayer --> TextEmbeds["Text Embeddings"]
        
        ImageEmbeds --> Fusion["scatter_image_embeds()<br/>Fuse at image_positions"]
        TextEmbeds --> Fusion
        
        Fusion --> FusedEmbeds["Fused Input Embeddings"]
        FusedEmbeds --> Transformer["Transformer Layers"]
    end
```

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:301-376](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:113-183]()

## VlmCausalLMBatch Structure

The `VlmCausalLMBatch` class extends `FlashCausalLMBatch` with image-specific metadata and processing capabilities.

### Core VLM Fields

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class FlashCausalLMBatch {
        +input_ids: Tensor
        +position_ids: Tensor
        +slot_indices: Tensor
        +block_tables: List
        +prefilling: bool
    }
    
    class VlmCausalLMBatch {
        +image_inputs: List[List[Dict]]
        +image_positions: List[List[ImagePositions]]
        +encoder_cache: List[Dict]
        +pixel_values: List[Tensor]
        +pixel_attention_mask: List[Tensor]
        +image_sizes: List[Tuple]
        +image_grid_thw: Tensor
        +has_image_inputs: bool
        +inputs_embeds: Tensor
        +cache_entries_to_free: List
        +concatenate()
        +filter()
        +batch_tokenized_inputs()
    }
    
    class ImagePositions {
        +offset: int
        +length: int
        +id: int
        +num_placeholder_tokens: int
        +is_embed: Optional[Tensor]
    }
    
    FlashCausalLMBatch <|-- VlmCausalLMBatch
    VlmCausalLMBatch --> ImagePositions
```

### ImagePositions Dataclass

The `ImagePositions` dataclass tracks where image tokens appear in the input sequence:

- `offset`: Starting position in the token sequence
- `length`: Total length of image token span
- `id`: Unique identifier for this image in the request
- `num_placeholder_tokens`: Number of actual image placeholder tokens (vs text tokens)
- `is_embed`: Boolean tensor indicating which positions are image embeddings

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:292-299](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:301-312]()

## Image Processing Pipeline

### Image Input Parsing

The image processing pipeline handles mixed text/image inputs from protobuf requests:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Request Input Chunks"
        TextChunk1["chunk.text"]
        ImageChunk["chunk.image.data"]
        TextChunk2["chunk.text"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing"
        TextChunk1 --> |"preprocess_text()"| ProcessedText1["Processed Text"]
        ImageChunk --> |"Image.open()"| PILImage["PIL Image"]
        PILImage --> |"preprocess_image()"| PrepImage["Preprocessed Image"]
        PrepImage --> |"processor.image_processor()"| ImgInput["image_input dict"]
        ImgInput --> |"image_text_replacement()"| ImgTokens["Image Placeholder Tokens"]
        TextChunk2 --> ProcessedText2["Processed Text"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        ProcessedText1 --> Concat["Concatenate"]
        ImgTokens --> Concat
        ProcessedText2 --> Concat
        Concat --> FullText["Full Text with Image Tokens"]
        FullText --> Tokenize["tokenizer()"]
        Tokenize --> InputIDs["input_ids"]
    end
```

### Model-Specific Image Preprocessing

Different VLM architectures require specific preprocessing steps:

**PaliGemma:**
- Prepends `<bos>` token to text
- Converts images to RGB format
- Wraps image in list for processor

**Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL:**
- Resizes small images (width ≤ 20) by 2x to avoid processing issues
- Uses grid-based vision pad tokens

**Llava Next / Gemma3 / Llama4:**
- Processes single images directly (not wrapped in list)
- Uses anyres or aspect-ratio based resolutions

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:194-212](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:406-428]()

### Image-to-Token Replacement

The `image_text_replacement()` function generates placeholder token sequences for each image:

```mermaid
graph TD
    ImageInput["Image Input"] --> ModelType{"model_type"}
    
    ModelType --> |"idefics2"| Idefics2["IDEFICS2_FAKE_TOKEN +<br/>IDEFICS2_IMAGE_TOKEN * 64 +<br/>IDEFICS2_FAKE_TOKEN<br/>(×5 if splitting)"]
    
    ModelType --> |"idefics3"| Idefics3["_prompt_split_image()<br/>row/col grid structure<br/>with GLOBAL_IMG_TOKEN"]
    
    ModelType --> |"llava_next"| LlavaNext["get_number_of_features()<br/>IMAGE_TOKEN * num_features"]
    
    ModelType --> |"paligemma"| Paligemma["IMAGE_TOKEN *<br/>num_image_tokens from config"]
    
    ModelType --> |"qwen2_vl"<br/>"qwen2_5_vl"| Qwen2VL["VISION_START +<br/>IMAGE_PAD * (grid_t×grid_h×grid_w÷4) +<br/>VISION_END"]
    
    ModelType --> |"gemma3"| Gemma3["START_OF_IMAGE +<br/>image_soft_token * 256 +<br/>END_OF_IMAGE"]
    
    ModelType --> |"llama4"| Llama4["prompt_split_image_llama4()<br/>aspect-ratio based patches"]
    
    Idefics2 --> Return["Return image_str, start_token"]
    Idefics3 --> Return
    LlavaNext --> Return
    Paligemma --> Return
    Qwen2VL --> Return
    Gemma3 --> Return
    Llama4 --> Return
```

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:113-183](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:33-57](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:61-87]()

## Feature Count Calculation

The router layer calculates the number of image features for each VLM architecture to properly allocate tokens:

### Llava Next Feature Calculation

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["Image: height, width"] --> GridShape["get_anyres_image_grid_shape()<br/>Select best resolution from pinpoints"]
    GridShape --> Pinpoints["image_grid_pinpoints<br/>e.g., [[336,672], [672,336], ...]"]
    Pinpoints --> BestFit["select_best_resolution()<br/>Maximize effective resolution"]
    BestFit --> Patches["num_patch_height, num_patch_width"]
    
    Patches --> Unpadded["get_unpadded_features()<br/>Calculate actual content area"]
    Unpadded --> UnpaddedCount["unpadded_features"]
    Unpadded --> NewlineCount["newline_features"]
    
    ImageSize["image_size ÷ patch_size"] --> NPatches["npatches"]
    NPatches --> BaseFeatures["base_features = npatches²"]
    
    UnpaddedCount --> Total["Total Features"]
    NewlineCount --> Total
    BaseFeatures --> Total
```

### Llama4 Aspect Ratio Calculation

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["Image: height, width"] --> MaxChunks["max_chunks parameter"]
    MaxChunks --> Supported["find_supported_resolutions()<br/>Generate all factor combinations"]
    Supported --> Factors["All possible (h,w) pairs<br/>from chunk factorizations"]
    Factors --> BestFit["get_best_fit()<br/>Choose best aspect ratio match"]
    BestFit --> TargetRes["target_height, target_width"]
    TargetRes --> AspectRatio["aspect_ratios = (h÷patch_size, w÷patch_size)"]
```

**Sources:** [router/src/config.rs:88-105](), [router/src/config.rs:220-242](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:242-266]()

## Image Embedding Fusion

The system uses scatter/gather operations to fuse image embeddings into the text token sequence:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Model as VlmCausalLM
    participant Embed as Embedding Layer
    participant Vision as Vision Encoder
    participant Scatter as scatter_image_embeds
    
    Model->>Embed: input_ids (text tokens)
    Embed-->>Model: text_embeddings [seq_len, hidden_size]
    
    Model->>Vision: pixel_values (images)
    Vision-->>Model: image_embeddings [num_image_tokens, hidden_size]
    
    Model->>Scatter: Fuse at image_positions
    Note over Scatter: is_embed mask indicates<br/>which positions are images
    
    Scatter->>Scatter: Create placeholder tensor<br/>filled with NaN
    Scatter->>Scatter: placeholders[is_embed] = image_embeddings
    Scatter-->>Model: fused_embeddings [seq_len, hidden_size]
    
    Model->>Model: Forward through transformer<br/>with fused embeddings
```

### Scatter/Gather Implementation

The `scatter_image_embeds()` function places image embeddings at their designated positions:

- Creates a tensor of NaN placeholders matching the full sequence length
- Uses the `is_embed` boolean tensor to scatter image embeddings
- Returns fused embeddings where images replace text tokens at specific positions

The `gather_image_embeds()` function extracts only the image embedding positions:

- Uses `is_embed` mask to select image positions
- Returns extracted embeddings or None if no images present

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:269-289](), [backends/gaudi/server/text_generation_server/models/flash_vlm_causal_lm.py:280-301]()

## Batch Operations

### Concatenation

When merging multiple `VlmCausalLMBatch` instances:

1. Calls parent `FlashCausalLMBatch.concatenate()` for text-specific fields
2. Extends `image_inputs`, `image_positions`, and `encoder_cache` lists
3. Resets tensor fields (`pixel_values`, `image_sizes`, etc.) to None
4. Sets `has_image_inputs` to False (re-computed in `prepare_for_prefill`)

### Filtering

When filtering a batch to a subset of requests:

1. Calls parent `filter()` to handle text fields
2. Filters `image_inputs`, `image_positions`, and `encoder_cache` based on request indices
3. Resets image tensor fields
4. Maintains image data structure for selected requests only

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:314-345](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:347-376]()

## Cross-Backend Support

### CUDA Backend

The CUDA backend implementation in [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py]() provides:

- Flash Attention integration for image-text fusion
- Efficient memory pooling for image embeddings
- Standard PyTorch vision encoder execution

### Gaudi Backend

The Gaudi backend implementation in [backends/gaudi/server/text_generation_server/models/flash_vlm_causal_lm.py]() includes:

- HPU-specific tensor operations using `htorch`
- Custom attention metadata (`HPUPagedAttentionMetadata`) 
- Memory profiling via `HabanaMemoryProfiler`
- Synchronization points with `htorch.core.mark_step()`

**Key Differences:**

| Aspect | CUDA Backend | Gaudi Backend |
|--------|--------------|---------------|
| Attention | Flash Attention 2 | HPU Paged Attention |
| Memory | MEM_POOL global | HPU memory profiler |
| Tensor Copy | Direct device placement | `_async_h2d_tensor_copy()` |
| Synchronization | CUDA streams | `htorch.core.mark_step()` |

**Sources:** [backends/gaudi/server/text_generation_server/models/flash_vlm_causal_lm.py:1-40](), [backends/gaudi/server/text_generation_server/models/flash_vlm_causal_lm.py:312-384]()

## Mllama Special Implementation

The Mllama model uses a unique cross-attention architecture requiring special handling:

### FlashMllamaCausalLMBatch

Extends `FlashVlmCausalLMBatch` with cross-attention specific fields:

- `cross_attention_states`: Pre-computed vision embeddings for cross-attention
- `image_indices`: Maps which batch indices contain images
- `aspect_ratio_ids`, `aspect_ratio_mask`: Aspect ratio metadata for vision encoder

### Cross-Attention State Generation

```mermaid
graph TD
    VisionEncoder["Vision Encoder"] --> CrossAttnStates["cross_attention_states<br/>[num_images, seq_len, hidden_size]"]
    ImageIndices["image_indices<br/>[batch positions with images]"] --> Mapping["generate_cross_attention_states()"]
    CrossAttnStates --> Mapping
    InputLengths["input_lengths<br/>[batch_size]"] --> Mapping
    
    Mapping --> |"prefilling=True"| PrefillIndices["Expand to sequence length:<br/>range(pad_seq_len×i, pad_seq_len×(i+1))"]
    Mapping --> |"prefilling=False"| DecodeIndices["Use direct indices:<br/>image_indices[:]"]
    
    PrefillIndices --> Return["Return indices, cross_attention_len"]
    DecodeIndices --> Return
```

The cross-attention states are:
- Pre-computed during prefill from the vision encoder
- Cached in batch for reuse during decode steps
- Indexed per batch position to enable cross-attention in transformer layers

**Sources:** [backends/gaudi/server/text_generation_server/models/mllama_causal_lm.py:44-113](), [backends/gaudi/server/text_generation_server/models/mllama_causal_lm.py:225-238]()

## Model Initialization Flow

### Model Selection Logic

```mermaid
graph TD
    GetModel["get_model()"] --> ConfigDict["Load config_dict<br/>from model_id"]
    ConfigDict --> ModelType{"model_type"}
    
    ModelType --> |"idefics2"| Idefics2Check{"processor.image_processor_class<br/>== 'Idefics2ImageProcessor'"}
    ModelType --> |"idefics3"| Idefics3Check{"processor.image_processor_class<br/>== 'Idefics3ImageProcessor'"}
    ModelType --> |"llava_next"| LlavaNextLoad["IdeficsCausalLM with<br/>LlavaNextForConditionalGeneration"]
    ModelType --> |"paligemma"| PaligemmaLoad["IdeficsCausalLM with<br/>PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration"]
    ModelType --> |"qwen2_vl"| Qwen2VLLoad["IdeficsCausalLM with<br/>Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration"]
    ModelType --> |"qwen2_5_vl"| Qwen25VLLoad["IdeficsCausalLM with<br/>Qwen2_5VLForConditionalGeneration"]
    ModelType --> |"mllama"| MllamaLoad["MllamaCausalLM with<br/>MllamaForConditionalGeneration"]
    ModelType --> |"llama4"| Llama4Load["TransformersLlama4VlmCausalLM with<br/>Llama4ForConditionalGeneration"]
    ModelType --> |"gemma3"| Gemma3Load["TransformersGemma3VlmCausalLM with<br/>Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration"]
    
    Idefics2Check --> |"Yes"| Idefics2Load["IdeficsCausalLM with<br/>Idefics2ForConditionalGeneration"]
    Idefics3Check --> |"Yes"| Idefics3Load["IdeficsCausalLM with<br/>Idefics3ForConditionalGeneration"]
    
    Idefics2Load --> Return["Return Model Instance"]
    Idefics3Load --> Return
    LlavaNextLoad --> Return
    PaligemmaLoad --> Return
    Qwen2VLLoad --> Return
    Qwen25VLLoad --> Return
    MllamaLoad --> Return
    Llama4Load --> Return
    Gemma3Load --> Return
```

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/__init__.py:1115-1192](), [server/text_generation_server/models/__init__.py:1194-1222]()

## Encoder Cache Management

The VLM system implements an encoder cache to avoid recomputing image embeddings:

### Cache Structure

- `encoder_cache`: `List[Dict[int, torch.Tensor]]` - One dict per request
- Key: Image ID (int) from `image_positions.id`
- Value: Pre-computed image embeddings tensor

### Cache Lifecycle

1. **Prefill Phase**: Images are encoded and stored in cache with their IDs
2. **Decode Phase**: Cache entries are retrieved using image IDs
3. **Filtering**: Cache is preserved for surviving requests, others freed
4. **Concatenation**: Cache lists are merged from multiple batches

The cache enables efficient reuse of expensive vision encoder computations across decode steps.

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:304](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:330-333](), [server/text_generation_server/models/vlm_causal_lm.py:354-360]()

- [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_neox_modeling.py](server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_neox_modeling.py)
- [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_phi_modeling.py](server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_phi_modeling.py)
- [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_rw_modeling.py](server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_rw_modeling.py)
- [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py](server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py)
- [server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py](server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document describes TGI's custom model implementations located in [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/](). These are optimized PyTorch modules that replace standard Transformers implementations to achieve higher throughput and lower latency through flash attention, paged attention, tensor parallelism, and custom kernels.

For information about how models are loaded and initialized, see [Model Loading and Initialization](#3.1). For details on attention optimizations, see [Attention Mechanisms](#4.2). For the higher-level model serving infrastructure, see [Model Server Component](#2.3).

---

## Overview

Custom model implementations in TGI are hand-optimized PyTorch modules that implement specific model architectures (Llama, Mistral, Mixtral, etc.) with performance enhancements not available in standard Transformers models. Each implementation follows a consistent pattern but includes architecture-specific optimizations.

### Why Custom Implementations

Standard Transformers models are not optimized for high-throughput inference scenarios. TGI's custom implementations provide:

- **Flash Attention v2** integration for memory-efficient attention computation
- **Paged Attention** support for efficient KV cache management
- **Fused operations** to reduce kernel launch overhead
- **Tensor parallelism** for multi-GPU sharding
- **Custom weight loading** that handles sharding and quantization
- **Adapter support** for LoRA and other parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:1-704](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_mistral_modeling.py:1-541]()

---

## Common Architecture Pattern

All custom model implementations follow a four-layer hierarchy:

```mermaid
graph TD
    ForCausalLM["FlashXXXForCausalLM<br/>(Top-level wrapper)"]
    Model["FlashXXXModel<br/>(Layer stack)"]
    Layer["FlashXXXLayer<br/>(Single transformer layer)"]
    Attention["FlashXXXAttention<br/>(Attention mechanism)"]
    MLP["XXXMLP<br/>(Feed-forward network)"]
    
    ForCausalLM --> Model
    Model --> Layer
    Layer --> Attention
    Layer --> MLP
    
    ForCausalLM --> EmbedTokens["embed_tokens<br/>TensorParallelEmbedding"]
    ForCausalLM --> LMHead["lm_head<br/>SpeculativeHead"]
    Model --> Norm["norm<br/>FastRMSNorm/FastLayerNorm"]
    Layer --> InputNorm["input_layernorm"]
    Layer --> PostAttnNorm["post_attention_layernorm"]
```

**Diagram: Four-Layer Model Hierarchy**

This pattern appears across all implementations with minor variations. Each level has specific responsibilities:

| Level | Class Pattern | Responsibilities |
|-------|--------------|------------------|
| **ForCausalLM** | `FlashXXXForCausalLM` | Embedding lookup, model forward, LM head projection |
| **Model** | `FlashXXXModel` | Layer iteration, final normalization, rotary embedding management |
| **Layer** | `FlashXXXLayer` | Pre/post normalization, attention+MLP orchestration, residual connections |
| **Attention** | `FlashXXXAttention` | QKV projection, rotary embeddings, flash/paged attention |
| **MLP** | `XXXMLP` | Gate/up projection fusion, activation, down projection |

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:617-704](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:503-615](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:407-501]()

---

## Weight Loading System

Custom models use the `Weights` abstraction for loading and sharding model weights. This system handles tensor parallelism, quantization, and adapter weights uniformly across all model types.

```mermaid
graph LR
    Weights["Weights<br/>(Safetensors routing)"]
    WeightsLoader["WeightsLoader<br/>(Abstract loader)"]
    
    DefaultLoader["DefaultWeightsLoader"]
    GPTQLoader["GPTQWeightsLoader"]
    FP8Loader["HybridFP8UnquantLoader"]
    
    Weights --> WeightsLoader
    WeightsLoader --> DefaultLoader
    WeightsLoader --> GPTQLoader
    WeightsLoader --> FP8Loader
    
    DefaultLoader --> UnquantizedWeight
    GPTQLoader --> GPTQWeight
    FP8Loader --> Fp8Weight
    
    UnquantizedWeight --> GetLinear["get_linear(weight, bias)"]
    GPTQWeight --> GetLinear
    Fp8Weight --> GetLinear
    
    GetLinear --> FastLinear
    GetLinear --> FastLinearROCm
    GetLinear --> QuantizedLinear["Quantized Linear Layers"]
```

**Diagram: Weight Loading and Quantization System**

### Key Loading Functions

Different architectures require different weight loading strategies:

**Standard QKV Loading (Llama, Mistral):**
```python
# server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:72-122
def load_attention(config, prefix: str, weights, layer_id):
    # Load separate q_proj, k_proj, v_proj or fused qkv_proj
    # Handle tensor parallelism sharding
    # Return TensorParallelMultiAdapterLinear for LoRA support
```

**Packed QKV Loading (GPT-2, Santacoder):**
```python
# server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_gpt2_modeling.py:42-133
def load_qkv(config, prefix: str, weights, head_size, num_heads):
    # Load from transposed, packed c_attn weight
    # Split into Q, K, V with proper sharding
```

**MoE Expert Loading (Mixtral, DBRX):**
```python
# server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_mixtral_modeling.py:146-180
def _load_experts(config, prefix: str, mat, weights):
    # Load all experts with proper sharding
    # Handle w1/w2/w3 matrices for each expert
```

### Sharding Methods

The `Weights` class provides several sharding methods for tensor parallelism:

| Method | Purpose | Usage |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `get_sharded` | Shard single tensor along dimension | Row/column linear sharding |
| `get_packed_sharded` | Shard packed tensor (QKV, gate-up) | Attention and MLP fusion |
| `get_multi_weights_col` | Concatenate and shard multiple tensors | Loading q_proj + k_proj + v_proj |
| `get_weights_row` | Row-wise sharding via loader | Output projections |

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py:139-443](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:72-122]()

---

## Attention Mechanism Implementation

All custom implementations use a two-phase attention strategy: flash attention for prefill and paged attention for decode.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["hidden_states<br/>(batch, hidden_size)"]
    QKV["query_key_value<br/>TensorParallelMultiAdapterLinear"]
    
    Split["Split QKV"]
    Query["query<br/>(batch, num_heads, head_size)"]
    KV["kv<br/>(batch, 2, num_kv_heads, head_size)"]
    
    Rotary["rotary_emb<br/>PositionRotaryEmbedding"]
    
    Store["kv_cache.store()<br/>Store in paged cache"]
    
    PrefillCheck{{"cu_seqlen_prefill<br/>is not None?"}}
    
    FlashAttn["attention()<br/>Flash Attention v2"]
    PagedAttn["paged_attention()<br/>Paged Attention"]
    
    OProj["o_proj<br/>TensorParallelAdapterRowLinear"]
    Output["attn_output"]
    
    Input --> QKV
    QKV --> Split
    Split --> Query
    Split --> KV
    
    Query --> Rotary
    KV --> Rotary
    
    Rotary --> Store
    Store --> PrefillCheck
    
    PrefillCheck -->|"Yes (Prefill)"| FlashAttn
    PrefillCheck -->|"No (Decode)"| PagedAttn
    
    FlashAttn --> OProj
    PagedAttn --> OProj
    OProj --> Output
```

**Diagram: Attention Forward Pass Flow**

### Common Attention Structure

All attention implementations follow this pattern in [flash_llama_modeling.py:137-268](), [flash_mistral_modeling.py:111-250]():

```
1. QKV Projection: Linear transformation with optional LoRA adapters
2. Reshape: View as (batch, heads, head_size)
3. Rotary Embeddings: Apply rotary position embeddings to Q and K
4. KV Cache Store: Store key/value in paged cache
5. Attention Computation:
   - Prefill: Flash Attention v2 (memory-efficient)
   - Decode: Paged Attention (uses cached KV)
6. Output Projection: Linear transformation with optional LoRA adapters
```

### Architecture-Specific Variations

| Model | Key Difference | Implementation |
|-------|---------------|----------------|
| **Llama** | Standard GQA, RMSNorm | [flash_llama_modeling.py:137-268]() |
| **Mistral** | Sliding window attention | [flash_mistral_modeling.py:111-250]() |
| **Phi** | Partial rotary embeddings | [flash_phi_modeling.py:107-224]() |
| **GPT-2** | No rotary, learned positions | [flash_gpt2_modeling.py:169-261]() |
| **Cohere** | Custom rotary, Q/K normalization | [flash_cohere_modeling.py:201-327]() |
| **Gemma2** | Softcap, alternating sliding window | [flash_gemma2_modeling.py:164-296]() |

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:137-268](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_mistral_modeling.py:111-250](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_phi_modeling.py:107-224]()

---

## MLP/FFN Layer Implementation

Most modern architectures use gated MLPs with fused gate/up projections for efficiency.

```mermaid
graph LR
    Input["hidden_states"]
    
    GateUp["gate_up_proj<br/>TensorParallelMultiAdapterLinear<br/>(2 * intermediate_size)"]
    
    View["view(-1, 2, intermediate_size)"]
    
    Gate["gate_states<br/>[..., 0]"]
    Up["up_states<br/>[..., 1]"]
    
    Act["act(gate_states)<br/>SiLU/GELU"]
    
    Mul["act * up_states"]
    
    Down["down_proj<br/>TensorParallelAdapterRowLinear"]
    
    Output["mlp_output"]
    
    Input --> GateUp
    GateUp --> View
    View --> Gate
    View --> Up
    Gate --> Act
    Act --> Mul
    Up --> Mul
    Mul --> Down
    Down --> Output
```

**Diagram: Gated MLP Forward Pass (Llama, Mistral, Gemma)**

### Standard Gated MLP Pattern

The gated MLP pattern in [flash_llama_modeling.py:306-405]() fuses `gate_proj` and `up_proj` into a single linear layer to reduce kernel launches:

```
1. Gate-Up Fusion: Load gate_proj and up_proj as single (2*intermediate_size, hidden_size) matrix
2. Single Forward: One matmul instead of two
3. View Reshape: Split output into gate and up components
4. Gated Activation: act(gate) * up
5. Down Projection: Final linear layer
```

### ROCm-Specific Optimizations

On AMD ROCm systems, custom kernels optimize small batch inference in [flash_llama_modeling.py:379-404]():

```python
if (SYSTEM == "rocm" and self.hidden_act == "silu" 
    and hidden_states.dtype == torch.float16
    and hidden_states.shape[0] == 1
    and not self.quantize):
    # Use LLMM_Silu fused kernel for batch_size=1
    ops.LLMM_Silu(self.gate_up_proj.weight, hidden_states, out, 8)
```

### MoE Implementations

Mixtral and DBRX use Mixture-of-Experts instead of standard MLPs:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["hidden_states"]
    Gate["gate(x)<br/>FastLinear"]
    RouterLogits["router_logits<br/>(num_tokens, n_experts)"]
    
    SelectExperts["select_experts()<br/>Top-K selection"]
    Weights["expert_weights"]
    Indices["selected_experts"]
    
    MoE["moe(x, gating_output)<br/>SparseMoELayer or DenseMoELayer"]
    
    AllReduce{{"process_group.size > 1?"}}
    Reduce["torch.distributed.all_reduce"]
    
    Output["moe_output"]
    
    Input --> Gate
    Gate --> RouterLogits
    RouterLogits --> SelectExperts
    SelectExperts --> Weights
    SelectExperts --> Indices
    
    Input --> MoE
    RouterLogits --> MoE
    
    MoE --> AllReduce
    AllReduce -->|Yes| Reduce
    AllReduce -->|No| Output
    Reduce --> Output
```

**Diagram: Mixture-of-Experts Forward Pass**

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:306-405](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_mixtral_modeling.py:317-352](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_dbrx_modeling.py:451-549]()

---

## Layer Structure and Residual Connections

Transformer layers orchestrate attention and MLP with normalization and residual connections. TGI uses fused residual operations for efficiency.

### Standard Layer Pattern (Llama, Mistral, Gemma)

The pattern in [flash_llama_modeling.py:407-501]() uses pre-normalization with fused residual addition:

```
Input: (hidden_states, residual)

1. input_layernorm(hidden_states, residual) -> (normed, new_residual)
   # Fuses: residual_add + rms_norm
   
2. attn_output = self_attn(normed, ...)

3. post_attention_layernorm(attn_output, new_residual) -> (normed2, attn_residual)
   # Fuses: residual_add + rms_norm
   
4. mlp_output = mlp(normed2, ...)

Output: (mlp_output, attn_residual)
```

This pattern eliminates explicit residual addition operations, fusing them into the normalization kernels for better performance.

### Parallel Residual Pattern (GPT-NeoX, Falcon)

Some models compute attention and MLP in parallel rather than sequentially:

```python
# server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_neox_modeling.py:270-316
if self.use_parallel_residual:
    ln1_hidden_states, _ = self.input_layernorm(hidden_states)
    attn_output = self.attention(ln1_hidden_states, ...)
    
    ln2_hidden_states, _ = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states)
    mlp_output = self.mlp(ln2_hidden_states)
    
    intermediate = mlp_output + attn_output
    return intermediate + hidden_states, None
```

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:407-501](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_neox_modeling.py:233-316](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_rw_modeling.py:381-487]()

---

## Model and ForCausalLM Wrappers

The top two layers handle embedding, layer iteration, and language modeling head projection.

### FlashXXXModel Responsibilities

The model class in [flash_llama_modeling.py:503-615]() manages:

1. **Layer Stack Initialization**: Create all transformer layers with proper FP8 handling
2. **Rotary Embedding Caching**: Pre-compute cos/sin for efficiency
3. **Layer Iteration**: Forward through all layers with residual tracking
4. **Final Normalization**: Apply final layer norm

```python
# Key pattern from flash_llama_modeling.py:572-614
def forward(self, inputs_embeds, position_ids, cu_seqlen_prefill, 
            kv_cache, block_tables, slots, seqlen, max_s, ...):
    hidden_states = inputs_embeds
    
    # Pre-compute rotary embeddings once
    cos, sin = self.layers[0].self_attn.rotary_emb.get_cos_sin(
        position_ids, max_s, hidden_states.dtype
    )
    
    residual = None
    for i, layer in enumerate(self.layers):
        hidden_states, residual = layer(
            hidden_states, residual, cos, sin, cu_seqlen_prefill,
            kv_cache[i], block_tables, slots, seqlen, max_s, adapter_data
        )
    
    hidden_states, _ = self.norm(hidden_states, residual)
    return hidden_states
```

### FlashXXXForCausalLM Responsibilities

The ForCausalLM wrapper in [flash_llama_modeling.py:617-704]() handles:

1. **Embedding Lookup**: `embed_tokens` for token IDs to embeddings
2. **Model Forward**: Call the main model
3. **Selective Indexing**: Apply `lm_head_indices` for efficient generation
4. **LM Head Projection**: Project to vocabulary space via `SpeculativeHead`
5. **Speculative Decoding**: Return both main and speculative logits if enabled

### FP8 Handling

TGI selectively disables FP8 quantization for first/last layers using the `no_fp8` context manager:

```python
# server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:514-523
with no_fp8(weights):
    self.layers.append(
        FlashLlamaLayer(index=0, ...)  # First layer
    )

# Middle layers use FP8 if configured
for layer_id in range(1, config.num_hidden_layers - 1):
    self.layers.append(FlashLlamaLayer(...))

with no_fp8(weights):
    self.layers.append(
        FlashLlamaLayer(index=last_layer_id, ...)  # Last layer
    )
```

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:503-615](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:617-704](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:124-135]()

---

## Model-Specific Implementation Details

### Llama Family (Llama 2, Llama 3, Granite)

File: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:1-704]()

**Key Features:**
- Supports both standard attention and cross-attention (for vision models like Mllama)
- Handles Phi3 packed QKV format and Baichuan W_pack format
- Supports Granite-specific config: `attention_multiplier`, `residual_multiplier`, `logits_scaling`, `embedding_multiplier`
- Extensive LoRA adapter support via `TensorParallelMultiAdapterLinear`

**Unique Code Paths:**
```python
# Lines 72-122: Multi-format attention loading
if config.model_type == "phi3":
    base_layer = TensorParallelColumnLinear.load_qkv(...)
elif config.model_type == "baichuan":
    base_layer = TensorParallelColumnLinear.load_qkv(...)
else:
    # Standard Llama q_proj, k_proj, v_proj
    base_layer = TensorParallelColumnLinear.load_multi(...)
```

### Mistral and Mixtral

Files: [flash_mistral_modeling.py:1-541](), [flash_mixtral_modeling.py:1-549]()

**Key Features:**
- Sliding window attention support (`config.sliding_window`)
- Mixtral adds Mixture-of-Experts with dynamic expert selection
- Both support FP8 and various quantization formats

**MoE Expert Selection:**
```python
# flash_mixtral_modeling.py:299-309
@torch.jit.script
def select_experts(gate_logits: torch.Tensor, top_k: int):
    all_probs = torch.nn.functional.softmax(gate_logits, dim=1, dtype=torch.float)
    weights, selected_experts = torch.topk(all_probs, top_k, dim=-1)
    weights /= weights.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    return selected_experts.view(-1), weights.view(-1)
```

### Gemma and Gemma2

Files: [flash_gemma_modeling.py:1-487](), [flash_gemma2_modeling.py:1-547]()

**Key Features:**
- Custom `GemmaFastRMSNorm` that adds 1 to weights and operates in FP32
- Gemma2 adds logit softcapping and query pre-attention scaling
- Gemma2 uses alternating sliding window (every other layer)

**Gemma2 Softcapping:**
```python
# flash_gemma2_modeling.py:185-196
self.softmax_scale = config.query_pre_attn_scalar**-0.5
self.softcap = config.attn_logit_softcapping

# In attention call
attn_output = attention(
    query=query, key=kv[:, 0], value=kv[:, 1],
    softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale,
    softcap=self.softcap,  # Caps logits before softmax
    window_size_left=self.window_size
)
```

### Santacoder and GPT-2

Files: [flash_santacoder_modeling.py:1-514](), [flash_gpt2_modeling.py:1-469]()

**Key Features:**
- Multi-Query Attention (MQA) with single KV head
- Transposed weight matrices (column-major format)
- Learned position embeddings instead of rotary
- Special GPTQ loading for packed c_attn weights

### DBRX

File: [flash_dbrx_modeling.py:1-673]()

**Key Features:**
- Fine-grained MoE with 16 experts, top-4 routing
- Expert normalization controlled by `moe_normalize_expert_weights`
- Custom config structure with nested `DbrxAttentionConfig` and `DbrxFFNConfig`
- Supports both CUDA MOE kernels and IPEX GatedMLPMOE

### Cohere

File: [flash_cohere_modeling.py:1-532]()

**Key Features:**
- Custom `CohereLayerNorm` that applies separate normalization per head
- Optional Q/K normalization layers (`use_qk_norm`)
- Custom `CohereRotary` that dispatches to platform-specific implementations
- Logit scaling support

**Sources:** All files in [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/]()

---

## Integration with TGI Infrastructure

Custom implementations integrate with TGI through several key interfaces:

### 1. Weight Loading Contract

All implementations use the `Weights` object for loading:

```python
def __init__(self, prefix: str, config, weights: Weights):
    # Access weights via:
    tensor = weights.get_tensor(f"{prefix}.weight")
    sharded = weights.get_sharded(f"{prefix}.weight", dim=0)
    multi = weights.get_multi_weights_col([...], dim=0)
```

### 2. Forward Pass Signature

All `forward()` methods accept the same core arguments for continuous batching:

| Argument | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `input_ids` or `inputs_embeds` | `torch.Tensor` | Input tokens or embeddings |
| `position_ids` | `torch.Tensor` | Position indices for rotary embeddings |
| `cu_seqlen_prefill` | `Optional[torch.Tensor]` | Cumulative sequence lengths (prefill only) |
| `kv_cache` | `List[KVCache]` | Paged KV cache per layer |
| `block_tables` | `torch.Tensor` | Virtual to physical block mapping |
| `slots` | `torch.Tensor` | Cache slot indices for each token |
| `seqlen` | `Seqlen` | Sequence lengths per request |
| `max_s` | `int` | Maximum sequence length in batch |
| `lm_head_indices` | `Optional[torch.Tensor]` | Indices for selective logit computation |
| `adapter_data` | `Optional[torch.Tensor]` | LoRA adapter routing information |

### 3. Layer Norm Fusion

All implementations use fused layer norms from [server/text_generation_server/layers/layernorm.py]():

- `FastRMSNorm`: Fused RMS normalization with residual addition
- `FastLayerNorm`: Fused standard layer normalization with residual addition
- Platform-specific implementations (CUDA, ROCm, IPEX)

### 4. Tensor Parallelism Layers

All linear layers use TP-aware wrappers from [server/text_generation_server/layers/]():

- `TensorParallelColumnLinear`: Column-wise sharding
- `TensorParallelRowLinear`: Row-wise sharding  
- `TensorParallelMultiAdapterLinear`: Column with LoRA adapter support
- `TensorParallelAdapterRowLinear`: Row with LoRA adapter support

### 5. Attention Backend Dispatch

Attention computation dispatches to platform-specific implementations:

```python
# Prefill path
attn_output = attention(
    query=query, key=key, value=value,
    seqlen=seqlen, block_tables=block_tables,
    softmax_scale=self.softmax_scale, ...
)

# Decode path  
attn_output = paged_attention(
    query, kv_cache, kv_head_mapping, softmax_scale,
    block_tables, seqlen, max_s, ...
)
```

These functions dispatch to CUDA Flash Attention, ROCm attention, or IPEX attention based on the detected system.

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:206-268](), [server/text_generation_server/layers/]()

---

This page documents the token generation logic in Text Generation Inference (TGI), covering how tokens are selected during the text generation process. This logic is responsible for transforming raw model outputs (logits) into selected tokens, applying various probability transformations, implementing sampling strategies, and determining when to stop generation.

For information about model loading and initialization, see [Model Loading and Initialization](#3.1). For details on specific model implementations, see [Causal Language Models](#3.2).

## Token Generation Overview

The token generation logic in TGI consists of several key components working together to control how tokens are selected:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Token Generation Pipeline"
        ModelOutput["Model Output Logits"] --> LogitsProcessors["Logits Processors"]
        LogitsProcessors --> LogitsWarpers["Logits Warpers"]
        LogitsWarpers --> TokenSelection["Token Selection Strategy"]
        TokenSelection --> StopCheck["Stopping Criteria Check"]
        StopCheck -->|"Continue"| NextToken["Add Token to Generation"]
        NextToken --> ModelInput["New Model Input"]
        ModelInput --> ModelOutput
        StopCheck -->|"Stop"| EndGeneration["End Generation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Logits Processors"
        LP1["WatermarkLogitsProcessor"]
        LP2["RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor"]
        LP3["FrequencyPenaltyLogitsProcessor"]
        LP4["GrammarLogitProcessor"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Logits Warpers"
        LW1["TemperatureLogitsWarper"]
        LW2["TopKLogitsWarper"]
        LW3["TopPLogitsWarper"]
        LW4["TypicalLogitsWarper"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Selection Strategies"
        SS1["Greedy (argmax)"]
        SS2["Sampling (Gumbel-Max)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stopping Criteria"
        SC1["Max New Tokens"]
        SC2["EOS Token Detection"]
        SC3["Stop Sequence Match"]
    end
    
    LogitsProcessors --- LP1
    LogitsProcessors --- LP2
    LogitsProcessors --- LP3
    LogitsProcessors --- LP4
    
    LogitsWarpers --- LW1
    LogitsWarpers --- LW2
    LogitsWarpers --- LW3
    LogitsWarpers --- LW4
    
    TokenSelection --- SS1
    TokenSelection --- SS2
    
    StopCheck --- SC1
    StopCheck --- SC2
    StopCheck --- SC3
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:24-128](), [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:131-206]()

## NextTokenChooser

The `NextTokenChooser` class is the central component responsible for selecting the next token based on model outputs and generation parameters.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "NextTokenChooser" {
        +watermark_processor
        +repetition_processor
        +frequency_processor
        +grammar_processor
        +static_warper
        +choice: Sampling|Greedy
        +__call__(input_ids, scores)
        +advance_grammar(next_id)
        +from_pb(pb, device, tokenizer)
    }
    
    class "Sampling" {
        +generator: torch.Generator
        +seed: int
        +__call__(logits)
    }
    
    class "Greedy" {
        +__call__(logits)
    }
    
    "NextTokenChooser" --> "Sampling": uses when do_sample=True
    "NextTokenChooser" --> "Greedy": uses when do_sample=False
```

### Initialization and Configuration

The `NextTokenChooser` is initialized with parameters that control token generation:

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    watermark: bool = False,
    temperature: float = 1.0,
    repetition_penalty: float = 1.0,
    frequency_penalty: float = 0.0,
    top_k: Optional[int] = None,
    top_p: Optional[float] = None,
    typical_p: Optional[float] = None,
    do_sample: bool = False,
    seed: int = 0,
    device: str = "cpu",
    tokenizer: Optional[PreTrainedTokenizerBase] = None,
    grammar: str = "",
    grammar_type: GrammarType = GrammarType.GRAMMAR_TYPE_NONE,
    fsm_grammar_state: int = 0,
):
```

The initializer creates various processors and warpers based on the provided parameters:

1. `watermark_processor`: Adds a watermark to generated text (optional)
2. `repetition_processor`: Penalizes repetition of tokens
3. `frequency_processor`: Penalizes frequently occurring tokens
4. `grammar_processor`: Ensures generated tokens follow grammar constraints
5. `static_warper`: Combines temperature, top_k, top_p, and typical_p warping
6. `choice`: Strategy for token selection (greedy or sampling)

### Token Selection Process

When called, the `NextTokenChooser` applies the configured processors and warpers to the logits before selecting the next token:

```python
def __call__(self, input_ids, scores):
    if self.watermark_processor is not None:
        scores = self.watermark_processor(input_ids, scores)
    if self.repetition_processor is not None:
        scores = self.repetition_processor(input_ids, scores)
    if self.frequency_processor is not None:
        scores = self.frequency_processor(input_ids, scores)
    if self.grammar_processor is not None:
        scores = self.grammar_processor(scores, self.fsm_grammar_state)

    if self.static_warper is None:
        next_logprob = torch.log_softmax(scores, -1)
    else:
        scores, next_logprob = self.static_warper(scores)

    next_id = self.choice(scores[-1]).view(1, 1)

    return next_id, next_logprob
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:24-105]()

## Sampling Strategies

TGI implements two main token selection strategies:

### Greedy Selection

The `Greedy` class implements deterministic token selection by taking the highest probability token (argmax):

```python
class Greedy:
    def __call__(self, logits):
        return logits.argmax(dim=-1)
```

### Sampling Selection

The `Sampling` class implements stochastic token selection based on token probabilities:

```python
class Sampling:
    def __init__(self, seed: int, device: str = "cpu"):
        self.generator = torch.Generator(device)
        self.generator.manual_seed(seed)
        self.seed = seed

    def __call__(self, logits):
        probs = torch.nn.functional.softmax(logits, -1)
        # Avoid GPU<->CPU sync done by torch multinomial
        q = torch.empty_like(probs).exponential_(1, generator=self.generator)
        return probs.div_(q).argmax()
```

This implements the Gumbel-max trick, which is equivalent to sampling from the distribution but avoids the GPU<->CPU synchronization overhead of torch.multinomial.

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:506-522]()

## Stopping Criteria

The `StoppingCriteria` class determines when token generation should stop based on several conditions:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Token["New Token Generated"] --> MaxTokens["Check if max_new_tokens reached"]
    MaxTokens -->|"Yes"| StopLength["Stop: Length Limit"]
    MaxTokens -->|"No"| EOSCheck["Check if token is EOS"]
    EOSCheck -->|"Yes"| StopEOS["Stop: EOS Token"]
    EOSCheck -->|"No"| StopSeqCheck["Check stop sequences"]
    StopSeqCheck -->|"Match found"| StopSeq["Stop: Stop Sequence"]
    StopSeqCheck -->|"No match"| Continue["Continue Generation"]
```

### StoppingCriteria Implementation

The `StoppingCriteria` class checks three main conditions:

1. **Maximum new tokens**: Stops generation after generating a specified number of tokens
2. **EOS token**: Stops when an end-of-sequence token is generated
3. **Stop sequences**: Stops when specific text sequences appear in the output

```python
def __call__(self, last_token: int, last_output: str) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[str]]:
    self.current_tokens += 1
    if self.current_tokens >= self.max_new_tokens:
        return True, FinishReason.FINISH_REASON_LENGTH

    if not self.ignore_eos_token and last_token in self.eos_token_ids:
        return True, FinishReason.FINISH_REASON_EOS_TOKEN

    if self.stop_sequence_criterias:
        self.current_output += last_output
        # There is no need to keep an output that is too long
        if len(self.current_output) > 300:
            # Slice to -200 to avoid doing it all the time
            self.current_output = self.current_output[-200:]
        for stop_sequence_criteria in self.stop_sequence_criterias:
            if stop_sequence_criteria(self.current_output):
                return True, FinishReason.FINISH_REASON_STOP_SEQUENCE

    return False, None
```

### Stop Sequence Detection

The `StopSequenceCriteria` class detects specific stop sequences using regular expressions:

```python
class StopSequenceCriteria:
    def __init__(self, stop_sequence: str):
        stop_sequence = re.escape(stop_sequence)
        self.regex = re.compile(f"{stop_sequence}$")

    def __call__(self, output: str) -> bool:
        if self.regex.findall(output):
            return True
        return False
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:131-206](), [server/tests/utils/test_tokens.py:10-46]()

## Heterogeneous Generation

For batch processing with different parameters per sequence, TGI provides `HeterogeneousNextTokenChooser`:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class "HeterogeneousNextTokenChooser" {
        +watermark_processor
        +repetition_processor
        +frequency_processor
        +grammar_processor
        +warpers
        +choice
        +__call__(input_ids, scores, speculate, speculated_ids, speculative_scores)
        +advance_grammar(next_ids)
        +advance_grammar_single(grammar_state_index, next_id)
        +filter(indices)
    }
    
    class "HeterogeneousSampling" {
        +seeds
        +greedy_indices
        +sampling_mapping
        +__call__(logits)
        +filter(indices)
    }
    
    "HeterogeneousNextTokenChooser" --> "HeterogeneousSampling": uses when any do_sample=True
    "HeterogeneousNextTokenChooser" --> "Greedy": uses when all do_sample=False
```

This class processes a batch of sequences with different generation parameters:

1. Creates per-sequence processors and warpers
2. Maintains independent grammar states for each sequence
3. Supports both sampling and greedy strategies within the same batch
4. Handles speculative decoding for improved performance

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:233-473](), [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:525-564]()

## Speculative Decoding

TGI implements speculative decoding to improve generation speed:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Input["Input Context + First Token"] --> FindMatch["Find Token in Context"]
    FindMatch --> PredictNext["Predict Next Tokens from Context"]
    PredictNext --> Verify["Verify Predictions with Model"]
    Verify --> Accept["Accept Correct Predictions"]
    Accept --> Continue["Continue Generation"]
```

The `create_n_gram_speculation` function tries to predict future tokens based on patterns in the input context:

```python
def create_n_gram_speculation(
    input_ids: torch.Tensor,
    next_ids: torch.Tensor,
    accepted_ids: torch.Tensor,
    speculate: int,
    verbose: bool,
):
    # Very trivial approach, find first match in the string.
    B = accepted_ids.shape[0]
    device = input_ids.device
    seeds = next_ids[accepted_ids.cumsum(dim=-1) - 1]
    indices = (input_ids == seeds.unsqueeze(-1)).max(dim=1).indices + 1
    all_indices = indices.unsqueeze(-1).expand(B, speculate) + torch.arange(
        speculate, device=device
    )
    all_indices = torch.clamp(all_indices, max=input_ids.shape[1] - 1)

    speculative_ids = input_ids.gather(dim=-1, index=all_indices)
    return speculative_ids
```

This approach:
1. Finds where the newly generated token appears in the input context
2. Uses tokens that follow it in the context as speculative predictions
3. Improves throughput when predictions are correct

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:209-230](), [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:326-412]()

## Grammar-Constrained Generation

TGI supports grammar-constrained generation through the `GrammarLogitProcessor`:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Grammar["Grammar Definition"] --> FSM["Finite State Machine"]
    ModelLogits["Model Output Logits"] --> Filtering["Grammar-Based Filtering"]
    FSM --> Filtering
    Filtering --> ValidTokens["Valid Next Tokens"]
    ValidTokens --> Selection["Token Selection"]
    Selection --> NextToken["Next Token"]
    NextToken --> UpdateState["Update Grammar State"]
    UpdateState --> FSM
```

After each token is generated, the grammar state is updated:

```python
def advance_grammar(self, next_id: int):
    if self.grammar_processor is not None:
        self.fsm_grammar_state = self.grammar_processor.advance(
            next_id, self.fsm_grammar_state
        )
    return self
```

For batch processing, the heterogeneous version handles multiple grammar states:

```python
def advance_grammar(self, next_ids: List[int]):
    if self.grammar_processor is not None:
        other_new_states = self.grammar_processor.advance_batch(
            next_ids, self.fsm_grammar_states
        )
        self.fsm_grammar_states = other_new_states
    return self
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:100-105](), [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:415-432]()

## Top-N Tokens Output

For applications that need access to the top token candidates (not just the selected token), TGI provides the `batch_top_tokens` function:

```python
def batch_top_tokens(
    top_n_tokens: List[int],
    top_n_tokens_tensor: torch.Tensor,
    logprobs: torch.Tensor,
    accepted_ids: torch.Tensor,
) -> Tuple[List[List[List[int]]], List[List[List[float]]]]:
    """Find the top n most likely tokens for a batch of generations.

    When multiple tokens have equal probabilities and they don't all fit, the
    remaining tokens are also returned.
    """
```

This function:
1. Determines the top N tokens by probability for each sequence
2. Handles ties by including all tokens with the same probability
3. Returns both token IDs and their log probabilities
4. Supports speculative decoding by accounting for accepted IDs

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:567-645](), [server/tests/utils/test_tokens.py:49-88]()

## Integration with TGI Architecture

The token generation logic is a core component of the TGI architecture, positioned between the model implementation and the response handling:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Router
    participant BatchProcessor
    participant ModelServer
    participant NextTokenChooser
    participant StoppingCriteria
    
    Client->>Router: Generate Request
    Router->>BatchProcessor: Process Request
    BatchProcessor->>ModelServer: Forward (Input Tokens)
    ModelServer->>BatchProcessor: Logits
    
    loop Until Stopping Criteria Met
        BatchProcessor->>NextTokenChooser: Select Next Token
        NextTokenChooser->>BatchProcessor: Next Token
        BatchProcessor->>StoppingCriteria: Check Stopping Conditions
        
        alt Continue Generation
            BatchProcessor->>ModelServer: Forward (Next Token)
            ModelServer->>BatchProcessor: Logits
            BatchProcessor->>Client: Stream Token
        else Stop Generation
            BatchProcessor->>Client: Complete Response
        end
    end
```

This integration enables TGI to efficiently generate tokens while applying sophisticated control mechanisms to influence the quality and characteristics of the generated text.

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/tokens.py:1-646]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document provides an overview of the advanced optimization and feature systems available in Text Generation Inference (TGI). These features enable production-grade performance, memory efficiency, and controlled generation for large language models. The content covers:

- **Quantization techniques** for memory reduction (detailed in [4.1](#4.1))
- **Attention mechanism optimizations** for computational efficiency (detailed in [4.2](#4.2))
- **Structured generation systems** for constrained output (detailed in [4.3](#4.3))
- **Additional performance optimizations** including speculative decoding and CUDA graphs

For model implementation details, see [Model Implementation](#3). For deployment configuration, see [Configuration and CLI](#6.2).

---

## Quantization Overview

TGI supports multiple quantization schemes that reduce model memory footprint while maintaining inference quality. Quantization methods fall into two categories:

### Pre-Quantized vs On-The-Fly Quantization

| Method | Type | Precision | Calibration Required | Performance Impact |
|--------|------|-----------|---------------------|-------------------|
| **GPTQ** | Pre-quantized | 4-bit | Yes (dataset) | Low latency |
| **AWQ** | Pre-quantized | 4-bit | Yes (activation-aware) | Low latency |
| **Marlin** | Pre-quantized | 4-bit | Yes | Lowest latency (optimized kernels) |
| **EXL2** | Pre-quantized | Variable (2-8 bit) | Yes | Medium latency |
| **bitsandbytes** | On-the-fly | 8-bit / 4-bit (NF4/FP4) | No | Higher latency |
| **EETQ** | On-the-fly | 8-bit | No | Medium latency |
| **FP8** | On-the-fly | 8-bit (E4M3/E5M2) | No | Low latency (H100+) |

### Quantization Configuration Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    CLI["text-generation-launcher CLI<br/>(launcher/src/main.rs:580-643)"]
    QuantEnum["Quantization Enum<br/>(launcher/src/main.rs:405-447)"]
    EnvVar["Environment Variable<br/>--quantize flag"]
    
    Server["Python Model Server<br/>(text_generation_server)"]
    ModelInit["Model Initialization<br/>(models/__init__.py)"]
    
    PreQuant["Pre-Quantized Weights<br/>(GPTQ/AWQ/Marlin/EXL2)"]
    OnFlyQuant["On-The-Fly Quantization<br/>(bitsandbytes/EETQ/FP8)"]
    
    LoadWeights["Load Safetensors<br/>from HF Hub or Local"]
    QuantizeLayer["Quantize Layers<br/>During Model Load"]
    
    CLI --> EnvVar
    EnvVar --> QuantEnum
    QuantEnum --> Server
    
    Server --> ModelInit
    ModelInit --> PreQuant
    ModelInit --> OnFlyQuant
    
    PreQuant --> LoadWeights
    OnFlyQuant --> QuantizeLayer
    
    LoadWeights --> InferenceReady["Inference Ready"]
    QuantizeLayer --> InferenceReady
```

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:405-487](), [README.md:48-54](), [docs/source/conceptual/quantization.md:1-73]()

### Quantization Enum Definition

The launcher defines supported quantization methods in the `Quantization` enum:

```
launcher/src/main.rs:405-447
```

Key quantization options:
- **AWQ**: 4-bit quantization with best latency for compatible models
- **GPTQ**: 4-bit quantization with broad model support, uses exllama or triton kernels
- **Marlin**: Optimized 4-bit format for GPTQ/AWQ with fastest kernels
- **bitsandbytes-nf4/fp4**: On-the-fly 4-bit quantization, no pre-processing needed
- **EETQ**: On-the-fly 8-bit quantization, drop-in replacement for bitsandbytes
- **FP8**: Native 8-bit float format for H100+ GPUs (E4M3/E5M2)

### Usage Examples

Pre-quantized model deployment:
```bash
# GPTQ quantized model
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 1g -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5 \
    --model-id TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-GPTQ --quantize gptq

# AWQ quantized model  
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 1g -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5 \
    --model-id TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-AWQ --quantize awq
```

On-the-fly quantization:
```bash
# 4-bit NF4 quantization
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 1g -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5 \
    --model-id meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf --quantize bitsandbytes-nf4

# FP8 quantization (H100+)
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 1g -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5 \
    --model-id meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf --quantize fp8
```

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:619-620](), [docs/source/conceptual/quantization.md:14-36](), [docs/source/quicktour.md:98-99]()

## Attention Mechanism Optimizations

TGI implements multiple attention optimization strategies that significantly reduce memory usage and computational cost during inference. See [Attention Mechanisms](#4.2) for detailed implementation.

### Attention Backend Selection

```mermaid
graph TB
    LauncherConfig["Launcher Configuration<br/>(launcher/src/main.rs:131-200)"]
    
    ComputeCap["GPU Compute Capability<br/>get_cuda_capability()"]
    ModelConfig["Model Config<br/>head_dim, model_type"]
    LoRAFlag["LoRA Adapters Flag"]
    VisionFlag["Vision Model Flag"]
    
    AttentionEnv["ATTENTION Environment Variable<br/>(flashinfer/paged/flashdecoding)"]
    PrefixCacheEnv["PREFIX_CACHING Environment Variable"]
    
    FlashInfer["FlashInfer Attention<br/>(Default for head_dim 64/128/256)"]
    PagedAttn["Paged Attention<br/>(Fallback for unsupported configs)"]
    FlashDecoding["Flash Decoding<br/>(SM 8.0+, large batches)"]
    
    PrefixCache["Prefix Caching Enabled<br/>(RadixAllocator)"]
    NoPrefixCache["Prefix Caching Disabled"]
    
    LauncherConfig --> ComputeCap
    LauncherConfig --> ModelConfig
    LauncherConfig --> LoRAFlag
    LauncherConfig --> VisionFlag
    
    ComputeCap --> AttentionEnv
    ModelConfig --> AttentionEnv
    AttentionEnv --> FlashInfer
    AttentionEnv --> PagedAttn
    AttentionEnv --> FlashDecoding
    
    ModelConfig --> PrefixCacheEnv
    LoRAFlag --> PrefixCacheEnv
    VisionFlag --> PrefixCacheEnv
    
    PrefixCacheEnv --> PrefixCache
    PrefixCacheEnv --> NoPrefixCache
```

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:131-200]()

### Attention Methods Comparison

| Method | Memory Pattern | Use Case | KV Cache | Prefix Reuse |
|--------|----------------|----------|----------|--------------|
| **Flash Attention v1/v2** | Memory-efficient block-wise | Default for modern GPUs | In SRAM/registers | No |
| **Paged Attention** | Block-based virtual memory | Long contexts, dynamic batching | Paged blocks | Yes (with RadixAllocator) |
| **Flash Decoding** | Optimized for decode phase | Large batch decoding | In SRAM/registers | No |
| **FlashInfer** | Combined prefill/decode | Default (SM 8.0+) | Optimized layout | Yes |

### Attention Backend Logic

The launcher automatically selects the appropriate attention backend based on model configuration:

```
launcher/src/main.rs:131-200 - resolve_attention()
```

Key decision factors:
1. **Head dimension**: FlashInfer requires head_dim of 64, 128, or 256
2. **Model type**: Some models (falcon, deepseek_v2) force paged attention
3. **Compute capability**: SM 8.0+ enables flash decoding fallback
4. **Vision models**: Disable prefix caching for VLM architectures
5. **Encoder-decoder**: Disable prefix caching for seq2seq models

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:131-200](), [README.md:47]()

---

## Structured Generation and Grammar Constraints

TGI provides grammar-constrained generation to ensure outputs conform to specific formats. This enables reliable tool calling, JSON output, and pattern-matched text generation. See [Chat Templates and Structured Generation](#4.3) for details.

### Grammar Types and Validation Pipeline

```mermaid
graph TB
    ClientRequest["Client Request<br/>GenerateRequest"]
    GrammarParam["parameters.grammar field<br/>(router/src/lib.rs:425-428)"]
    
    GrammarType["GrammarType Enum<br/>(router/src/lib.rs:238-258)"]
    
    JSONType["Json(serde_json::Value)<br/>JSON Schema object"]
    RegexType["Regex(String)<br/>Regular expression pattern"]
    JSONSchemaType["JsonSchema(JsonSchemaConfig)<br/>Named schema with metadata"]
    
    ValidationLayer["Validation Layer<br/>(router/src/validation.rs:347-392)"]
    
    DisableCheck["Check disable_grammar_support<br/>(validation.rs:100)"]
    JSONValidation["JSON Schema Validation<br/>jsonschema crate"]
    RegexValidation["Regex Compilation<br/>regex crate"]
    OutlinesCore["outlines_core::json_schema_to_regex<br/>(validation.rs:10)"]
    
    ServerGrammar["Server Grammar String<br/>Passed to Python server"]
    FSMCompiler["FSM Compiler<br/>(Python: outlines integration)"]
    ConstrainedSampling["Constrained Token Sampling<br/>During generation"]
    
    ClientRequest --> GrammarParam
    GrammarParam --> GrammarType
    
    GrammarType --> JSONType
    GrammarType --> RegexType
    GrammarType --> JSONSchemaType
    
    JSONType --> ValidationLayer
    RegexType --> ValidationLayer
    JSONSchemaType --> ValidationLayer
    
    ValidationLayer --> DisableCheck
    DisableCheck -->|Enabled| JSONValidation
    DisableCheck -->|Enabled| RegexValidation
    
    JSONValidation --> OutlinesCore
    RegexValidation --> ServerGrammar
    OutlinesCore --> ServerGrammar
    
    ServerGrammar --> FSMCompiler
    FSMCompiler --> ConstrainedSampling
```

**Sources:** [router/src/lib.rs:238-258](), [router/src/validation.rs:347-392]()

### Grammar Type Definitions

TGI defines three grammar types in the router:

```
router/src/lib.rs:238-258 - GrammarType enum
```

Grammar types:
- **Json**: Direct JSON Schema value for simple object constraints
- **Regex**: Regular expression pattern for text matching
- **JsonSchema**: Named JSON Schema with optional strict mode flag

### Grammar Validation Implementation

Validation occurs in the router before requests are sent to the model server:

```
router/src/validation.rs:347-392 - Grammar validation logic
```

Validation steps:
1. Check if grammar support is disabled (`disable_grammar_support` flag)
2. For JSON grammars:
   - Validate JSON schema structure using `jsonschema` crate
   - Convert schema to regex using `outlines_core::json_schema_to_regex`
3. For Regex grammars:
   - Validate regex pattern compilation
   - Pass directly to server
4. Return validated grammar string to be compiled into FSM by Python server

**Sources:** [router/src/validation.rs:347-392](), [router/Cargo.toml:26]()

### Usage Example: JSON Schema Constraint

```bash
curl localhost:8080/generate \
    -X POST \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{
      "inputs": "Generate a person record:",
      "parameters": {
        "max_new_tokens": 100,
        "grammar": {
          "type": "json_schema",
          "value": {
            "name": "Person",
            "schema": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "name": {"type": "string"},
                "age": {"type": "integer"},
                "email": {"type": "string", "format": "email"}
              },
              "required": ["name", "age"]
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }'
```

**Sources:** [router/src/lib.rs:252-257](), [README.md:61]()

## Additional Performance Optimizations

### Speculative Decoding

Speculative decoding uses a smaller "draft" model to predict multiple tokens ahead, which are then verified by the main model in parallel. This can provide ~2x latency improvement for compatible models.

Configuration:
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-hf --speculate 2
```

The `--speculate N` flag sets the number of tokens to speculate. For Medusa models, speculation heads are automatically detected from the model configuration.

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:622-627](), [README.md:60]()

### CUDA Graphs

CUDA graphs reduce kernel launch overhead by capturing and replaying sequences of GPU operations. This is particularly effective for decode operations with fixed batch sizes.

Configuration in launcher:
```
launcher/src/main.rs:766 - cuda_graphs parameter
```

Default batch sizes for CUDA graphs: `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`

Disable CUDA graphs:
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1 --cuda-graphs 0
```

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:762-766]()

### Prefix Caching with RadixAllocator

Prefix caching stores and reuses KV cache values for common prompt prefixes, reducing redundant computation. The `RadixAllocator` implements a radix trie with LRU eviction to manage cached prefixes efficiently.

Prefix caching is automatically enabled based on model compatibility:
- **Enabled by default** for standard causal LMs with supported head dimensions
- **Disabled automatically** for vision-language models, encoder-decoder models, and LoRA adapters
- **Disabled automatically** when using paged attention backend

Environment variable override:
```bash
PREFIX_CACHING=1  # Force enable
PREFIX_CACHING=0  # Force disable
```

The launcher's `resolve_attention()` function determines prefix caching availability:

```
launcher/src/main.rs:133-198
```

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:133-198](), [README.md:47]()

### KV Cache Dtype Quantization

TGI supports quantizing the key-value cache to FP8 format, reducing memory usage during inference with minimal quality impact on H100+ GPUs.

```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3fn
```

Supported KV cache dtypes:
```
launcher/src/main.rs:511-530 - KVCacheDtype enum
```

Options:
- `fp8_e4m3fn`: FP8 with 4-bit mantissa (higher precision)
- `fp8_e5m2`: FP8 with 2-bit mantissa (wider range)

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:511-530](), [launcher/src/main.rs:636-637]()

### Continuous Batching

Continuous batching dynamically adds and removes requests from active batches without waiting for full batch completion. This maximizes GPU utilization and reduces latency for concurrent requests.

Key parameters controlling batching behavior:

| Parameter | Default | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `max_concurrent_requests` | 128 | Maximum number of concurrent requests |
| `max_batch_total_tokens` | Auto-inferred | Total token budget across batch |
| `max_batch_prefill_tokens` | `max_input_tokens + 50` | Prefill operation token limit |
| `waiting_served_ratio` | 0.3 | Ratio for pausing running queries to include waiting ones |
| `max_waiting_tokens` | 20 | Tokens to decode before considering new prefill |

Configuration:
```
launcher/src/main.rs:645-755
```

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:645-755](), [README.md:45]()

---

## Feature Configuration Summary

### Launcher CLI Parameters

The following table summarizes key advanced feature flags available through `text-generation-launcher`:

| Flag | Type | Purpose | Default |
|------|------|---------|---------|
| `--quantize` | Enum | Quantization method | None |
| `--speculate` | usize | Speculation token count | None |
| `--kv-cache-dtype` | Enum | KV cache quantization | Model dtype |
| `--cuda-graphs` | Vec<usize> | CUDA graph batch sizes | `[1,2,4,8,16,32]` |
| `--max-batch-total-tokens` | u32 | Batch token budget | Auto-inferred |
| `--max-concurrent-requests` | usize | Request concurrency limit | 128 |
| `--disable-custom-kernels` | bool | Disable optimized kernels | false |

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Values | Purpose |
|----------|--------|---------|
| `ATTENTION` | `flashinfer`, `paged`, `flashdecoding` | Override attention backend |
| `PREFIX_CACHING` | `0`, `1`, `true`, `false` | Control prefix caching |
| `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED` | `0`, `1` | Enable TunableOp (ROCm) |
| `ROCM_USE_FLASH_ATTN_V2_TRITON` | `0`, `1` | Use Triton FA (ROCm) |
| `ROCM_USE_CUSTOM_PAGED_ATTN` | `0`, `1` | Use custom paged attn (ROCm) |

**Sources:** [launcher/src/main.rs:580-850](), [docs/source/installation_amd.md:20-39]()

This page provides a comprehensive guide to quantization in Text Generation Inference (TGI). Quantization reduces model memory usage and increases inference speed by representing weights with lower precision, enabling efficient deployment of large language models.

TGI supports multiple quantization methods, each with different trade-offs between model quality, memory usage, and inference speed:

- **Pre-quantized formats**: GPTQ, AWQ, Marlin, EXL2 (requires quantized weights)
- **On-the-fly quantization**: bitsandbytes, EETQ, FP8 (quantizes at load time)

## Quantization Methods Overview

The following table summarizes the quantization methods supported in TGI:

| Method | Precision | Type | Hardware | Memory Savings | Speed | Quality |
|--------|-----------|------|----------|----------------|-------|---------|
| **bitsandbytes** | 4-bit, 8-bit | On-the-fly | CUDA | High | Moderate | Good |
| **GPTQ** | 4-bit, 8-bit | Pre-quantized | CUDA, ROCm | High | Fast | Good |
| **AWQ** | 4-bit | Pre-quantized | CUDA | High | Fast | Better |
| **Marlin** | 4-bit, 8-bit | Pre-quantized | CUDA (≥8.0) | High | Very Fast | Good |
| **EXL2** | Variable | Pre-quantized | CUDA | Configurable | Fast | Configurable |
| **EETQ** | 8-bit | On-the-fly | CUDA | Moderate | Fast | High |
| **FP8** | 8-bit | On-the-fly | CUDA (≥9.0), ROCm | Moderate | Very Fast | High |

Sources: [README.md:48-54](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:18-28](), [docs/source/conceptual/quantization.md:1-73]()

### Diagram: Quantization Architecture in TGI

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Model Loading"
        ModelID["Model ID"]
        Launcher["text-generation-launcher"]
        CLI["--quantize flag"]
    end

        DefaultLoader["DefaultWeightsLoader"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Weight Types"
        GPTQWeight["GPTQWeight"]
        MarlinWeight["GPTQMarlinWeight"]
        BNBWeight["Weight with BNB"]
        UnquantWeight["UnquantizedWeight"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Linear Layers"
        QuantLinear["QuantLinear"]
        ExllamaLinear["ExllamaQuantLinear"]
        AWQLinear["WQLinear"]
        MarlinLinear["GPTQMarlinLinear"]
        BNBLinear["Linear4bit/Linear8bit"]
        FastLinear["FastLinear"]
    end
    
    ModelID --> Launcher
    Launcher --> CLI
    CLI --> GetLoader
    ConfigFiles --> ConfigCheck
    ConfigCheck --> GetLoader
    
    GetLoader -->|"gptq/awq"| GPTQLoader
    GetLoader -->|"marlin"| MarlinLoader
    GetLoader -->|"bitsandbytes"| BNBLoader
    GetLoader -->|"eetq"| EETQLoader
```
