```mermaid
    GetLoader -->|"exl2"| EXL2Loader
    GetLoader -->|"none"| DefaultLoader
    
    GPTQLoader --> GPTQWeight
    MarlinLoader --> MarlinWeight
    BNBLoader --> BNBWeight
    DefaultLoader --> UnquantWeight
    
    GPTQWeight -->|"use_exllama"| ExllamaLinear
    GPTQWeight -->|"use_awq_kernel"| AWQLinear
    GPTQWeight -->|"default"| QuantLinear
    MarlinWeight --> MarlinLinear
    BNBWeight --> BNBLinear
    UnquantWeight --> FastLinear
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/quantization.py:124-171](), [server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py:13-443](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:18-28]()

## On-The-Fly Quantization

On-the-fly quantization methods convert full-precision weights to quantized representations at model load time. These methods don't require pre-quantized model files and work with standard model checkpoints.

### bitsandbytes

The `bitsandbytes` library provides 4-bit and 8-bit quantization with three data types:

- **8-bit quantization** (`--quantize bitsandbytes`): Direct 8-bit quantization
- **4-bit NF4** (`--quantize bitsandbytes-nf4`): 4-bit NormalFloat format, optimized for normally distributed weights
- **4-bit FP4** (`--quantize bitsandbytes-fp4`): 4-bit floating point format

**Usage:**
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 --quantize bitsandbytes-nf4
```

**Characteristics:**
- No calibration dataset needed
- Automatic quantization on load
- Slower inference compared to GPTQ/AWQ
- Good memory savings (4-bit ~4x, 8-bit ~2x)
- Works only on CUDA

Sources: [README.md:316-323](), [docs/source/conceptual/quantization.md:14-36](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:19-21]()

### EETQ

EETQ (Efficient Efficient Transformer Quantization) provides fast 8-bit weight-only quantization:

**Usage:**
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 --quantize eetq
```

**Characteristics:**
- 8-bit integer quantization
- Faster than bitsandbytes
- Good balance between quality and speed
- Minimal quality degradation
- CUDA only

Sources: [README.md:51](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:25]()

### FP8

FP8 (8-bit floating point) quantization uses hardware-native FP8 formats on modern GPUs:

**Usage:**
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 --quantize fp8
```

**Characteristics:**
- Uses hardware FP8 (E4M3 or E5M2 formats)
- Very fast on supported hardware
- Minimal accuracy loss
- Requires CUDA compute ≥9.0 or ROCm
- Can also quantize KV cache with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2`

The FP8 quantization is handled by `HybridFP8UnquantLoader`, which can optionally convert weights to FP8 format during loading.

Sources: [README.md:54](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:27-28, 36-38](), [server/text_generation_server/layers/fp8.py:1-100]()

## Pre-Quantized Models

Pre-quantized models store weights in compressed formats, requiring quantization to be performed offline before deployment. TGI can load these models directly without additional processing.

### GPTQ

GPTQ (Generalized Post-Training Quantization) optimizes quantization by minimizing layer-wise reconstruction error:

$$({\hat{W}_{l}}^{*} = argmin_{\hat{W_{l}}} ||W_{l}X-\hat{W}_{l}X||^{2}_{2})$$

**Usage:**
```bash
# Run pre-quantized GPTQ model
text-generation-launcher --model-id TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-GPTQ --quantize gptq

# Or quantize a model
text-generation-server quantize mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 /data/mistral-gptq
```

**Characteristics:**
- Typically 4-bit quantization (3-8 bits supported)
- Requires calibration dataset for quantization
- Good quality with significant memory savings
- Fast inference with optimized kernels
- Works on CUDA and ROCm

GPTQ models in TGI use the `GPTQWeightsLoader` class which:
- Detects quantization parameters from config files
- Loads packed quantized weights (`qweight`, `qzeros`, `scales`, `g_idx`)
- Converts between formats (AWQ→GPTQ) when needed
- Selects appropriate inference kernels

Sources: [README.md:316-323](), [docs/source/conceptual/quantization.md:39-73](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:22]()

### AWQ

AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization) preserves important weights based on activation magnitudes:

**Usage:**
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-AWQ --quantize awq
```

**Characteristics:**
- 4-bit quantization
- Better quality than GPTQ for same bit-width
- Requires calibration dataset
- Specialized `WQLinear` kernels on CUDA
- Can be converted to GPTQ format for compatibility

AWQ models can use dedicated AWQ kernels (`use_awq_kernel=True`) or be converted to GPTQ format for broader hardware support.

Sources: [README.md:52](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:23]()

### Marlin

Marlin provides highly optimized kernels for GPTQ and AWQ quantized models:

**Usage:**
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id neuralmagic/Llama-2-7b-pruned50-retrained-marlin --quantize marlin
```

**Characteristics:**
- 4-bit and 8-bit quantization
- Optimized kernel implementation
- Fastest inference among quantization methods
- Requires CUDA compute ≥8.0
- Supports specific group sizes: -1, 32, 64, 128
- Repacks GPTQ weights for optimal memory layout

The `GPTQMarlinWeightsLoader` automatically repacks GPTQ weights using `repack_gptq_for_marlin()` for maximum performance.

Sources: [README.md:53](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:28]()

### EXL2

EXL2 provides variable bit-width quantization for fine-grained control:

**Usage:**
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id turboderp/Llama-2-7B-exl2 --quantize exl2
```

**Characteristics:**
- Variable bit-width (2-8 bits per weight)
- Configurable quality/size trade-off
- Custom quantization required
- CUDA only

Sources: [README.md:54](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:26]()

### compressed-tensors

The `compressed-tensors` format provides a standardized quantization format:

**Usage:**
```bash
text-generation-launcher --model-id neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a8 --quantize compressed-tensors
```

This format is detected automatically and doesn't require explicit `--quantize` flag.

Sources: [server/pyproject.toml:76-77](), [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:24]()

## Weight Loading Architecture

TGI uses a flexible weight loading architecture based on the `WeightsLoader` abstract class and the `Weights` class that manages weight access:

### Diagram: WeightsLoader Class Hierarchy

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class WeightsLoader {
        <<abstract>>
        +get_weights(weights, prefix)*
        +get_weights_col(weights, prefix)
        +get_weights_col_packed(weights, prefix, block_sizes)*
        +get_multi_weights_col(weights, prefixes, dim)*
        +get_weights_row(weights, prefix)*
    }
    
    class DefaultWeightsLoader {
        +weight_class: Type[UnquantizedWeight]
        +get_weights(weights, prefix)
        +get_weights_col_packed(weights, prefix, block_sizes)
        +get_multi_weights_col(weights, prefixes, dim)
        +get_weights_row(weights, prefix)
    }
    
    class GPTQWeightsLoader {
        +bits: int
        +groupsize: int
        +quant_method: str
        +quantize: str
        +get_weights(weights, prefix)
        +get_weights_col_packed(weights, prefix, block_sizes)
        +_get_gptq_params(weights)
    }
    
    class GPTQMarlinWeightsLoader {
        +get_weights_col_packed(weights, prefix, block_sizes)
    }
    
    class HybridFP8UnquantLoader {
        +activation_scale_ub: float
        +to_fp8: bool
        +get_weights(weights, prefix)
        +get_weights_col_packed(weights, prefix, block_sizes)
    }
    
    class Weights {
        +routing: Dict
        +device: device
        +dtype: dtype
        +process_group: ProcessGroup
        +weights_loader: WeightsLoader
        +get_tensor(tensor_name)
        +get_sharded(tensor_name, dim)
        +get_weights(prefix)
        +get_weights_col_packed(prefix, block_sizes)
        +use_loader(weights_loader)
    }
    
    WeightsLoader <|-- DefaultWeightsLoader
    WeightsLoader <|-- GPTQWeightsLoader
    WeightsLoader <|-- GPTQMarlinWeightsLoader
    WeightsLoader <|-- HybridFP8UnquantLoader
    
    Weights --> WeightsLoader
```

The `Weights` class coordinates weight loading:
- Maintains routing information for tensor locations in safetensors files
- Delegates to `WeightsLoader` implementations for quantization-specific logic
- Provides unified interface: `get_weights()`, `get_weights_col_packed()`, etc.
- Supports temporary loader switching via `use_loader()` context manager

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py:13-443]()

### Weight Classes and Linear Layers

Different quantization methods produce different weight types:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class Weight {
        <<abstract>>
        +get_linear(bias)*
    }
    
    class UnquantizedWeight {
        +weight: Tensor
        +get_linear(bias)
    }
    
    class GPTQWeight {
        +qweight: Tensor
        +qzeros: Tensor
        +scales: Tensor
        +g_idx: Tensor
        +bits: int
        +groupsize: int
        +use_awq_kernel: bool
        +use_exllama: bool
        +get_linear(bias)
    }
    
    class GPTQMarlinWeight {
        +get_linear(bias)
    }
    
    Weight <|-- UnquantizedWeight
    Weight <|-- GPTQWeight
    Weight <|-- GPTQMarlinWeight
    
    UnquantizedWeight --> FastLinear : creates
    UnquantizedWeight --> FastLinearROCm : creates on ROCm
    
    GPTQWeight --> QuantLinear : creates (default)
    GPTQWeight --> ExllamaQuantLinear : creates (use_exllama)
    GPTQWeight --> WQLinear : creates (use_awq_kernel)
    
    GPTQMarlinWeight --> GPTQMarlinLinear : creates
```

The `Weight.get_linear()` method creates the appropriate linear layer:
- `FastLinear` / `FastLinearROCm`: Standard unquantized linear layers
- `QuantLinear`: Basic GPTQ kernel (CPU, CUDA, ROCm)
- `ExllamaQuantLinear`: Optimized Exllama kernel for 4-bit GPTQ
- `WQLinear`: Specialized AWQ kernel (CUDA only)
- `GPTQMarlinLinear`: Marlin optimized kernel

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py:76-137](), [server/text_generation_server/layers/linear.py:21-99]()

## Quantization Detection and Configuration

TGI automatically detects quantization from model configuration files:

### Diagram: Configuration Detection Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Model Loading"] --> CheckCLI{"--quantize flag?"}
    CheckCLI -->|"Yes"| UseCLI["Use CLI value"]
    CheckCLI -->|"No"| ConfigCheck["_get_quantizer_config()"]
    
    ConfigCheck --> TryConfig1["Try config.json"]
    TryConfig1 --> HasQuantConfig{"Has quantization_config?"}
    HasQuantConfig -->|"Yes"| ExtractConfig["Extract parameters"]
    HasQuantConfig -->|"No"| TryConfig2["Try quantize_config.json"]
    
    TryConfig2 --> Exists2{"File exists?"}
    Exists2 -->|"Yes"| ExtractConfig
    Exists2 -->|"No"| TryConfig3["Try quant_config.json"]
    
    TryConfig3 --> Exists3{"File exists?"}
    Exists3 -->|"Yes"| ExtractConfig
    Exists3 -->|"No"| NoQuant["No quantization"]
    
    ExtractConfig --> DetectMethod{"Detect method"}
    DetectMethod -->|"quant_method=gptq/awq"| GPTQ["Use GPTQ"]
    DetectMethod -->|"checkpoint_format=marlin"| Marlin["Use Marlin"]
    DetectMethod -->|"Other"| Auto["Auto-detect"]
    
    UseCLI --> GetLoader["get_loader()"]
    GPTQ --> GetLoader
    Marlin --> GetLoader
    Auto --> GetLoader
    NoQuant --> GetLoader
    
    GetLoader --> LoaderInstance["WeightsLoader instance"]
```

Configuration parameters extracted:
- `bits`: Bit width (typically 4 or 8)
- `group_size` / `q_group_size`: Grouping for scales/zeros
- `quant_method`: Quantization method ("gptq", "awq", etc.)
- `sym`: Symmetric quantization flag
- `desc_act`: Activation ordering flag

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/quantization.py:14-171]()

### Kernel Selection

For GPTQ models, TGI selects the optimal kernel based on model parameters and hardware:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    GPTQModel["GPTQ Model"] --> CheckMarlin{"Can use Marlin?"}
    
    CheckMarlin -->|"Yes:<br/>- CUDA compute ≥8.0<br/>- bits in [4,8]<br/>- groupsize in [-1,32,64,128]<br/>- sym=True or AWQ"| UseMarlin["GPTQMarlinWeightsLoader"]
    
    CheckMarlin -->|"No"| CheckBits{"bits == 4?"}
    
    CheckBits -->|"Yes"| CheckDescAct{"desc_act?"}
    CheckDescAct -->|"False"| CheckHW{"Hardware?"}
    CheckHW -->|"CUDA/ROCm<br/>compute ≥8.0"| UseExllama["use_exllama=True"]
    CheckHW -->|"Other"| UseBasic["Basic QuantLinear"]
    CheckDescAct -->|"True"| UseBasic
    
    CheckBits -->|"No"| CheckAWQ{"quant_method=awq?"}
    CheckAWQ -->|"Yes + CUDA"| UseAWQKernel["use_awq_kernel=True"]
    CheckAWQ -->|"No or not CUDA"| UseBasic
    
    UseMarlin --> MarlinLinear["GPTQMarlinLinear"]
    UseExllama --> ExllamaLinear["ExllamaQuantLinear"]
    UseAWQKernel --> AWQLinear["WQLinear"]
    UseBasic --> BasicLinear["QuantLinear"]
```

Special case: AWQ models can be converted to GPTQ format on-the-fly using `fast_awq_to_gptq()` to enable use of GPTQ kernels on platforms where AWQ kernels aren't available.

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/quantization.py:145-162]()

## Usage and Configuration

### Command-Line Interface

Quantization is enabled via the `--quantize` flag in `text-generation-launcher`:

```bash
# On-the-fly quantization
text-generation-launcher --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 --quantize bitsandbytes-nf4
text-generation-launcher --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 --quantize eetq
text-generation-launcher --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 --quantize fp8

# Pre-quantized models
text-generation-launcher --model-id TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-GPTQ --quantize gptq
text-generation-launcher --model-id TheBloke/Llama-2-7B-AWQ --quantize awq
text-generation-launcher --model-id neuralmagic/Llama-2-7b-pruned50-retrained-marlin --quantize marlin
```

The `Quantization` enum in `cli.py` defines available options:
- `bitsandbytes`, `bitsandbytes-nf4`, `bitsandbytes-fp4`
- `gptq`, `awq`, `marlin`
- `eetq`, `exl2`, `fp8`
- `compressed-tensors`

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:18-28, 42-131](), [README.md:314-323]()

### Creating Quantized Models

For methods requiring pre-quantization, use the quantization command:

```bash
# Quantize a model to GPTQ format
text-generation-server quantize \
    mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 \
    /data/mistral-gptq \
    --upload-to-model-id myusername/Mistral-7B-GPTQ

# Parameters
text-generation-server quantize --help
#   --bits: Bit width (default: 4)
#   --groupsize: Group size (default: 128)
#   --percdamp: Damping factor (default: 0.01)
#   --act-order: Activation ordering
```

This creates quantized weights using the specified parameters and optionally uploads them to Hugging Face Hub.

For other quantization methods, use their official tools:
- AWQ: [AutoAWQ](https://github.com/casper-hansen/AutoAWQ)
- Marlin: [AutoGPTQ](https://github.com/AutoGPTQ/AutoGPTQ) with Marlin format
- EXL2: [ExLlamaV2](https://github.com/turboderp/exllamav2)

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:338-373](), [docs/source/conceptual/quantization.md:56-73]()

### KV Cache Quantization

FP8 quantization can also be applied to the KV cache to further reduce memory usage:

```bash
text-generation-launcher \
    --model-id mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 \
    --quantize fp8 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2
```

Available KV cache dtypes:
- `fp8_e4m3fn`: FP8 with 4-bit exponent, 3-bit mantissa
- `fp8_e5m2`: FP8 with 5-bit exponent, 2-bit mantissa

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/cli.py:36-38, 49]()

## Hardware Compatibility

Quantization support varies across hardware platforms:

### Quantization Method Support by Platform

| Method | CUDA | ROCm | Intel XPU/CPU | Comments |
|--------|------|------|---------------|----------|
| **bitsandbytes** | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | CUDA only |
| **GPTQ** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓* | Basic kernel on all, optimized on CUDA/ROCm |
| **AWQ** | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | Dedicated kernels CUDA only |
| **Marlin** | ✓** | ✗ | ✗ | Requires CUDA compute ≥8.0 |
| **EXL2** | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | CUDA only |
| **EETQ** | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | CUDA only |
| **FP8** | ✓*** | ✓ | ✗ | CUDA compute ≥9.0 or ROCm |
| **compressed-tensors** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Platform-agnostic format |

\* Basic GPTQ kernel implementation  
\*\* Requires Ampere or newer (compute capability ≥ 8.0)  
\*\*\* Best on Hopper (compute capability ≥ 9.0)

### Kernel Implementation Selection

The system automatically selects the appropriate kernel implementation:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    System["Detect System"] --> IsCUDA{"SYSTEM?"}
    
    IsCUDA -->|"cuda"| CUDAImpl["CUDA Implementation"]
    IsCUDA -->|"rocm"| ROCmImpl["ROCm Implementation"]
    IsCUDA -->|"ipex"| IPEXImpl["IPEX Implementation"]
    IsCUDA -->|"other"| CPUImpl["CPU Implementation"]
    
    CUDAImpl --> CUDAKernels["Available:<br/>- Exllama<br/>- AWQ<br/>- Marlin<br/>- FP8<br/>- Triton"]
    
    ROCmImpl --> ROCmKernels["Available:<br/>- Exllama (CK)<br/>- FP8<br/>- Triton"]
    
    IPEXImpl --> IPEXKernels["Available:<br/>- Basic QuantLinear<br/>- IPEX optimizations"]
    
    CPUImpl --> CPUKernels["Available:<br/>- Basic QuantLinear"]
```

The `SYSTEM` variable is detected at import time from environment variables and hardware detection in `server/text_generation_server/utils/import_utils.py`.

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/import_utils.py:42-76](), [docs/source/installation_amd.md:42-44]()

### Platform-Specific Notes

**CUDA:**
- Most comprehensive quantization support
- All methods available
- Marlin requires Ampere or newer GPUs (A100, RTX 30/40 series, H100)
- FP8 optimized on Hopper (H100)

**ROCm:**
- GPTQ with Exllama kernels using Composable Kernel (CK) implementation
- FP8 support on MI250/MI300 GPUs
- AWQ kernels not available - AWQ models converted to GPTQ format
- Custom paged attention implementation

**Intel XPU:**
- Basic GPTQ support via IPEX
- No specialized quantization kernels

Sources: [docs/source/installation_nvidia.md:1-19](), [docs/source/installation_amd.md:1-45](), [docs/source/installation_intel.md:1-36]()

## Choosing a Quantization Method

The optimal quantization method depends on your requirements:

### Decision Guide

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start["Select Quantization"] --> HasModel{"Pre-quantized<br/>model available?"}
    
    HasModel -->|"Yes"| WhichFormat{"Format?"}
    WhichFormat -->|"GPTQ"| CheckGPU1{"GPU type?"}
    WhichFormat -->|"AWQ"| CheckGPU2{"GPU type?"}
    WhichFormat -->|"Marlin"| UseMarlin["Use Marlin<br/>--quantize marlin"]
    WhichFormat -->|"EXL2"| UseEXL2["Use EXL2<br/>--quantize exl2"]
    
    CheckGPU1 -->|"CUDA ≥8.0"| TryMarlin{"Can convert<br/>to Marlin?"}
    CheckGPU1 -->|"Other CUDA/ROCm"| UseGPTQ["Use GPTQ<br/>--quantize gptq"]
    
    TryMarlin -->|"Yes:<br/>bits in [4,8]<br/>groupsize ok"| UseMarlin
    TryMarlin -->|"No"| UseGPTQ
    
    CheckGPU2 -->|"CUDA"| UseAWQ["Use AWQ<br/>--quantize awq"]
    CheckGPU2 -->|"ROCm"| ConvertAWQ["Convert to GPTQ<br/>--quantize gptq"]
    
    HasModel -->|"No"| Priority{"Priority?"}
    
    Priority -->|"Speed<br/>(Hopper GPU)"| UseFP8["Use FP8<br/>--quantize fp8"]
    Priority -->|"Memory<br/>(any GPU)"| UseBNB4["Use bitsandbytes<br/>--quantize bitsandbytes-nf4"]
    Priority -->|"Quality<br/>(CUDA)"| UseEETQ["Use EETQ<br/>--quantize eetq"]
    Priority -->|"Custom"| CreateQuant["Create quantized<br/>model offline"]
```

### Recommendations by Use Case

| Use Case | Recommended Method | Rationale |
|----------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Production, modern NVIDIA GPU** | Marlin or FP8 | Highest performance with minimal quality loss |
| **Production, older NVIDIA GPU** | GPTQ with Exllama | Good balance of speed and compatibility |
| **Production, AMD GPU** | GPTQ or FP8 | Best performance on ROCm |
| **Development, quick testing** | bitsandbytes-nf4 | No preprocessing needed, automatic |
| **Maximum memory savings** | 4-bit GPTQ or AWQ | Best compression ratio |
| **Minimal quality loss** | FP8 or EETQ | 8-bit with excellent quality retention |
| **Variable requirements** | EXL2 | Configurable bit-width per layer |

### Quality vs. Performance Trade-offs

Approximate quality retention (higher is better):

```
FP8 (99%) > EETQ (98%) > AWQ-4bit (96%) > GPTQ-4bit (95%) > bitsandbytes-nf4 (94%) > bitsandbytes-fp4 (92%)
```

Approximate inference speed (higher is better):

```
Marlin > FP8 > AWQ > GPTQ-Exllama > EETQ > bitsandbytes
```

Memory savings (4-bit: ~75%, 8-bit: ~50% vs FP16)

Sources: [docs/source/conceptual/quantization.md:1-73](), [README.md:48-54]()

## Performance Considerations

When using GPTQ and AWQ quantization in TGI, consider the following:

1. **Memory vs Accuracy Trade-offs**:
   - 4-bit quantization provides maximum memory savings (~4x vs FP16)
   - 8-bit quantization offers better accuracy but less memory reduction (~2x)

2. **Kernel Selection**:
   - Exllama kernels provide significant speedups for 4-bit GPTQ models
   - AWQ kernels are optimized for AWQ quantization on CUDA
   - Marlin kernels offer the highest performance when supported

3. **Hardware Requirements**:
   - CUDA platforms offer the most optimized experience
   - ROCm supports Exllama but not AWQ kernels
   - Intel/CPU platforms have basic support without specialized kernels

4. **Recommended Configurations**:
   - For modern NVIDIA GPUs: 4-bit quantization with Marlin or Exllama
   - For AMD GPUs: 4-bit GPTQ with Exllama kernels
   - For broader compatibility: 4-bit GPTQ with basic kernels

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/layers/gptq/__init__.py:142-149](), [server/text_generation_server/layers/marlin/gptq.py:295-307]()

## Conclusion

GPTQ and AWQ quantization in TGI provide effective ways to reduce memory usage and increase inference speed for large language models. By supporting multiple optimization kernels and hardware platforms, TGI enables efficient deployment across a variety of environments while maintaining acceptable model quality.

# Optimized Attention Mechanisms

This document explains the various optimized attention mechanisms implemented in the Text Generation Inference (TGI) codebase. It covers Flash Attention, Paged Attention, attention variants (multi-query, grouped-query), and how these are integrated with KV caching and tensor parallelism to enable efficient large language model inference.

For information about model quantization techniques like GPTQ and AWQ, see [GPTQ and AWQ Quantization](#4.1).

## 1. Attention Implementation Overview

TGI implements several optimized attention mechanisms that balance computational efficiency and memory usage during inference. The attention computations are split into two distinct phases:

1. **Prefill phase**: Processing the entire prompt at once, using Flash Attention to efficiently compute attention scores
2. **Decode phase**: Generating one token at a time, using Paged Attention to efficiently access cached key-value pairs

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Attention Implementation"
        direction TB
        Attn["Attention Phase"]
        Attn --> |"Prompt tokens"| Prefill["Prefill (Flash Attention)"]
        Attn --> |"Generation tokens"| Decode["Decode (Paged Attention)"]
        
        Prefill --> |"Compute Q,K,V"| FA["Flash Attention"]
        FA --> |"Initial tokens"| FA_Out["Output hidden states"]
        FA --> |"Store K,V"| KVC["KV Cache"]
        
        Decode --> |"Compute Q only"| PA["Paged Attention"]
        PA --> |"Retrieve cached K,V"| KVC
        PA --> |"Next token"| PA_Out["Output hidden state"]
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:206-267]()

## 2. Key Components of Optimized Attention

### 2.1 Flash Attention

Flash Attention is an algorithm that reduces memory usage and increases computational efficiency by reducing memory I/O operations during attention computation. TGI implements Flash Attention for the prefill phase, enabling efficient processing of long prompts.

Key features:
- Avoids materializing the large attention matrix
- Processes attention computation in blocks to maximize GPU cache usage
- Reduces memory bandwidth requirements

In TGI, Flash Attention is implemented as the `attention` function used during the prefill phase:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Flash Attention"
        direction TB
        Input["Input Tokens"] --> QKV["Query/Key/Value Projection"]
        QKV --> FA["Flash Attention Kernel"]
        FA --> Out["Output Hidden States"]
        FA --> |"Store"| KV["KV Cache"]
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:242-251](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py:296-306]()

### 2.2 Paged Attention

Paged Attention is a memory management technique that addresses the KV cache management challenge. It allows efficient storage and retrieval of key-value pairs for long sequences by organizing the KV cache in fixed-size blocks and using block tables for indirection.

Key features:
- Enables non-contiguous storage of KV cache entries
- Reduces memory fragmentation
- Supports efficient batch processing with varying sequence lengths

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Paged Attention"
        direction TB
        Query["Query Tensor"] --> PA["Paged Attention Kernel"]
        KVCache["KV Cache"] --> |"Block Tables"| PA
        PA --> |"Attention Scores"| Out["Output Hidden States"]
    end
    
    subgraph "KV Cache Structure"
        direction LR
        BT["Block Tables"] --> |"Maps sequence positions to blocks"| Blocks["Memory Blocks"]
        Blocks --> |"Contains"| Keys["Key Tensors"]
        Blocks --> |"Contains"| Values["Value Tensors"]
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:254-263](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py:309-318]()

## 3. Attention Variants

TGI implements several attention variants to accommodate different model architectures and to optimize for performance and memory usage.

### 3.1 Standard Multi-Head Attention

The traditional multi-head attention mechanism where each head has its own key and value projections.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Standard Multi-Head Attention"
        Input["Input Embedding"] -->|"Project"| Query["Query Heads (Nx)"]
        Input -->|"Project"| Key["Key Heads (Nx)"]
        Input -->|"Project"| Value["Value Heads (Nx)"]
        
        Query --> |"Attention"| Output["Attention Output"]
        Key --> |"Attention"| Output
        Value --> |"Attention"| Output
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:137-205]()

### 3.2 Multi-Query Attention (MQA)

In Multi-Query Attention, multiple query heads attend to a single key-value head, reducing memory requirements for storing the KV cache.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Multi-Query Attention"
        Input["Input Embedding"] -->|"Project"| Query["Query Heads (Nx)"]
        Input -->|"Project"| Key["Key Head (1x)"]
        Input -->|"Project"| Value["Value Head (1x)"]
        
        Query --> |"Attention"| Output["Attention Output"]
        Key --> |"Attention"| Output
        Value --> |"Attention"| Output
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py:230-320]()

### 3.3 Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)

Grouped-Query Attention is a middle ground between standard multi-head attention and multi-query attention. It groups query heads to share key-value heads, balancing memory usage and model quality.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Grouped-Query Attention"
        Input["Input Embedding"] -->|"Project"| Query["Query Heads (Nx)"]
        Input -->|"Project"| Key["Key Heads (Mx)"]
        Input -->|"Project"| Value["Value Heads (Mx)"]
        
        Query --> |"Group mapping"| AttentionOp["Attention Operation"]
        Key --> AttentionOp
        Value --> AttentionOp
        AttentionOp --> Output["Attention Output"]
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:201-204](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_rw_modeling.py:240-359]()

## 4. Key Optimization Techniques

### 4.1 Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE)

TGI implements Rotary Position Embeddings for encoding token positions in a way that enables efficient relative attention computation.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Rotary Position Embeddings"
        direction TB
        Query["Query Tensor"] --> |"Apply rotation"| RotQuery["Rotated Query"]
        Key["Key Tensor"] --> |"Apply rotation"| RotKey["Rotated Key"]
        Pos["Position IDs"] --> |"Generate"| CosSin["Cos/Sin Values"]
        CosSin --> |"Rotation matrix"| RotQuery
        CosSin --> |"Rotation matrix"| RotKey
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:155-160](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:591-593]()

### 4.2 Efficient KV Cache Management

The KV cache stores key and value tensors from previous tokens to avoid recomputation during auto-regressive generation.

Key optimizations:
- Block-based storage for non-contiguous memory access
- Efficient indexing through block tables
- Support for quantized KV cache to reduce memory footprint

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "KV Cache Management"
        direction TB
        Tensors["Key/Value Tensors"] --> |"Store"| Store["KVCache.store()"]
        Store --> |"Write to blocks"| Cache["Cached Key/Values"]
        Query["Query Tensor"] --> |"Retrieve relevant KV"| Retrieve["Paged Attention"]
        Cache --> |"Block Tables"| Retrieve
        Retrieve --> |"Compute Attention"| Output["Output Hidden States"]
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:232-237](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py:287-292]()

## 5. Tensor Parallelism Integration

TGI implements tensor parallelism for attention to allow distribution of attention computation across multiple GPUs.

### 5.1 Attention Tensor Splitting

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Tensor Parallelism for Attention"
        direction TB
        QKV["QKV Projection"] --> |"Split across devices"| ParallelHeads["Parallel Attention Heads"]
        ParallelHeads --> |"Process independently"| LocalAttn["Local Attention Computation"]
        LocalAttn --> |"Gather results"| OutputProj["Output Projection"]
    end
```

Key aspects:
- Query-Key-Value projections are sharded across devices
- Each device processes a subset of attention heads
- Results are gathered for the output projection

The code implements this by dividing the number of heads by the process group size:

```
self.num_heads = self.num_heads // weights.process_group.size()
self.num_key_value_heads = config.num_key_value_heads // weights.process_group.size()
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:177-180](), [server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py:268-279]()

### 5.2 Weight Loading for Tensor Parallelism

TGI uses specialized weight loading mechanisms for tensor-parallel attention:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Tensor-Parallel Weight Loading"
        direction TB
        Weights["Model Weights"] --> |"get_weights_col"| QKV["QKV Weights"]
        Weights --> |"get_weights_row"| Out["Output Projection Weights"]
        QKV --> |"Shard by column"| TPCol["TP Column Linear"]
        Out --> |"Shard by row"| TPRow["TP Row Linear"]
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/utils/weights.py:347-396](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:182-199]()

## 6. Attention Implementation Details by Model Type

TGI includes specialized attention implementations for different model architectures:

| Model Type | Attention Class | Special Features |
|------------|----------------|------------------|
| Llama      | FlashLlamaAttention | Supports multi-query/grouped-query, custom softmax scaling |
| Santacoder | FlashMQAttention | Implements Multi-Query Attention |
| NeoX       | FlashNeoxAttention | Partial rotary embeddings, specialized MLP integration |
| RefinedWeb | FlashRWAttention | Support for different layer norm configurations |
| Falcon     | FlashRWLargeAttention | Grouped-query attention with specialized block structure |

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:137-267](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py:230-320](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_neox_modeling.py:98-201](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_rw_modeling.py:128-237](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_rw_modeling.py:240-359]()

## 7. Attention Data Flow

The following diagram illustrates the data flow during attention computation in TGI:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Input as "Input Tokens"
    participant Linear as "Linear Projections"
    participant Rotary as "Rotary Embeddings"
    participant Cache as "KV Cache"
    participant Attn as "Attention Computation"
    participant Output as "Output Projection"
    
    Input->>Linear: Forward
    Linear->>Linear: Split into Q, K, V
    Linear->>Rotary: Apply position encoding
    Rotary->>Cache: Store K, V tensors
    
    alt Prefill Phase
        Rotary->>Attn: Q, K, V with Flash Attention
        Cache->>Attn: Block tables for storage
    else Decode Phase
        Rotary->>Attn: Only Q tensor
        Cache->>Attn: Retrieve K, V using Paged Attention
    end
    
    Attn->>Output: Attention output
    Output->>Output: Project to hidden size
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:206-267]()

## 8. Hardware-Specific Optimizations

TGI includes hardware-specific optimizations for attention computation:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Hardware-Specific Optimizations"
        direction TB
        CUDA["NVIDIA CUDA"] --> |"Flash Attention, Paged Attention"| Attention["Attention Computation"]
        ROCm["AMD ROCm"] --> |"Optimized linear ops"| Linear["Linear Projections"]
        TPU["Google TPU"] --> Attention
        Neuron["AWS Neuron"] --> Attention
    end
```

Key optimizations:
- NVIDIA CUDA: Flash Attention and Paged Attention kernels
- AMD ROCm: Optimized linear operations for attention projections
- Platform-specific conditional paths for optimal performance

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/layers/linear.py:47-113](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:62-69]()

## 9. Memory Optimization Techniques

Memory optimization is critical for efficient LLM inference. TGI implements several techniques:

1. **Flash Attention**: Reduces memory bandwidth requirements by avoiding materialization of the attention matrix
2. **Paged Attention**: Enables efficient memory management for the KV cache
3. **Attention Variants**: 
   - Multi-query attention: Reduces KV cache size by using one KV head for multiple query heads
   - Grouped-query attention: Balances model quality and memory usage

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Memory Usage by Attention Variant"
        direction LR
        Standard["Standard MHA"] --> |"N heads * seq_len * head_dim * 2"| StdMem["High Memory"]
        GQA["Grouped-Query"] --> |"(N/G) heads * seq_len * head_dim * 2"| GQAMem["Medium Memory"]
        MQA["Multi-Query"] --> |"1 head * seq_len * head_dim * 2"| MQAMem["Low Memory"]
    end
```

Sources: [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_llama_modeling.py:177-180](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_santacoder_modeling.py:230-320](), [server/text_generation_server/models/custom_modeling/flash_rw_modeling.py:240-359]()

# Page: Chat Templates and Structured Generation

# Chat Templates and Structured Generation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [backends/v2/src/backend.rs](backends/v2/src/backend.rs)
- [backends/v3/Cargo.toml](backends/v3/Cargo.toml)
- [backends/v3/src/backend.rs](backends/v3/src/backend.rs)
- [backends/v3/src/queue.rs](backends/v3/src/queue.rs)
- [backends/v3/src/radix.rs](backends/v3/src/radix.rs)
- [launcher/src/main.rs](launcher/src/main.rs)
- [router/Cargo.toml](router/Cargo.toml)
- [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs](router/src/infer/chat_template.rs)
- [router/src/infer/mod.rs](router/src/infer/mod.rs)
- [router/src/lib.rs](router/src/lib.rs)
- [router/src/server.rs](router/src/server.rs)
- [router/src/validation.rs](router/src/validation.rs)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents TGI's chat template system and structured generation capabilities. Chat templates transform conversational messages into model-specific prompt formats, while structured generation enforces output constraints through grammar-based validation. For information about the overall request processing pipeline, see [Request Flow and Batching](#2.4).

**Key capabilities covered:**
- Chat message formatting using Jinja2 templates
- JSON schema and regex-based output constraints
- Tool/function calling integration
- Grammar compilation and validation

---

## Chat Template System

### Overview

The chat template system converts OpenAI-style message arrays into model-specific prompt formats. Each model may require different conversation formatting (e.g., special tokens, role markers, system message placement).

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:1-138]()

### Template Engine Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    Request["ChatRequest<br/>{messages, tools}"]
    Template["ChatTemplate<br/>router/src/infer/chat_template.rs"]
    Minijinja["minijinja::Environment<br/>Template Engine"]
    Config["HubTokenizerConfig<br/>tokenizer_config.json"]
    
    Request --> Apply["apply()"]
    Template --> Apply
    Apply --> Minijinja
    Config --> |"chat_template field"| Template
    
    Apply --> ToolCheck{"tools defined?"}
    ToolCheck -->|"Yes"| AppendTools["Append tool JSON<br/>to last message"]
    ToolCheck -->|"No"| Render
    AppendTools --> Render["minijinja render()"]
    
    Render --> Output["Formatted Prompt String"]
    
    Template -.-> |"bos_token<br/>eos_token"| Render
    
    style Template fill:#f9f9f9
    style Minijinja fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:19-77](), [router/src/lib.rs:121-145]()

### Template Loading

Templates are loaded from the model's `tokenizer_config.json` or `preprocessor_config.json`:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Infer["Infer::new()"]
    TokenizerConfig["HubTokenizerConfig<br/>tokenizer_config.json"]
    ProcessorConfig["HubProcessorConfig<br/>preprocessor_config.json"]
    
    Infer --> Check{"template source?"}
    Check --> TokenizerConfig
    Check --> ProcessorConfig
    
    TokenizerConfig --> Versions{"ChatTemplateVersions"}
    Versions --> Single["Single(String)"]
    Versions --> Multiple["Multiple(Vec)"]
    
    Multiple --> FindDefault["Find 'default' template"]
    Single --> Create
    FindDefault --> Create["ChatTemplate::new()"]
    
    Create --> MinijinjaEnv["Create minijinja::Environment"]
    MinijinjaEnv --> AddFunctions["Add custom functions:<br/>raise_exception()<br/>strftime_now()"]
    AddFunctions --> ParseTemplate["Parse template string"]
    ParseTemplate --> DetectToolSupport["Detect if 'tools'<br/>variable exists"]
    
    style Create fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/mod.rs:64-96](), [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:28-77]()

### Template Application Process

The `ChatTemplate::apply()` method processes messages and tools:

| Step | Action | Code Location |
|------|--------|---------------|
| 1. Tool Handling | If tools provided and template doesn't use `tools` variable, append tool JSON to last message content | [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:84-105]() |
| 2. Message Conversion | Convert `Message` objects to `TextMessage` format | [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:107]() |
| 3. Template Rendering | Render using minijinja with `ChatTemplateInputs` | [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:109-118]() |
| 4. Assistant Continuation | If last message is from assistant, trim to continue generation | [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:120-133]() |

**Template Variables Available:**
- `messages`: Array of message objects with `role` and `content`
- `bos_token`: Beginning of sequence token (optional)
- `eos_token`: End of sequence token (optional)
- `add_generation_prompt`: Boolean flag (always `true`)
- `tools`: Array of tool definitions (optional)

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:79-137]()

### Custom Template Functions

Two custom functions are injected into the template environment:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Functions["Custom Functions"]
    RaiseException["raise_exception(err_text)<br/>Throws minijinja::Error"]
    StrftimeNow["strftime_now(format_str)<br/>Returns formatted datetime"]
    
    Functions --> RaiseException
    Functions --> StrftimeNow
    
    RaiseException --> Usage1["Used in templates for<br/>validation errors"]
    StrftimeNow --> Usage2["Used for date injection<br/>(e.g., Llama templates)"]
```

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:9-17](), [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:56-57]()

### Template Mutations

TGI applies several template string transformations before parsing:

| Mutation | Purpose | Example |
|----------|---------|---------|
| Gemma3 Content Path | Fix nested content access | `messages[0]['content'][0]['text']` → `messages[0]['content']` |
| Qwen3 List Reversal | Replace Python list reversal | `[::-1]` → `\|reverse` |
| Remove Generation Tags | Strip training-only markers | `{% generation %}` → (removed) |

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:38-53]()

---

## Structured Generation

### Grammar Types

TGI supports three types of grammar constraints defined in the `GrammarType` enum:

```mermaid
graph TB
    GrammarType["GrammarType enum<br/>router/src/lib.rs:239-258"]
    
    GrammarType --> Json["Json(serde_json::Value)<br/>Simple JSON schema"]
    GrammarType --> JsonSchema["JsonSchema(JsonSchemaConfig)<br/>Schema + metadata"]
    GrammarType --> Regex["Regex(String)<br/>Pattern constraint"]
    
    Json --> JsonDesc["Auto-converted to regex<br/>via outlines-core"]
    JsonSchema --> JsonSchemaDesc["name: Option String<br/>schema: serde_json::Value<br/>strict mode support"]
    Regex --> RegexDesc["Direct regex pattern<br/>applied to tokens"]
    
    style GrammarType fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [router/src/lib.rs:236-258]()

### JSON Schema Configuration

The `JsonSchemaConfig` structure supports advanced JSON schema validation:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Config["JsonSchemaConfig"]
    Config --> Name["name: Option String<br/>Schema identifier"]
    Config --> Schema["schema: serde_json::Value<br/>JSON schema definition"]
    
    Config --> Validation["Validation Requirements"]
    Validation --> V1["Must be valid JSON Schema<br/>(draft202012)"]
    Validation --> V2["Must have 'properties' field"]
    Validation --> V3["Compiled to regex<br/>for enforcement"]
```

**Sources:** [router/src/lib.rs:225-258](), [router/src/validation.rs:385-406]()

### Grammar Validation Pipeline

```mermaid
graph TB
    Request["GenerateRequest<br/>with grammar field"]
    Validate["Validation::validate()"]
    
    Request --> Validate
    Validate --> CheckSupport{"Grammar support<br/>enabled?"}
    CheckSupport -->|"No"| Error["ValidationError::Grammar"]
    CheckSupport -->|"Yes"| ParseType{"Grammar Type?"}
    
    ParseType --> JsonPath["Json Type"]
    ParseType --> JsonSchemaPath["JsonSchema Type"]
    ParseType --> RegexPath["Regex Type"]
    
    JsonPath --> EnsureObject["Ensure JSON object<br/>(parse if string)"]
    EnsureObject --> ValidateSchema1["jsonschema::validate()"]
    ValidateSchema1 --> CheckProps1["Check 'properties' exists"]
    CheckProps1 --> Compile1["json_schema_to_regex()<br/>outlines-core"]
    
    JsonSchemaPath --> ValidateSchema2["jsonschema::validate()"]
    ValidateSchema2 --> CheckProps2["Check 'properties' exists"]
    CheckProps2 --> Compile2["json_schema_to_regex()<br/>outlines-core"]
    
    RegexPath --> DirectUse["Use regex directly"]
    
    Compile1 --> ValidGrammar["ValidGrammar::Regex(String)"]
    Compile2 --> ValidGrammar
    DirectUse --> ValidGrammar
    
    ValidGrammar --> SendToPython["Sent to Python server<br/>for enforcement"]
    
    style Validate fill:#f9f9f9
    style ValidGrammar fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [router/src/validation.rs:346-412](), [router/Cargo.toml:26]()

### Validation Implementation Details

The validation process occurs in `Validation::validate()`:

| Step | Check | Error Type |
|------|-------|------------|
| 1. Feature Check | `disable_grammar_support == false` | `ValidationError::Grammar` |
| 2. JSON Parsing | If string, parse to JSON object | `ValidationError::InvalidGrammar` |
| 3. Schema Validation | Validate against JSON Schema draft202012 | `ValidationError::InvalidGrammar` |
| 4. Properties Check | Ensure `properties` field exists | `ValidationError::InvalidGrammar` |
| 5. Regex Compilation | Compile schema to regex via `outlines-core` | `ValidationError::RegexFromSchema` |

**Sources:** [router/src/validation.rs:348-412]()

### Grammar Enforcement

Once validated, grammars are sent to the Python server as part of the request:

```mermaid
graph LR
    ValidRequest["ValidGenerateRequest<br/>parameters.grammar"]
    Queue["Queue::append()"]
    Batch["Batch creation"]
    
    ValidRequest --> Queue
    Queue --> Batch
    
    Batch --> Request["Request proto<br/>NextTokenChooserParameters"]
    Request --> Grammar["grammar: Option String<br/>grammar_type: GrammarType"]
    
    Grammar --> Python["Python Server<br/>FSM-based sampling"]
    Python --> Token["Constrained token<br/>selection"]
```

**Sources:** [backends/v3/src/queue.rs:430-442]()

---

## Tool Calling Integration

### Tool Grammar System

TGI provides a dedicated tool grammar system in `router/src/infer/tool_grammar.rs`:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Tools["Vec Tool<br/>Function definitions"]
    ToolGrammar["ToolGrammar struct<br/>router/src/infer/tool_grammar.rs"]
    
    Tools --> Build["ToolGrammar::from_tools()"]
    Build --> Parse["Parse each FunctionDefinition"]
    Parse --> ExtractParams["Extract parameters schema"]
    
    ExtractParams --> CreateSchema["Build JSON schema:<br/>{<br/>  name: function_name,<br/>  parameters: {...}<br/>}"]
    
    CreateSchema --> Compile["Compile to regex<br/>via outlines-core"]
    Compile --> ToolGrammar
    
    ToolGrammar --> Apply["Apply to generation"]
    Apply --> Parse2["Parse generated JSON"]
    Parse2 --> ToolCall["Extract ToolCall objects"]
    
    style ToolGrammar fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/tool_grammar.rs]() (referenced but not fully shown in files)

### Tool Integration with Chat Templates

When tools are provided, they're integrated into the chat template application:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Router as Router
    participant Infer as Infer
    participant ChatTemplate as ChatTemplate
    participant Validation as Validation
    
    Router->>Infer: apply_chat_template(messages, tools)
    
    alt tools provided
        Infer->>Infer: Prepare tools_and_prompt<br/>(tools, tool_prompt)
    end
    
    Infer->>ChatTemplate: apply(messages, tools_and_prompt)
    
    alt template uses 'tools' variable
        ChatTemplate->>ChatTemplate: Pass tools to template
    else template doesn't use 'tools'
        ChatTemplate->>ChatTemplate: Append tool JSON + prompt<br/>to last message
    end
    
    ChatTemplate->>ChatTemplate: Render with minijinja
    ChatTemplate-->>Infer: Formatted prompt string
    
    Infer->>Validation: validate(GenerateRequest)
    
    alt grammar specified
        Validation->>Validation: Validate and compile grammar
    end
    
    Validation-->>Router: ValidGenerateRequest
```

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/chat_template.rs:79-105](), [router/src/infer/mod.rs:225-241]()

### Tool Call Message Format

Tool calls are represented in the message structure:

```mermaid
graph TB
    OutputMessage["OutputMessage enum"]
    
    OutputMessage --> ChatMsg["ChatMessage(TextMessage)<br/>Regular text response"]
    OutputMessage --> ToolMsg["ToolCall(ToolCallMessage)<br/>Function call response"]
    
    ToolMsg --> TCM["ToolCallMessage"]
    TCM --> Role["role: 'assistant'"]
    TCM --> Calls["tool_calls: Vec ToolCall"]
    
    Calls --> TC["ToolCall"]
    TC --> Index["index: u32"]
    TC --> ID["id: String"]
    TC --> Type["type: 'function'"]
    TC --> Func["function: FunctionName"]
    
    Func --> FName["name: String"]
    Func --> Args["arguments: String (JSON)"]
```

**Sources:** [router/src/lib.rs:827-891]() (various tool-related structures)

---

## Request Flow Integration

### End-to-End Processing

The complete flow from chat request to constrained generation:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Client["Client Request"]
    ChatEndpoint["/v1/chat/completions<br/>router/src/server.rs:chat"]
    
    Client --> ChatEndpoint
    
    ChatEndpoint --> ParseTools{"tools field<br/>present?"}
    ParseTools -->|"Yes"| ToolProcess["Process tool definitions<br/>Extract grammar"]
    ParseTools -->|"No"| SkipTools["No tool processing"]
    
    ToolProcess --> ApplyTemplate
    SkipTools --> ApplyTemplate["Infer::apply_chat_template()"]
    
    ApplyTemplate --> ChatTemplate["ChatTemplate::apply()<br/>Format messages"]
    ChatTemplate --> FormattedPrompt["Formatted prompt string"]
    
    FormattedPrompt --> CreateRequest["GenerateRequest"]
    CreateRequest --> Validate["Validation::validate()"]
    
    Validate --> CheckGrammar{"grammar parameter?"}
    CheckGrammar -->|"Yes"| ValidateGrammar["Validate and compile grammar"]
    CheckGrammar -->|"No"| SkipGrammar["No grammar constraint"]
    
    ValidateGrammar --> ValidRequest
    SkipGrammar --> ValidRequest["ValidGenerateRequest"]
    
    ValidRequest --> Backend["Backend::schedule()"]
    Backend --> PythonServer["Python Server<br/>FSM-constrained sampling"]
    
    PythonServer --> Response["Generated tokens<br/>(constrained if grammar)"]
    
    style ChatTemplate fill:#f9f9f9
    style ValidateGrammar fill:#f9f9f9
```

**Sources:** [router/src/server.rs:1010-1090](), [router/src/infer/mod.rs:225-241](), [router/src/validation.rs:203-447]()

### Configuration Sources

Chat templates and grammar support are configured from multiple sources:

| Configuration | Source | Priority |
|---------------|--------|----------|
| Chat Template | `processor_config.json` | Higher |
| Chat Template | `tokenizer_config.json` | Lower |
| BOS/EOS Tokens | `tokenizer_config.json` | Only source |
| Grammar Support | `--disable-grammar-support` flag | Launch time |

**Sources:** [router/src/infer/mod.rs:71-81](), [router/src/validation.rs:41-102]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes TGI's multi-backend architecture, which enables deployment across diverse hardware platforms including Nvidia GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel GPUs/CPUs, Intel Gaudi accelerators, AWS Inferentia/Trainium, and Google TPUs. The backend abstraction layer provides a consistent API interface while allowing platform-specific optimizations.

For specific deployment instructions on each platform, see:
- Nvidia GPUs: see platform-specific documentation (not in wiki)
- AMD GPUs: see platform-specific documentation  
- Intel hardware: see platform-specific documentation
- Other backends: [TensorRT-LLM backend](#5), [Neuron backend](#5), [llama.cpp backend](#5)

For information about the overall system architecture, see [System Architecture](#2).

## Backend Architecture Overview

TGI's backend system separates the platform-agnostic **Router** component from platform-specific **Model Server** implementations. The launcher (`text-generation-launcher`) selects and configures the appropriate backend at startup based on environment variables and command-line arguments.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Common Layer"
        Launcher["text-generation-launcher<br/>[launcher/src/main.rs]"]
        Router["text-generation-router<br/>[backends/v3/src]<br/>Platform-agnostic gRPC client"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Backend Selection Logic"
        EnvDetect["Environment Detection<br/>CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES<br/>ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES<br/>etc."]
        DockerImage["Docker Image Selection<br/>Dockerfile*"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Backend Implementations"
        CudaServer["CUDA Server<br/>[server/text_generation_server]<br/>Nvidia GPUs"]
        RocmServer["ROCm Server<br/>[Dockerfile_amd]<br/>AMD GPUs"]
        IntelServer["Intel Server<br/>[Dockerfile_intel]<br/>XPU/CPU"]
        GaudiServer["Gaudi Server<br/>[backends/gaudi]<br/>Intel Gaudi"]
        NeuronServer["Neuron Server<br/>[backends/neuron]<br/>AWS Inferentia"]
        TrtllmServer["TensorRT-LLM Server<br/>[backends/trtllm]<br/>Nvidia Optimized"]
        LlamacppServer["llama.cpp Server<br/>[backends/llamacpp]<br/>CPU/Universal"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Hardware Layer"
        NvidiaGPU["Nvidia GPU<br/>H100/A100/etc."]
        AMDGPU["AMD GPU<br/>MI210/MI250/MI300"]
        IntelXPU["Intel GPU<br/>Max1100/Max1550"]
        IntelCPU["Intel CPU"]
        GaudiChip["Gaudi Accelerator"]
        InferentiaChip["AWS Inferentia"]
    end
    
    Launcher --> EnvDetect
    Launcher --> DockerImage
    Launcher --> Router
    
    Router -.->|"gRPC Interface"| CudaServer
    Router -.->|"gRPC Interface"| RocmServer
    Router -.->|"gRPC Interface"| IntelServer
    Router -.->|"gRPC Interface"| GaudiServer
    Router -.->|"gRPC Interface"| NeuronServer
    Router -.->|"gRPC Interface"| TrtllmServer
    Router -.->|"gRPC Interface"| LlamacppServer
    
    CudaServer --> NvidiaGPU
    RocmServer --> AMDGPU
    IntelServer --> IntelXPU
    IntelServer --> IntelCPU
    GaudiServer --> GaudiChip
    NeuronServer --> InferentiaChip
    TrtllmServer --> NvidiaGPU
    LlamacppServer --> IntelCPU
```

**Sources:** [README.md:65-72](), [docs/source/multi_backend_support.md:1-17](), [Cargo.toml:3-11]()

## Backend Selection Mechanism

Backend selection occurs through multiple mechanisms:

### Docker Image Selection

The primary method for backend selection is choosing the appropriate Docker image. Each backend has a dedicated Dockerfile that installs platform-specific dependencies:

| Backend | Dockerfile | Base Image | Docker Tag Suffix |
|---------|-----------|------------|-------------------|
| CUDA (Default) | `Dockerfile` | `nvidia/cuda:12.4.0-base-ubuntu22.04` | *(none)* |
| ROCm | `Dockerfile_amd` | `rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:6.3.1-complete` | `-rocm` |
| Intel XPU | `Dockerfile_intel` | `intel/oneapi-basekit:2025.1.3-0-devel-ubuntu22.04` | `-intel-xpu` |
| Intel CPU | `Dockerfile_intel` | `ubuntu:22.04` | `-intel-cpu` |
| Gaudi | `Dockerfile_gaudi` | Backend-specific | `-gaudi` |
| Neuron | `Dockerfile.neuron` | Backend-specific | `-neuron` |
| TensorRT-LLM | `Dockerfile_trtllm` | Backend-specific | `-trtllm` |

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:58-136](), [Dockerfile:1-251](), [Dockerfile_amd:1-315](), [Dockerfile_intel:1-223]()

### Environment Variable Configuration

Backends are configured through environment variables set in the Docker containers:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "CUDA Backend Variables"
        CUDA_VISIBLE["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"]
        TORCH_ARCH["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"]
        EXLLAMA["EXLLAMA_NO_FLASH_ATTN"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ROCm Backend Variables"
        ROCM_DEVICE["ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES"]
        ROCM_FA["ROCM_USE_FLASH_ATTN_V2_TRITON"]
        ROCM_PA["ROCM_USE_CUSTOM_PAGED_ATTN"]
        PYTORCH_TUNE["PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED"]
        HIP_FORCE["HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Intel Backend Variables"
        CCL_ZE["CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE"]
        TORCH_LLM["TORCH_LLM_ALLREDUCE"]
        CCL_TOPO["CCL_TOPO_FABRIC_VERTEX_CONNECTION_CHECK"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Common Variables"
        ATTENTION["ATTENTION"]

```

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:147-216](), [Dockerfile_amd:242-306](), [Dockerfile_intel:93-119](), [Dockerfile_intel:192-197]()

### Build Matrix Strategy

The CI/CD system builds all backend variants in parallel using a matrix strategy:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "GitHub Actions Workflow"
        Trigger["Workflow Trigger<br/>ci_build.yaml"]
        Matrix["Matrix Strategy<br/>7 Hardware Platforms"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Build Jobs"
        CudaBuild["cuda build<br/>Dockerfile"]
        TrtllmBuild["cuda-trtllm build<br/>Dockerfile_trtllm"]
        RocmBuild["rocm build<br/>Dockerfile_amd"]
        IntelXpuBuild["intel-xpu build<br/>Dockerfile_intel<br/>PLATFORM=xpu"]
        IntelCpuBuild["intel-cpu build<br/>Dockerfile_intel<br/>PLATFORM=cpu"]
        NeuronBuild["neuron build<br/>Dockerfile.neuron"]
        GaudiBuild["gaudi build<br/>Dockerfile_gaudi"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Build Outputs"
        DockerRegistry["Docker Registries<br/>ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:*"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Tests"
        TestRunner["pytest integration-tests/<br/>--neuron or --gaudi flags"]
    end
    
    Trigger --> Matrix
    Matrix --> CudaBuild
    Matrix --> TrtllmBuild
    Matrix --> RocmBuild
    Matrix --> IntelXpuBuild
    Matrix --> IntelCpuBuild
    Matrix --> NeuronBuild
    Matrix --> GaudiBuild
    
    CudaBuild --> DockerRegistry
    TrtllmBuild --> DockerRegistry
    RocmBuild --> DockerRegistry
    IntelXpuBuild --> DockerRegistry
    IntelCpuBuild --> DockerRegistry
    NeuronBuild --> DockerRegistry
    GaudiBuild --> DockerRegistry
    
    DockerRegistry --> TestRunner
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/ci_build.yaml:36-52](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:21-52]()

## Supported Backends

### CUDA Backend (Nvidia GPUs)

The default and most feature-complete backend, optimized for Nvidia GPUs with CUDA 12.2+.

**Key Features:**
- Flash Attention v1 and v2
- Paged Attention
- FP8/INT8 quantization (GPTQ, AWQ, bitsandbytes, EETQ, Marlin)
- CUDA Graphs for reduced kernel launch overhead
- NCCL for multi-GPU tensor parallelism
- Custom kernels for specific operations (RoPE, LayerNorm, etc.)

**Kernel Build Stages:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    BaseImage["pytorch-install stage<br/>PyTorch 2.7 + CUDA 12.4"]
    
    FlashAtt["flash-att-builder<br/>[server/Makefile-flash-att]"]
    FlashAttV2["flash-att-v2-builder<br/>[server/Makefile-flash-att-v2]"]
    Exllama["exllama-kernels-builder<br/>[server/exllama_kernels/]"]
    ExllamaV2["exllamav2-kernels-builder<br/>[server/Makefile-exllamav2]"]
    AWQ["awq-kernels-builder<br/>[server/Makefile-awq]"]
    Custom["custom-kernels-builder<br/>[server/custom_kernels/]"]
    Mamba["mamba-builder<br/>[server/Makefile-selective-scan]"]
    Flashinfer["flashinfer-builder<br/>[server/Makefile-flashinfer]"]
    
    BaseImage --> FlashAtt
    BaseImage --> FlashAttV2
    BaseImage --> Exllama
    BaseImage --> ExllamaV2
    BaseImage --> AWQ
    BaseImage --> Custom
    BaseImage --> Mamba
    BaseImage --> Flashinfer
    
    FlashAtt --> FinalImage["Final CUDA Image"]
    FlashAttV2 --> FinalImage
    Exllama --> FinalImage
    ExllamaV2 --> FinalImage
    AWQ --> FinalImage
    Custom --> FinalImage
    Mamba --> FinalImage
    Flashinfer --> FinalImage
```

**Environment Variables:**
- `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.0;8.6;9.0+PTX"` - Target GPU architectures
- `EXLLAMA_NO_FLASH_ATTN=1` - Disable flash attention in exllama
- `MAX_JOBS=8` - Parallel compilation jobs

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-251](), [Dockerfile:73-142](), [server/Makefile:1-51]()

### ROCm Backend (AMD GPUs)

Supports AMD Instinct MI210, MI250, and MI300 GPUs using the ROCm platform.

**Key Features:**
- Flash Attention (Composable Kernel or Triton implementation)
- Custom Paged Attention kernel
- TunableOp for GEMM optimization
- ROCm-specific quantization kernels

**Backend-Specific Optimizations:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ROCm Kernel Builds"
        HipBLASLt["build_hipblaslt stage<br/>hipBLASLt library<br/>HIPBLASLT_BRANCH=4d40e36"]
        RCCL["build_rccl stage<br/>RCCL collective ops<br/>RCCL_BRANCH=648a58d"]
        Triton["build_triton stage<br/>Triton compiler<br/>TRITON_BRANCH=e5be006"]
        PyTorch["build_pytorch stage<br/>PyTorch + ROCm<br/>PYTORCH_BRANCH=3a585126"]
        FlashAttn["Flash Attention<br/>FA_BRANCH=b7d29fb"]
        Aiter["aiter library<br/>AITER_BRANCH=21d47a9"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Custom Kernels"
        VllmROCm["vllm-builder<br/>[server/Makefile-vllm]<br/>ROCm-specific vLLM"]
        MarlinROCm["marlin-kernels<br/>v0.3.6<br/>VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm"]
        MoeROCm["moe-kernels<br/>v0.8.2<br/>VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Environment Configuration"
        FlashMode["ROCM_USE_FLASH_ATTN_V2_TRITON=0<br/>Use CK instead of Triton"]
        PagedMode["ROCM_USE_CUSTOM_PAGED_ATTN=1<br/>Custom paged attention"]
        TunableOp["PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=1<br/>GEMM kernel selection"]
        SkinnyGemm["ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=1<br/>Optimized GEMM shapes"]
    end
```

**Configuration Variables:**
- `ROCM_USE_FLASH_ATTN_V2_TRITON=0` - Use Composable Kernel (default)
- `ROCM_USE_CUSTOM_PAGED_ATTN=1` - Enable custom paged attention
- `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_ENABLED=1` - Enable TunableOp warmup
- `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx90a;gfx942"` - Target GPU architectures
- `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1` - ROCm execution optimization

**Sources:** [Dockerfile_amd:1-315](), [Dockerfile_amd:44-66](), [Dockerfile_amd:97-230](), [docs/source/installation_amd.md:1-45]()

### Intel XPU Backend (Intel GPUs)

Supports Intel Data Center GPUs (Max1100, Max1550) using Intel Extension for PyTorch (IPEX).

**Key Features:**
- Flash Decoding attention via IPEX
- OneDNN optimizations
- Prefix caching and prefill chunking

**Build Process:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    BaseOneAPI["intel/oneapi-basekit:2025.1.3-0<br/>OneAPI Tools"]
    
    Mambaforge["Mambaforge Install<br/>Python 3.11.10"]
    
    LibSSL["libssl.so.1.1 Install<br/>Ubuntu 22.04 compatibility"]
    
    IntelRepos["Intel Repository Setup<br/>intel-graphics.key<br/>oneAPI repos"]
    
    XPUTools["XPU Tools Install<br/>xpu-smi, ocloc, libnl-genl"]
    
    PyTorchXPU["PyTorch XPU Install<br/>torch==2.8.0<br/>--index-url pytorch.org/whl/xpu"]
    
    IPEX["IPEX Install<br/>intel_extension_for_pytorch<br/>2.8.10+xpu"]
    
    BaseOneAPI --> Mambaforge
    Mambaforge --> LibSSL
    LibSSL --> IntelRepos
    IntelRepos --> XPUTools
    XPUTools --> PyTorchXPU
    PyTorchXPU --> IPEX
```

**Environment Variables:**
- `CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=sockets` - Collective communication method
- `TORCH_LLM_ALLREDUCE=1` - Enable all-reduce optimization
- `CCL_TOPO_FABRIC_VERTEX_CONNECTION_CHECK=0` - Disable topology check
- `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0` - Disable auto-loading
- `ATTENTION=flashdecoding-ipex` - Use IPEX flash decoding

**Sources:** [Dockerfile_intel:1-120](), [Dockerfile_intel:48-120](), [docs/source/installation_intel.md:1-18]()

### Intel CPU Backend

Optimized inference on Intel CPUs using IPEX and OneDNN.

**Key Features:**
- OneDNN primitive operations
- MKL (Math Kernel Library) optimizations
- tcmalloc memory allocator
- OneCCL for multi-socket communication

**Build Configuration:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    UbuntuBase["ubuntu:22.04"]
    
    Compilers["g++-12, gcc-12, cmake<br/>libnuma-dev"]
    
    Mambaforge["Mambaforge<br/>Python 3.11.10"]
    
    CondaTools["conda install<br/>gperftools, mkl"]
    
    PyTorchCPU["PyTorch CPU<br/>torch==2.7.0<br/>--index-url pytorch.org/whl/cpu"]
    
    TritonLibnuma["triton==3.2.0<br/>py-libnuma"]
    
    IPEXCPU["IPEX CPU<br/>intel_extension_for_pytorch<br/>2.7.0+cpu"]
    
    OneCCL["oneccl_bind_pt<br/>2.7.0+cpu"]
    
    UbuntuBase --> Compilers
    Compilers --> Mambaforge
    Mambaforge --> CondaTools
    CondaTools --> PyTorchCPU
    PyTorchCPU --> TritonLibnuma
    TritonLibnuma --> IPEXCPU
    IPEXCPU --> OneCCL
```

**Environment Variables:**
- `LD_PRELOAD=/opt/conda/lib/libtcmalloc.so` - Memory allocator
- `CCL_ROOT=/opt/conda/lib/python3.11/site-packages/oneccl_bindings_for_pytorch`
- `ATTENTION=flashdecoding-ipex`
- `PREFIX_CACHING=1`
- `PREFILL_CHUNKING=1`
- `CUDA_GRAPHS=0` - Disabled for CPU

**Sources:** [Dockerfile_intel:130-214](), [Dockerfile_intel:181-197](), [docs/source/installation_intel.md:19-36]()

### Gaudi Backend (Intel Gaudi Accelerators)

Specialized backend for Intel Gaudi AI accelerators with HPU-specific optimizations.

**Key Features:**
- HPU Graphs for kernel fusion
- Exponential bucketing for sequence lengths
- HPU-specific paged attention
- Custom collective operations

**Integration:**
- Backend code in separate directory: `backends/gaudi/`
- Specialized Docker image: `Dockerfile_gaudi`
- Test fixtures: `integration-tests/fixtures/gaudi/service.py`

**Configuration:**
- Requires `--gaudi` flag in integration tests
- Custom environment setup for HPU devices
- Test subset via `--gaudi-all-models` flag

**Sources:** [integration-tests/conftest.py:76-84](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:101-114](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:127-136]()

### Neuron Backend (AWS Inferentia/Trainium)

Backend for AWS Neuron SDK on Inferentia and Trainium chips.

**Key Features:**
- Model pre-compilation to Neuron format
- Export models script for compilation
- Specialized test fixtures

**Pre-compilation Workflow:**

```mermaid
graph LR
    HubModel["Hugging Face Hub Model<br/>Original Model"]
    
    ExportScript["export_models.py<br/>[integration-tests/fixtures/neuron/]<br/>Compilation script"]
    
    NeuronModel["Neuron-compiled Model<br/>Optimized for Inferentia"]
    
    TestFixture["tgi_service fixture<br/>[integration-tests/neuron/test_implicit_env.py]<br/>hub/hub-neuron/local-neuron"]
    
    TGIService["TGI Service<br/>--neuron flag"]
    
    HubModel --> ExportScript
    ExportScript --> NeuronModel
    NeuronModel --> TestFixture
    TestFixture --> TGIService
```

**Test Configuration:**
- Environment variables: `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `MAX_INPUT_TOKENS`, `MAX_TOTAL_TOKENS`, `HF_NUM_CORES`, `HF_AUTO_CAST_TYPE`
- Model deployment options: hub original, hub pre-exported, local path
- Integration test flag: `--neuron`

**Sources:** [integration-tests/conftest.py:68-84](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:116-131](), [integration-tests/neuron/test_implicit_env.py:1-65](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:250-278]()

### TensorRT-LLM Backend

High-performance backend leveraging Nvidia's TensorRT-LLM library.

**Key Features:**
- Model-specific compilation for GPU architecture
- Custom optimized kernels
- Advanced quantization support
- Requires compilation step per model/GPU combination

**Build System:**
- Dockerfile: `Dockerfile_trtllm`
- Backend directory: `backends/trtllm/`
- Version extraction: `grep -oP '([a-z,0-9]{40})' backends/trtllm/cmake/trtllm.cmake`
- Build type selection: `release` for tags, `dev` with `ci-runtime` target otherwise

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:51-54](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:69-83](), [Cargo.toml:7]()

### llama.cpp Backend

Universal CPU/GPU backend using llama.cpp inference engine.

**Key Features:**
- CPU-optimized inference
- Wide model compatibility
- No GPU required
- Portable deployment

**Integration:**
- Backend directory: `backends/llamacpp/`
- Rust workspace member
- Universal fallback option

**Sources:** [Cargo.toml:8](), [docs/source/multi_backend_support.md:14-15]()

## Build System Integration

### Multi-Stage Docker Build Pattern

All backends follow a similar multi-stage build pattern:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Stage 1: Rust Build"
        Chef["cargo-chef<br/>Dependency caching"]
        Planner["planner stage<br/>recipe.json generation"]
        Builder["builder stage<br/>Release compilation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Python Environment"
        PyBase["Base Python Stage<br/>PyTorch + dependencies"]
        KernelBuilders["Kernel Builder Stages<br/>Platform-specific"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Assembly"
        ServerInstall["Server Install<br/>[server/text_generation_server]<br/>uv sync"]
        KernelCopy["Copy Kernel Artifacts<br/>--from=kernel-builders"]
        BinaryCopy["Copy Rust Binaries<br/>text-generation-*"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Final Stage"
        Entrypoint["Entrypoint Setup<br/>tgi-entrypoint.sh"]
        EnvVars["Environment Variables<br/>Backend-specific"]
    end
    
    Chef --> Planner
    Planner --> Builder
    
    PyBase --> KernelBuilders
    
    Builder --> BinaryCopy
    KernelBuilders --> KernelCopy
    PyBase --> ServerInstall
    
    BinaryCopy --> Entrypoint
    KernelCopy --> Entrypoint
    ServerInstall --> Entrypoint
    Entrypoint --> EnvVars
```

**Common Rust Binaries:**
- `text-generation-launcher` - [launcher/src/main.rs]()
- `text-generation-router` - [backends/v3/src]()
- `text-generation-benchmark` - [benchmark/src]()

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-251](), [Dockerfile_amd:1-315](), [Dockerfile_intel:1-223]()

### CI/CD Matrix Build

The build workflow constructs all backends in parallel:

```mermaid
graph TB
    PushTrigger["GitHub Push/Tag/PR<br/>ci_build.yaml"]
    
    MatrixDef["Matrix Definition<br/>hardware: [cuda, cuda-trtllm, rocm,<br/>intel-xpu, intel-cpu, neuron, gaudi]"]
    
    subgraph "Per-Backend Jobs"
        HWVars["Construct Hardware Variables<br/>dockerfile, label_extension,<br/>docker_devices, runs_on, platform"]
        DockerBuild["Docker Build & Push<br/>--platform linux/amd64<br/>AWS S3 cache"]
        IntTests["Integration Tests<br/>pytest integration-tests/<br/>--release flag conditional"]
    end
    
    Registries["Push to Registries<br/>ghcr.io, docker.io<br/>registry.internal.huggingface.tech"]
    
    PushTrigger --> MatrixDef
    MatrixDef --> HWVars
    HWVars --> DockerBuild
    DockerBuild --> Registries
    DockerBuild --> IntTests
```

**Build Variables per Hardware:**
- `dockerfile` - Dockerfile name
- `label_extension` - Docker tag suffix (e.g., `-rocm`, `-intel-xpu`)
- `docker_devices` - Device mount points (e.g., `/dev/kfd`, `/dev/dri`)
- `docker_volume` - Cache volume mount
- `runs_on` - GitHub runner label
- `platform` - Backend platform identifier
- `extra_pytest` - Additional pytest flags

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/ci_build.yaml:35-52](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:55-152](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:212-235]()

## Testing Infrastructure

### Backend-Specific Test Fixtures

The test infrastructure provides backend-specific fixtures:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "pytest Configuration"
        AddOptions["pytest_addoption<br/>[conftest.py:68-84]<br/>--release, --neuron, --gaudi"]
        Configure["pytest_configure<br/>Register markers"]
        ModifyItems["pytest_collection_modifyitems<br/>Skip logic per backend"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Service Fixtures"
        NeuronService["neuron_launcher fixture<br/>[fixtures/neuron/service.py]"]
        GaudiService["gaudi_launcher fixture<br/>[fixtures/gaudi/service.py]"]
        GenericLauncher["launcher fixture<br/>[conftest.py:463-587]<br/>local_launcher context manager"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Test Execution"
        NeuronTests["Neuron Tests<br/>integration-tests/neuron/<br/>@pytest.mark.neuron"]
        GaudiTests["Gaudi Tests<br/>@pytest.mark.gaudi"]
        StandardTests["Standard Tests<br/>All other tests"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Docker Configuration"
        DockerImage["DOCKER_IMAGE env var<br/>Backend-specific image"]
        DockerDevices["DOCKER_DEVICES env var<br/>/dev/kfd, /dev/neuron0, etc."]
        DockerVolume["DOCKER_VOLUME env var<br/>Cache mount point"]
    end
    
    AddOptions --> Configure
    Configure --> ModifyItems
    ModifyItems --> NeuronTests
    ModifyItems --> GaudiTests
    ModifyItems --> StandardTests
    
    NeuronService --> NeuronTests
    GaudiService --> GaudiTests
    GenericLauncher --> StandardTests
    
    DockerImage --> GenericLauncher
    DockerDevices --> GenericLauncher
    DockerVolume --> GenericLauncher
```

**Environment Variables:**
- `DOCKER_IMAGE` - Backend-specific image from build matrix
- `DOCKER_DEVICES` - Hardware device mounts
- `DOCKER_VOLUME` - Volume for model cache
- `HF_TOKEN` - Hugging Face authentication

**Test Markers:**
- `@pytest.mark.neuron` - Neuron backend tests
- `@pytest.mark.gaudi` - Gaudi backend tests
- `@pytest.mark.release` - Long-running release tests

**Sources:** [integration-tests/conftest.py:1-587](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:68-136](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:463-587](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:279-310]()

### Backend Test Execution Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant GHA as GitHub Actions
    participant Build as build-and-push Job
    participant Docker as Docker Registry
    participant Test as integration_tests Job
    participant Neuron as precompile_neuron_models Job
    
    GHA->>Build: Trigger for hardware backend
    Build->>Build: Construct hardware variables
    Build->>Build: docker build with platform args
    Build->>Docker: Push image with label_extension
    Build->>Test: Output docker_image, docker_devices
    
    alt Neuron Backend
        Build->>Neuron: Trigger if label_extension == '-neuron'
        Neuron->>Docker: Pull docker_image
        Neuron->>Neuron: python export_models.py
        Neuron->>Neuron: Pre-compile models to neuron format
        Neuron->>Test: Signal completion
    end
    
    Test->>Docker: Pull docker_image
    Test->>Test: Set DOCKER_IMAGE, DOCKER_DEVICES, DOCKER_VOLUME
    Test->>Test: pytest integration-tests ${PYTEST_FLAGS} ${EXTRA_PYTEST}
    Test->>Test: Backend-specific test skipping
```

**Test Skip Logic:**
- If `--neuron` not provided, skip tests marked with `@pytest.mark.neuron`
- If `--gaudi` not provided, skip tests marked with `@pytest.mark.gaudi`
- If `--gaudi` provided, skip tests NOT marked with `@pytest.mark.gaudi`
- If `--release` not provided, skip tests marked with `@pytest.mark.release`

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:250-310](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:86-136]()

## Backend Deployment Examples

### CUDA Deployment
```bash
docker run --gpus all --shm-size 1g -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5 \
    --model-id $model
```

### ROCm Deployment
```bash
docker run --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --shm-size 1g \
    -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5-rocm \
    --model-id $model
```

### Intel XPU Deployment
```bash
docker run --privileged --device=/dev/dri --shm-size 1g \
    -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5-intel-xpu \
    --model-id $model --cuda-graphs 0
```

### Intel CPU Deployment
```bash
docker run --shm-size 1g -p 8080:80 -v $volume:/data \
    ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:3.3.5-intel-cpu \
    --model-id $model --cuda-graphs 0
```

**Sources:** [README.md:81-88](), [README.md:124](), [docs/source/quicktour.md:7-28](), [docs/source/installation_amd.md:6-16](), [docs/source/installation_intel.md:6-34]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes TGI's multi-backend architecture, which enables serving large language models across diverse hardware platforms including NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA), AMD GPUs (ROCm), Intel GPUs/CPUs, Intel Gaudi accelerators, AWS Inferentia/Trainium, Google TPUs, and CPU-only deployments. The backend system abstracts platform-specific optimizations and kernels behind a unified interface, allowing the same router and API to work seamlessly across all supported hardware.

For information about the overall system architecture including the router and launcher components, see [System Architecture](#2). For details on specific backend implementations (Neuron, Gaudi, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp), see [Hardware-Specific Backends](#5.2).

## Backend Abstraction Layers

TGI's backend architecture consists of three primary layers that enable hardware portability while maintaining platform-specific optimizations:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Common Layer - Platform Agnostic"
```

### Common Layer Components

The router and launcher binaries are compiled once and work across all backends without modification:

| Component | Language | Purpose | Build Location |
|-----------|----------|---------|----------------|
| `text-generation-router` | Rust | HTTP/gRPC server, request batching, client API | [router/]() |
| `text-generation-launcher` | Rust | Process orchestration, backend selection | [launcher/]() |
| `text-generation-benchmark` | Rust | Performance benchmarking tool | [benchmark/]() |

These components are built during the Docker multi-stage build process using `cargo chef` for dependency caching:

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-43](), [Cargo.toml:1-21](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:1-331]()

### gRPC Protocol Definition

All backends implement the same gRPC interface defined in the protocol buffers:

```mermaid
graph LR
    Proto["proto/v3/generate.proto"]
    Router["Router Client"]
    Server["Backend Server"]
    
    Proto -->|Defines| PrefillRequest["Prefill Request"]
    Proto -->|Defines| DecodeRequest["Decode Request"]
    Proto -->|Defines| CachedBatch["Cached Batch"]
    
    Router -->|"gRPC Prefill"| Server
    Router -->|"gRPC Decode"| Server
    Server -->|"CachedBatch"| Router
```

The protocol is compiled into Python stubs for the backend server during installation:

**Sources:** [server/Makefile:16-30](), [Dockerfile:175-189]()

### CUDA Backend - Default Implementation

The CUDA backend is the most feature-complete and serves as the reference implementation. It includes multiple stages of kernel compilation:

#### PyTorch and CUDA Environment

```mermaid
graph LR
    Base["nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel-ubuntu22.04"]
    PyTorchStage["pytorch-install Stage"]
    
    Base --> PyTorchStage
    PyTorchStage -->|"uv venv"| VEnv["Python 3.11 venv"]
    VEnv -->|"uv pip install"| PyTorch["torch==2.7"]
    PyTorch --> TorchVision["torchvision"]
    
    PyTorchStage -->|"ENV"| TorchArch["TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST<br/>8.0;8.6;9.0+PTX"]
```

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:47-71]()

#### Kernel Build Pipeline

Each kernel type is built in a separate Docker stage to enable parallel compilation and layer caching:

| Kernel Builder Stage | Purpose | Build Command | Output Location |
|---------------------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| `flash-att-builder` | Flash Attention v1 | `make build-flash-attention` | [Dockerfile:83-93]() |
| `flash-att-v2-builder` | Flash Attention v2 CUDA | `make build-flash-attention-v2-cuda` | [Dockerfile:93-100]() |
| `custom-kernels-builder` | GPT-NeoX, BLOOM kernels | `python setup.py build` | [Dockerfile:125-129]() |
| `exllama-kernels-builder` | ExLlama quantization | `python setup.py build` | [Dockerfile:103-107]() |
| `exllamav2-kernels-builder` | ExLlama v2 quantization | `make build-exllamav2` | [Dockerfile:110-115]() |
| `awq-kernels-builder` | AWQ quantization | `make build-awq` | [Dockerfile:118-122]() |
| `mamba-builder` | Mamba state-space models | `make build-all` | [Dockerfile:132-135]() |
| `flashinfer-builder` | FlashInfer attention | `make install-flashinfer` | [Dockerfile:138-141]() |

The compiled kernels are copied into the final image:

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:191-209]()
