This page provides resources and guidance for developers working on Text Generation Inference (TGI). It covers the development environment setup, testing infrastructure, and CI/CD pipeline processes. For deployment information, see [Deployment](#5), and for detailed architecture, see [System Architecture](#2).

## Development Setup

### Prerequisites

To develop TGI, you'll need:

- Rust toolchain (1.85.1+)
- Python 3.11+
- CUDA toolkit (12.8+ recommended for most backends)
- CMake 3.20+
- Ninja build system
- Docker (for containerized testing)

Different hardware backends have additional requirements:

| Backend | Additional Requirements |
|---------|-------------------------|
| CUDA | NVIDIA CUDA 12.8+, cuDNN |
| ROCm | AMD ROCm 5.6+ |
| TensorRT-LLM | TensorRT 10.8+, OpenMPI |
| Neuron | AWS Inferentia SDK |
| Intel | oneDNN, IPEX |

### Repository Structure

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Repository Structure"

        launcher["launcher/"]
        integTests["integration-tests/"]
        benchmark["benchmark/"]
        cicd[".github/workflows/"]

        root --> router
        root --> backends
        root --> launcher
        root --> integTests
        root --> benchmark
        root --> cicd
        root --> dockerfile

        backends --> cuda["cuda/"]
        backends --> rocm["rocm/"]
        backends --> trtllm["trtllm/"]
        backends --> neuron["neuron/"]
        backends --> intel["intel/"]
    end
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/build.yaml:1-247](), [Dockerfile_trtllm:1-160]()

## Testing Framework

TGI employs a comprehensive testing strategy with multiple test types:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "TGI Testing Framework"
        unitTests["Unit Tests"]
        integrationTests["Integration Tests"]
        backendTests["Backend-specific Tests"]
        benchmarks["Benchmarks"]
    end

    unitTests --> rust["Rust Unit Tests\nCore components"]
    unitTests --> cpp["C++ Unit Tests\nHardware backends"]
    integrationTests --> model["Model Loading Tests"]
    integrationTests --> generation["Generation Tests"]
    integrationTests --> api["API Endpoint Tests"]
    backendTests --> cuda["CUDA Tests"]
    backendTests --> trtllm["TensorRT-LLM Tests"]
    backendTests --> neuron["Neuron Tests"]
    benchmarks --> perf["Performance Tests"]
    benchmarks --> throughput["Throughput Tests"]
```

Sources: [integration-tests/conftest.py:14-106](), [backends/trtllm/CMakeLists.txt:72-120]()

### Test Configuration

The test configuration is managed through `pytest` and custom fixtures. The main configuration is defined in `conftest.py`:

- Test markers for specific hardware (e.g., `neuron`)
- Release vs. development testing modes
- Test fixtures for model loading and inference
- Docker container management for isolated testing
- Response comparison utilities with flexible tolerance

### Running Tests Locally

To run integration tests locally:

1. Install test dependencies:
   ```bash
   make install-integration-tests
   ```

2. Run all tests:
   ```bash
   pytest -xvs integration-tests
   ```

3. Run specific hardware tests:
   ```bash
   pytest -xvs integration-tests --neuron  # For Neuron tests
   ```

4. Run tests in release mode (includes additional tests):
   ```bash
   pytest -xvs integration-tests --release
   ```

For backend-specific tests, see the corresponding backend section below.

Sources: [integration-tests/conftest.py:63-105](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:297-307]()

### Test Fixtures and Utilities

TGI provides several pytest fixtures to simplify testing:

| Fixture | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `launcher` | Creates a TGI instance for testing |
| `generate_load` | Generates multiple completions in parallel |
| `generate_multi` | Tests multi-prompt batching |
| `error_log` | Captures error logs during tests |
| `response_snapshot` | Compares responses with snapshots |

The test framework includes custom response comparators that handle numerical variations in token probabilities:

- `ResponseComparator` - Standard comparison with 20% relative tolerance
- `GenerousResponseComparator` - Allows 75% relative tolerance for quantized models
- `IgnoreLogProbResponseComparator` - Ignores log probabilities completely

Sources: [integration-tests/conftest.py:107-362](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:411-423]()

## CI/CD Pipeline

The CI/CD pipeline is implemented using GitHub Actions and is defined in the `.github/workflows` directory.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    pr["Pull Request"]
    main["Main Branch"]
    tag["Release Tag"]

    pr --> build["Build Docker Image\nbuild.yaml"]
    main --> build
    tag --> build

    build --> buildPush["Build and Push\nDocker Image"]
    buildPush --> tests["Run Integration Tests"]
    
    subgraph "Hardware-specific Paths"
        cuda["CUDA"]
        rocm["ROCm"] 
        trtllm["TensorRT-LLM"]
        neuron["Neuron"]
        intel["Intel"]
    end

    buildPush --> cuda
    buildPush --> rocm
    buildPush --> trtllm
    buildPush --> neuron
    buildPush --> intel

    cuda --> tests
    rocm --> tests
    trtllm --> trtllmTests["TensorRT-LLM C++ Tests"]
    trtllm --> tests
    neuron --> precompile["Precompile Neuron Models"]
    precompile --> tests
    intel --> tests

    tests --> publish["Publish Images\n(if main or tag)"]
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/build.yaml:21-307]()

### Build Process

The build process uses Docker with the following steps:

1. Choose the appropriate Dockerfile based on target hardware
2. Set up build environment and variables
3. Build the Docker image with caching for faster rebuilds
4. Push the image to internal registries for testing
5. If successful and on main/tag, push to public registries

For TensorRT-LLM and other complex backends, specialized build processes handle dependencies like TensorRT, OpenMPI, and hardware-specific compilers.

Sources: [.github/workflows/build.yaml:153-232](), [Dockerfile_trtllm:10-91]()

### Testing in CI

After a successful build, the CI runs integration tests against the newly built image:

1. Pull the image from the registry
2. Configure environment variables for testing
3. Run appropriate integration tests with backend-specific flags
4. For specialized hardware (Neuron, TensorRT-LLM), run additional backend-specific tests

The CI uses different hardware runners based on the backend being tested. For example, NVIDIA tests run on GPU-enabled runners, while Neuron tests run on AWS Inferentia instances.

Sources: [.github/workflows/build.yaml:276-307](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:309-327]()

## Hardware Backend Development

TGI supports multiple hardware backends, each with specialized development and testing requirements.

### TensorRT-LLM Backend

The TensorRT-LLM backend requires a more complex build process due to its C++ components and CUDA integration:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    src["TensorRT-LLM Source"]
    trt["TensorRT Libraries"]
    mpi["OpenMPI"]
    cuda["CUDA Toolkit"]

    src --> cmake["CMake Build"]
    trt --> cmake
    mpi --> cmake
    cuda --> cmake

    cmake --> buildBackend["Build Backend Library"]
    buildBackend --> tests["Run Backend Tests"]
    buildBackend --> ffi["Build FFI Layer"]

    ffi --> rustCrate["Rust TensorRT-LLM Crate"]
    rustCrate --> tgiBackend["TGI Backend Integration"]
```

Sources: [backends/trtllm/build.rs:87-175](), [backends/trtllm/CMakeLists.txt:1-120]()

#### Building the TensorRT-LLM Backend

The TensorRT-LLM backend uses a multi-stage build process:

1. Install required dependencies (TensorRT, OpenMPI)
2. Build the C++ components using CMake
3. Build the Rust FFI layer to connect to the backend
4. Link everything together in the final binary

The build uses optimizations like sccache for faster rebuilds in CI environments.

Sources: [backends/trtllm/build.rs:25-250](), [backends/trtllm/scripts/install_tensorrt.sh:1-114]()

#### Testing TensorRT-LLM

Tests for the TensorRT-LLM backend include:

- C++ unit tests for backend functionality
- Integration tests for model loading and inference
- End-to-end generation tests

For development, you can run the C++ tests with:

```bash
cd backends/trtllm
cargo build --features="testing"
/usr/local/tgi/bin/tgi_trtllm_backend_tests
```

Sources: [backends/trtllm/CMakeLists.txt:72-120](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:309-327]()

### Neuron Backend

The AWS Neuron backend has a unique testing approach with pre-compilation of models:

1. Export and compile models for Neuron hardware
2. Run specialized tests that verify Neuron-specific functionality
3. Test performance and accuracy on Inferentia hardware

Sources: [.github/workflows/build.yaml:247-275](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:75-105]()

## Development Best Practices

When contributing to TGI, follow these best practices:

1. **Testing**: Add tests for new features and fix any broken tests
2. **Documentation**: Update documentation to reflect changes
3. **Compatibility**: Ensure backward compatibility or document breaking changes
4. **Performance**: Profile and optimize performance-critical code
5. **Cross-platform**: Test on all supported hardware backends when applicable

### Common Development Tasks

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Build all components | `cargo build --release` |
| Run Rust tests | `cargo test` |
| Run integration tests | `pytest -xvs integration-tests` |
| Format code | `cargo fmt` |
| Lint code | `cargo clippy` |
| Build Docker image | `docker build -t text-generation-inference .` |

## Troubleshooting

Common issues during development:

1. **CUDA version mismatch**: Ensure your CUDA version matches the one specified in the Dockerfile
2. **Missing dependencies**: Install all required libraries for your target backend
3. **Test failures**: Check logs for specific errors, especially hardware-specific issues
4. **Build errors**: Verify that your build environment matches the requirements

For hardware-specific troubleshooting, refer to the backend-specific documentation and test logs.

Sources: [backends/trtllm/scripts/install_tensorrt.sh:25-36](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:107-119]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page documents TGI's build infrastructure, covering both Docker-based production builds and Nix-based development environments. For information about deploying built images, see [Docker Deployment](#6.1). For CI/CD pipeline details, see [CI/CD Pipeline](#7.2).

TGI employs two parallel build systems:
1. **Docker multi-stage builds** - Production deployments across 7 hardware platforms
2. **Nix flake** - Reproducible development environments with hermetic dependency management

## Build System Architecture

## Docker Multi-Stage Build System

### Stage Architecture

TGI's Docker builds use a multi-stage approach to minimize final image size and optimize build caching. The CUDA build (Dockerfile) defines the canonical structure:

| Stage | Base Image | Purpose | Key Outputs |
|-------|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `chef` | `lukemathwalker/cargo-chef:latest-rust-1.85.1` | Dependency analysis | N/A |
| `planner` | `chef` | Generate dependency recipe | `recipe.json` |
| `builder` | `chef` | Compile Rust binaries | `text-generation-router`, `text-generation-launcher`, `text-generation-benchmark` |
| `pytorch-install` | `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel-ubuntu22.04` | Install PyTorch | Python environment with PyTorch 2.7 |
| `kernel-builder` | `pytorch-install` | Base for kernel compilation | CUDA environment |
| `flash-att-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build Flash Attention v1 | `.so` files |
| `flash-att-v2-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build Flash Attention v2 | `.so` files |
| `custom-kernels-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build custom CUDA kernels | Python wheels |
| `exllama-kernels-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build ExLlama kernels | Python wheels |
| `exllamav2-kernels-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build ExLlamaV2 kernels | Python wheels |
| `awq-kernels-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build AWQ quantization kernels | Python wheels |
| `mamba-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build Mamba/SSM kernels | Python wheels |
| `flashinfer-builder` | `kernel-builder` | Build FlashInfer | Python wheels |
| `base` | `nvidia/cuda:12.4.0-base-ubuntu22.04` | Runtime environment | Final dependencies |
| `final` | `base` | Assembly stage | Complete runtime image |

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-251]()

### Cargo Chef Dependency Caching

The Rust build leverages `cargo-chef` for efficient dependency caching:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Planner as planner Stage
    participant Recipe as recipe.json
    participant Builder as builder Stage
    participant Cache as Docker Layer Cache
    
    Planner->>Planner: Copy Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock
    Planner->>Planner: cargo chef prepare
    Planner->>Recipe: Generate recipe.json
    
    Recipe->>Builder: COPY recipe.json
    Builder->>Builder: cargo chef cook --profile release-opt
    Note over Builder,Cache: Dependencies compiled<br/>Cached separately from source
    
    Builder->>Builder: COPY source code
    Builder->>Builder: cargo build --profile release-opt
    Note over Builder: Only recompiles<br/>changed crates
```

The `planner` stage analyzes dependencies at [Dockerfile:7-17]() and generates a recipe that allows `cargo chef cook` to compile dependencies independently at [Dockerfile:30](). This separates dependency compilation from source compilation, maximizing cache hit rates.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:2-43]()

### Kernel Builder Pattern

Each hardware-specific kernel uses a dedicated builder stage that inherits from `kernel-builder`:

```mermaid
graph LR
    KernelBase["kernel-builder<br/>PyTorch + CUDA toolkit<br/>MAX_JOBS=8<br/>TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST"]
    
    FlashAtt1["flash-att-builder<br/>Makefile-flash-att<br/>make build-flash-attention"]
    FlashAtt2["flash-att-v2-builder<br/>Makefile-flash-att-v2<br/>make build-flash-attention-v2-cuda"]
    Custom["custom-kernels-builder<br/>server/custom_kernels/<br/>python setup.py build"]
    Exllama["exllama-kernels-builder<br/>server/exllama_kernels/<br/>python setup.py build"]
    Exllamav2["exllamav2-kernels-builder<br/>Makefile-exllamav2<br/>make build-exllamav2"]
    AWQ["awq-kernels-builder<br/>Makefile-awq<br/>make build-awq"]
    Mamba["mamba-builder<br/>Makefile-selective-scan<br/>make build-all"]
    Flashinfer["flashinfer-builder<br/>Makefile-flashinfer<br/>make install-flashinfer"]
    
    KernelBase --> FlashAtt1
    KernelBase --> FlashAtt2
    KernelBase --> Custom
    KernelBase --> Exllama
    KernelBase --> Exllamav2
    KernelBase --> AWQ
    KernelBase --> Mamba
    KernelBase --> Flashinfer
```

The `kernel-builder` stage at [Dockerfile:73-80]() sets critical environment variables:
- `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.0;8.6;9.0+PTX"` - Target GPU architectures (Ampere, Ada, Hopper)
- `MAX_JOBS=8` - Parallel compilation limit

Each builder compiles its kernel and outputs to a known location, allowing the final stage to copy artifacts via `--from=<stage>` bind mounts.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:73-141]()

### Final Assembly Stage

The `base` and final stages assemble the runtime image:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Base["base Stage<br/>nvidia/cuda:12.4.0-base-ubuntu22.04"]
    
    PyTorchEnv["Copy PyTorch Environment<br/>--from=pytorch-install<br/>/usr/src/.venv"]
    
    ServerInstall["Install Server<br/>uv sync --frozen<br/>--extra gen --extra bnb<br/>--extra accelerate etc."]
    
    KernelCopies["Copy Kernel Artifacts<br/>Flash Attention .so files<br/>Custom kernel wheels<br/>Quantization kernels"]
    
    RustBinaries["Copy Rust Binaries<br/>text-generation-router<br/>text-generation-launcher<br/>text-generation-benchmark"]
    
    Final["Final Runtime Image<br/>Entrypoint: tgi-entrypoint.sh"]
    
    Base --> PyTorchEnv
    PyTorchEnv --> ServerInstall
    ServerInstall --> KernelCopies
    KernelCopies --> RustBinaries
    RustBinaries --> Final
```

Key steps:
1. **Environment setup** [Dockerfile:144-172]() - Base image with minimal runtime dependencies
2. **Python environment** [Dockerfile:168]() - Copy pre-built venv from `pytorch-install`
3. **Server installation** [Dockerfile:179-188]() - Install Python server with `uv sync`
4. **Kernel artifacts** [Dockerfile:191-209]() - Copy compiled `.so` files and wheels from builder stages
5. **Rust binaries** [Dockerfile:227-231]() - Copy optimized binaries from `builder` stage

The final image uses `tgi-entrypoint.sh` as the entrypoint, which launches the text-generation-launcher binary.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:144-251]()

## Platform-Specific Dockerfiles

### CUDA (Dockerfile)

The default Dockerfile targets NVIDIA GPUs with CUDA 12.4:

- **Base image:** `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel-ubuntu22.04` for building, `nvidia/cuda:12.4.0-base-ubuntu22.04` for runtime
- **PyTorch:** 2.7 from official PyTorch index
- **CUDA architectures:** 8.0 (A100), 8.6 (RTX 3090/4090), 9.0 (H100) with PTX for future compatibility
- **Custom kernels:** Flash Attention v1/v2, AWQ, ExLlama, ExLlamaV2, Mamba, FlashInfer, custom fused kernels
- **NCCL:** `nvidia-nccl-cu12==2.25.1` for multi-GPU communication

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-251]()

### ROCm (Dockerfile_amd)

AMD GPU support via ROCm 6.3.1:

```mermaid
graph TB
    RocmBase["rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:6.3.1-complete"]
    
    BuildDeps["Build Custom Dependencies"]
    HipBLASlt["hipBLASLt + hipBLAS-common<br/>build_hipblaslt stage<br/>HIPBLASLT_BRANCH=4d40e36"]
    RCCL["RCCL Communication Library<br/>build_rccl stage<br/>RCCL_BRANCH=648a58d"]
    Triton["Triton Compiler<br/>build_triton stage<br/>TRITON_BRANCH=e5be006"]
    AMDsmi["AMD SMI Python Bindings<br/>build_amdsmi stage"]
    PyTorch["Custom PyTorch Build<br/>build_pytorch stage<br/>PYTORCH_BRANCH=3a585126<br/>PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx90a;gfx942"]
    FlashAttn["Flash Attention for ROCm<br/>FA_BRANCH=b7d29fb"]
    
    ROCmKernels["ROCm-Specific Kernels"]
    VLLMRocm["vllm-builder<br/>make build-vllm-rocm"]
    CustomRocm["custom-kernels-builder"]
    ExllamaRocm["exllama/exllamav2 builders"]
    MarlinKernels["marlin-kernels<br/>v0.3.6"]
    MoeKernels["moe-kernels<br/>v0.8.2"]
    
    RocmBase --> BuildDeps
    BuildDeps --> HipBLASlt
    BuildDeps --> RCCL
    BuildDeps --> Triton
    BuildDeps --> AMDsmi
    BuildDeps --> PyTorch
    PyTorch --> FlashAttn
    
    RocmBase --> ROCmKernels
    ROCmKernels --> VLLMRocm
    ROCmKernels --> CustomRocm
    ROCmKernels --> ExllamaRocm
    ROCmKernels --> MarlinKernels
    ROCmKernels --> MoeKernels
```

ROCm builds compile many dependencies from source:
- **hipBLASLt** [Dockerfile_amd:97-116]() - GPU BLAS library for MI series accelerators
- **RCCL** [Dockerfile_amd:118-125]() - ROCm collective communications
- **Triton** [Dockerfile_amd:127-135]() - Custom fork with ROCm support
- **PyTorch** [Dockerfile_amd:142-166]() - Built with `tools/amd_build/build_amd.py` for ROCm
- **Flash Attention** [Dockerfile_amd:159-163]() - ROCm-optimized implementation using Composable Kernel

Environment variables configure ROCm behavior:
- `ROCM_USE_FLASH_ATTN_V2_TRITON=0` - Prefer CK over Triton for Flash Attention
- `ROCM_USE_CUSTOM_PAGED_ATTN=1` - Use custom paged attention implementation
- `PYTORCH_TUNABLEOP_TUNING_AFTER_WARMUP=0` - Disable auto-tuning
- `ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=1` - Optimize for skinny matrix multiplications

**Sources:** [Dockerfile_amd:1-315]()

### Intel (Dockerfile_intel)

Intel builds support both XPU (discrete GPUs) and CPU platforms via a single Dockerfile with `ARG PLATFORM`:

| Stage | Base Image | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| `xpu` | `intel/oneapi-basekit:2025.1.3-0-devel-ubuntu22.04` | Intel discrete GPU support |
| `cpu` | `ubuntu:22.04` | Intel CPU optimizations |
| `final` | Selected via `${PLATFORM}` | Runtime configuration |

**XPU Build** [Dockerfile_intel:48-127]():
- **Intel Extension for PyTorch (IPEX):** Version 2.8.10 for XPU
- **PyTorch:** 2.8.0 with XPU index
- **oneAPI:** Full basekit with Level Zero runtime
- **Environment:** `CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=sockets`, `TORCH_LLM_ALLREDUCE=1`

**CPU Build** [Dockerfile_intel:130-214]():
- **PyTorch:** 2.7.0 CPU-only variant
- **IPEX:** 2.7.0 CPU variant with oneCCL bindings
- **Optimizations:** gperftools (`libtcmalloc.so` preload), MKL, py-libnuma
- **Environment:** `LD_PRELOAD=/opt/conda/lib/libtcmalloc.so` for efficient memory allocation

Both variants use Miniforge for Python 3.11.10 since Ubuntu 22.04's default Python is too old.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile_intel:1-223]()

### Build Argument Propagation

The CI workflow configures platform-specific builds via Docker build arguments:

```mermaid
graph LR
    CIMatrix["CI Matrix Strategy<br/>7 hardware types"]
    
    BuildArgs["Docker Build Args"]
    GitSHA["GIT_SHA"]
    DockerLabel["DOCKER_LABEL"]
    Platform["PLATFORM<br/>xpu/cpu/none"]
    BuildType["build_type<br/>release/dev"]
    
    TargetStage["Target Stage"]
    Default["default: final"]
    TRTLLMDev["cuda-trtllm dev:<br/>ci-runtime"]
    
    CIMatrix --> BuildArgs
    BuildArgs --> GitSHA
    BuildArgs --> DockerLabel
    BuildArgs --> Platform
    BuildArgs --> BuildType
    
    BuildArgs --> TargetStage
    TargetStage --> Default
    TargetStage --> TRTLLMDev
```

The `build.yaml` workflow at [.github/workflows/build.yaml:55-152]() constructs hardware-specific variables:
- **Dockerfile selection:** Maps hardware type to appropriate Dockerfile
- **Platform argument:** Sets `PLATFORM=xpu` or `PLATFORM=cpu` for Intel builds
- **Runner selection:** Chooses appropriate GitHub Actions runner for the hardware
- **Extra pytest flags:** Hardware-specific test filters

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:55-152]()

## Nix Flake Build System

### Flake Structure

The `flake.nix` defines a reproducible build environment:

```mermaid
graph TB
    FlakeInputs["Flake Inputs"]
    Crate2NixInput["crate2nix<br/>Rust→Nix converter"]
    NixFilter["nix-filter<br/>Source filtering"]
    HFNix["hf-nix<br/>Custom nixpkgs"]
    RustOverlay["rust-overlay<br/>Rust toolchain"]
    
    FlakeOutputs["Flake Outputs"]
    
    Checks["checks.rust<br/>rustfmt, clippy, cargo test"]
    
    DevShells["devShells"]
    Pure["pure (default)<br/>benchmark, launcher,<br/>router, server"]
    Test["test<br/>+ client, pytest, pre-commit"]
    Impure["impure<br/>System libraries"]
    ImpureWithCuda["impureWithCuda<br/>CUDA development"]
    
    Packages["packages"]
    DefaultPackage["default<br/>Combined launcher script"]
    Server["server<br/>Python package"]
    DockerImage["dockerImage<br/>dockerImageStreamed"]
    
    FlakeInputs --> Crate2NixInput
    FlakeInputs --> NixFilter
    FlakeInputs --> HFNix
    FlakeInputs --> RustOverlay
    
    FlakeInputs --> FlakeOutputs
    
    FlakeOutputs --> Checks
    FlakeOutputs --> DevShells
    FlakeOutputs --> Packages
    
    DevShells --> Pure
    DevShells --> Test
    DevShells --> Impure
    DevShells --> ImpureWithCuda
    
    Packages --> DefaultPackage
    Packages --> Server
    Packages --> DockerImage
```

The flake's structure at [flake.nix:16-193]():
- **Inputs:** External flakes for dependencies (crate2nix for Rust, hf-nix for custom packages)
- **CargoNix:** Converts Cargo.toml to Nix expressions using crate2nix [flake.nix:29-33]()
- **Crate overrides:** Custom build configurations at [flake.nix:43]() referencing `nix/crate-overrides.nix`
- **Packages:** Builds router, launcher, benchmark, server, and combines them into a default package
- **Development shells:** Multiple variants for different use cases

**Sources:** [flake.nix:1-194]()

### Crate2Nix Integration

The `crate2nix` tool generates Nix expressions from Cargo metadata:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Cargo as Cargo.toml<br/>Cargo.lock
    participant C2N as crate2nix
    participant CargoNix as cargoNix.workspaceMembers
    participant Overrides as crate-overrides.nix
    participant Binaries as Built Binaries
    
    Cargo->>C2N: cargo chef prepare --recipe-path recipe.json
    C2N->>C2N: Parse dependencies<br/>--all-features
    C2N->>CargoNix: Generate Nix expressions
    
    Note over CargoNix: workspace members:<br/>text-generation-benchmark<br/>text-generation-launcher<br/>text-generation-router-v3
    
    CargoNix->>Overrides: Apply crate-specific patches
    Note over Overrides: aws-lc-rs: fix parsing<br/>text-generation-*: src filtering<br/>protobuf dependencies
    
    Overrides->>Binaries: Build with nativeBuildInputs
    Note over Binaries: clippy, pkg-config,<br/>protobuf, python3
```

The integration at [flake.nix:29-33]() calls `crate2nix.tools.${system}.appliedCargoNix` with:
- **Root:** Repository root directory
- **Arguments:** `--all-features` to include all optional features

Crate overrides at [nix/crate-overrides.nix:1-88]() handle special cases:
- **aws-lc-rs** [nix/crate-overrides.nix:9-19]() - Patches DEP_* parsing for custom build scripts
- **text-generation-router-v3** [nix/crate-overrides.nix:73-86]() - Sets source root to include proto files
- **text-generation-client** [nix/crate-overrides.nix:43-54]() - Adds protobuf to buildInputs

**Sources:** [flake.nix:29-46](), [nix/crate-overrides.nix:1-88]()

### Python Server Package

The server package is built using Poetry-based Python packaging:

```mermaid
graph TB
    ServerNix["nix/server.nix"]
    
    SourceFilter["Source Filtering<br/>nix-filter"]
    ServerPy["server/**/*.py, **/*.pyi"]
    PyProject["server/pyproject.toml"]
    ProtoFiles["proto/v3/*.proto"]
    
    BuildSystem["Build System<br/>poetry-core"]
    
    NativeBuild["Native Build Inputs<br/>mypy-protobuf"]
    
    Dependencies["Python Dependencies"]
    Inference["Inference: torch, transformers,<br/>tokenizers, safetensors"]
    Attention["Attention: flash-attn,<br/>paged-attention, flashinfer"]
    Quantization["Quantization: awq-inference-engine,<br/>exllamav2, quantization, quantization-eetq"]
    Training["Training: peft, compressed-tensors"]
    Kernels["Kernels: mamba-ssm, causal-conv1d,<br/>punica-sgmv, moe, rotary"]
    Telemetry["Telemetry: opentelemetry-*"]
    Structured["Structured Gen: outlines"]
    Server["Server: grpcio-*, prometheus-client"]
    
    PrePatch["prePatch: Generate gRPC<br/>python -m grpc_tools.protoc"]
    
    ServerNix --> SourceFilter
    SourceFilter --> ServerPy
    SourceFilter --> PyProject
    SourceFilter --> ProtoFiles
    
    ServerNix --> BuildSystem
    ServerNix --> NativeBuild
    ServerNix --> Dependencies
    
    Dependencies --> Inference
    Dependencies --> Attention
    Dependencies --> Quantization
    Dependencies --> Training
    Dependencies --> Kernels
    Dependencies --> Telemetry
    Dependencies --> Structured
    Dependencies --> Server
    
    ServerNix --> PrePatch
```

The server package definition at [nix/server.nix:48-130]():
- **Source filtering** [nix/server.nix:54-62]() - Only includes necessary Python files and proto definitions
- **Build system** [nix/server.nix:66]() - Uses `poetry-core` for PEP 517 builds
- **Dependency relaxation** [nix/server.nix:70-78]() - Allows version flexibility for common packages
- **prePatch** [nix/server.nix:123-129]() - Generates gRPC Python code from proto files before build

**Sources:** [nix/server.nix:1-131]()

### Development Shells

The flake provides multiple development environments:

| Shell | Purpose | Key Packages |
|-------|---------|--------------|
| `pure` (default) | Hermetic environment for testing | benchmark, launcher, router, server |
| `test` | Development with test tools | + client, pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, pre-commit |
| `impure` | Allow system libraries | server + system OpenSSL, CUDA libs if available |
| `impureWithCuda` | CUDA development | impure + withCuda flag for flash-attn |
| `impure-flash-attn-v1` | Legacy Flash Attention | flash-attn-v1 instead of default v2 |

The shell definitions at [flake.nix:118-163]():

```nix
pure = mkShell {
  buildInputs = [
    benchmark
    launcher
    router
    server
  ];
};

test = mkShell {
  buildInputs = [
    benchmark launcher router server client
    openssl.dev pkg-config cargo rustfmt clippy
  ] ++ (with python3.pkgs; [
    docker pytest pytest-asyncio syrupy pre-commit ruff
  ]);
};
```

The `impure` shell at [flake.nix:153]() is defined in `nix/impure-shell.nix` and allows access to system libraries like `/usr/lib`, enabling use of system CUDA installations.

**Sources:** [flake.nix:118-163]()

### Docker Image Generation

Nix can build Docker images with reproducible layer composition:

```mermaid
graph TB
    DefaultPkg["default Package<br/>Combined launcher script"]
    
    LauncherWrapped["Wrapped text-generation-launcher<br/>with PYTHONPATH"]
    RouterWrapped["Wrapped text-generation-router<br/>with PYTHONPATH"]
    ServerPkg["server Package<br/>Python dependencies"]
    
    DockerTools["nixpkgs.dockerTools"]
    
    DockerImage["dockerImage<br/>Standard layered image"]
    DockerImageStreamed["dockerImageStreamed<br/>Streamable image"]
    
    DefaultPkg --> LauncherWrapped
    DefaultPkg --> RouterWrapped
    DefaultPkg --> ServerPkg
    
    LauncherWrapped --> DockerTools
    RouterWrapped --> DockerTools
    ServerPkg --> DockerTools
    
    DockerTools --> DockerImage
    DockerTools --> DockerImageStreamed
```

The default package at [flake.nix:168-177]() wraps the launcher with proper PYTHONPATH:

```nix
default = pkgs.writeShellApplication {
  name = "text-generation-inference";
  runtimeInputs = [ server router ];
  text = ''
    ${launcher}/bin/text-generation-launcher "$@"
  '';
};
```

Docker images at [flake.nix:183-190]() use `nixpkgs.dockerTools` to create layered images without rebuilds, as they don't use the overlays that cause rebuilds.

**Sources:** [flake.nix:165-191]()

## CI/CD Build Orchestration

### Matrix Build Strategy

The CI system builds all platform variants in parallel:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Trigger["Trigger Events<br/>push to main,<br/>tags v*,<br/>pull_request"]
    
    CIBuild["ci_build.yaml<br/>Entry workflow"]
    
    Matrix["Matrix Strategy<br/>fail-fast: false"]
    
    Hardware["7 Hardware Types"]
    CUDA["cuda<br/>Dockerfile<br/>aws-g6-12xl-plus-priv-cache"]
    CUDATRTLLM["cuda-trtllm<br/>Dockerfile_trtllm<br/>ubuntu-latest"]
    ROCm["rocm<br/>Dockerfile_amd<br/>ubuntu-latest"]
    IntelXPU["intel-xpu<br/>Dockerfile_intel PLATFORM=xpu<br/>ubuntu-latest"]
    IntelCPU["intel-cpu<br/>Dockerfile_intel PLATFORM=cpu<br/>aws-highmemory-32-plus-priv"]
    Neuron["neuron<br/>Dockerfile.neuron<br/>aws-inf2-8xlarge"]
    Gaudi["gaudi<br/>Dockerfile_gaudi<br/>itac-bm-emr-gaudi3-dell-2gaudi"]
    
    BuildWorkflow["build.yaml<br/>Build orchestration"]
    
    BuildPush["build-and-push Job<br/>aws-highmemory-64-plus-priv"]
    PrecompileNeuron["precompile_neuron_models<br/>Only for neuron"]
    IntegrationTests["integration_tests<br/>pytest with built image"]
    
    Trigger --> CIBuild
    CIBuild --> Matrix
    
    Matrix --> Hardware
    Hardware --> CUDA
    Hardware --> CUDATRTLLM
    Hardware --> ROCm
    Hardware --> IntelXPU
    Hardware --> IntelCPU
    Hardware --> Neuron
    Hardware --> Gaudi
    
    CUDA --> BuildWorkflow
    CUDATRTLLM --> BuildWorkflow
    ROCm --> BuildWorkflow
    IntelXPU --> BuildWorkflow
    IntelCPU --> BuildWorkflow
    Neuron --> BuildWorkflow
    Gaudi --> BuildWorkflow
    
    BuildWorkflow --> BuildPush
    BuildPush --> PrecompileNeuron
    PrecompileNeuron --> IntegrationTests
```

The matrix at [.github/workflows/ci_build.yaml:36-52]() defines:
```yaml
strategy:
  fail-fast: false
  matrix:
    hardware: ["cuda", "cuda-trtllm", "rocm", "intel-xpu", "intel-cpu", "neuron", "gaudi"]
```

Each hardware type triggers the reusable `build.yaml` workflow with platform-specific configuration.

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/ci_build.yaml:1-53](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:21-152]()

### Build and Push Job

The main build job at [.github/workflows/build.yaml:22-235]() performs:

1. **Setup** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:40-54]()
   - Checkout repository
   - Inject slug/short variables for tagging
   - Configure sccache for GitHub Actions cache

2. **Hardware configuration** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:55-152]()
   - Select Dockerfile based on hardware type
   - Configure Docker volume mounts (`/mnt/cache` for CUDA, `/mnt` for ROCm)
   - Set device mappings (`/dev/kfd,/dev/dri` for ROCm, `/dev/neuron0` for Neuron)
   - Choose runner (e.g., `aws-g6-12xl-plus-priv-cache` for CUDA)

3. **Docker Buildx** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:153-157]()
   - Initialize BuildKit daemon with custom configuration

4. **Registry authentication** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:158-177]()
   - Login to internal Hugging Face registry
   - Login to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io)
   - Login to Docker Hub

5. **Build and push** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:212-235]()
   - Extract metadata for tagging
   - Build with BuildKit
   - Push to registries
   - Use S3 for build cache (AWS BuildKit cache bucket)

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:22-249]()

### Cache Strategy

The build system uses multiple cache layers:

| Cache Type | Location | Purpose | Configured At |
|------------|----------|---------|---------------|
| Cargo Chef | Docker layers | Rust dependencies | [Dockerfile:17-30]() |
| Docker BuildKit | AWS S3 | Cross-build artifact sharing | [.github/workflows/build.yaml:234-235]() |
| sccache | GitHub Actions | Rust incremental compilation | [.github/workflows/build.yaml:44-49]() |
| Nix store | `/nix/store` | Hermetic build outputs | [flake.lock:1-998]() |

The S3 cache configuration at [.github/workflows/build.yaml:234-235]():
```yaml
cache-from: type=s3,region=us-east-1,bucket=${{ vars.AWS_S3BUCKET_GITHUB_BUILDX_CACHE }},name=text-generation-inference-cache${{ env.LABEL }},mode=min
cache-to: type=s3,region=us-east-1,bucket=${{ vars.AWS_S3BUCKET_GITHUB_BUILDX_CACHE }},name=text-generation-inference-cache${{ env.LABEL }},mode=min
```

Each hardware variant maintains a separate cache namespace via `${{ env.LABEL }}`.

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:178-235](), [Dockerfile:17-30]()

## Build Artifacts and Distribution

### Binary Artifacts

The build produces three Rust binaries:

| Binary | Path | Purpose | Built From |
|--------|------|---------|-----------|
| `text-generation-launcher` | `/usr/local/bin/` | Process orchestrator | [launcher/]() |
| `text-generation-router` | `/usr/local/bin/` | HTTP/gRPC router | [backends/v3/]() |
| `text-generation-benchmark` | `/usr/local/bin/` | Benchmarking tool | [benchmark/]() |

All three are compiled with `--profile release-opt` at [Dockerfile:43](), which configures optimization level and debug symbols in Cargo.toml.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:227-231]()

### Python Package

The server package is installed as an editable package:

```bash
cd server && \
uv sync --frozen --extra gen --extra bnb --extra accelerate \
  --extra compressed-tensors --extra quantize --extra peft \
  --extra outlines --extra torch --active
```

This installs:
- **Core:** text_generation_server package with gRPC server
- **Extras:** Optional dependencies for different features (quantization, LoRA, etc.)
- **Entry point:** `text-generation-server` command

The installation at [Dockerfile:179-188]() uses `uv` for fast, reliable dependency resolution.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:174-188]()

### Docker Image Tags

Built images are tagged based on the trigger event:

| Event | Tag Pattern | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| Pull request | `sha-<SHORT_SHA>-<LABEL>` | `sha-abc1234-rocm` |
| Main branch | `latest-<LABEL>` | `latest-cuda` |
| Tag | `<VERSION>-<LABEL>` | `v2.0.0-cuda` |
| Tag | `<MAJOR>.<MINOR>-<LABEL>` | `v2.0-cuda` |

The tagging logic at [.github/workflows/build.yaml:187-211]() uses `docker/metadata-action` to generate tags from Git metadata.

Images are pushed to:
- **Internal registry:** `registry.internal.huggingface.tech/api-inference/community/text-generation-inference`
- **GitHub Container Registry:** `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference`
- **Docker Hub:** `docker.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference` (CI builds only)

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:187-211]()

### Kernel Artifacts

Compiled CUDA/ROCm kernels are installed to Python's site-packages:

```
/usr/src/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/
├── flash_attn/                    # Flash Attention v1
├── flash_attn_2_cuda.cpython-*.so # Flash Attention v2
├── custom_kernels/                # Fused CUDA kernels
├── exllama_kernels/               # ExLlama quantization
├── exllamav2/                     # ExLlamaV2 quantization
├── awq/                           # AWQ quantization
├── mamba_ssm/                     # Mamba state-space models
├── causal_conv1d/                 # Causal convolutions
└── flashinfer/                    # FlashInfer attention
```

The copy operations at [Dockerfile:191-209]() use Docker layer caching to avoid recompiling unchanged kernels.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:191-209]()

## Server Makefile Targets

The server Makefile provides convenient build targets:

| Target | Purpose | Key Commands |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `gen-server` | Generate gRPC code | `python -m grpc_tools.protoc` with mypy types |
| `gen-server-raw` | Generate without installing deps | Same as above, no pip install |
| `install-server` | Install Python server | `uv sync` with extras |
| `install-cuda` | Full CUDA installation | install-server + Flash Attention + kernels |
| `install-rocm` | Full ROCm installation | install-server + Flash Attention ROCm + vllm-rocm |
| `unit-tests` | Run Python unit tests | `pytest -s -vv -m "not private" tests` |
| `export-requirements` | Generate requirements.txt | `uv pip compile` for different platforms |

The proto compilation target at [server/Makefile:15-23]():
```makefile
gen-server:
	pip install -U pip uv
	uv pip install -r requirements_gen.txt
	mkdir text_generation_server/pb || true
	python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I../proto/v3 --python_out=text_generation_server/pb \
		--grpc_python_out=text_generation_server/pb --mypy_out=text_generation_server/pb ../proto/v3/generate.proto
	find text_generation_server/pb/ -type f -name "*.py" -print0 -exec sed -i -e 's/^\(import.*pb2\)/from . \1/g' {} \;
	touch text_generation_server/pb/__init__.py
```

The Makefile includes other Makefiles for specific kernel builds: `Makefile-flash-att`, `Makefile-flash-att-v2`, `Makefile-vllm`, etc.

**Sources:** [server/Makefile:1-51]()

## Locked Kernel System

TGI uses a kernel locking system to ensure reproducible builds across environments:

```mermaid
graph LR
    KernelsRepo["huggingface/kernels<br/>Pre-built wheels on Hub"]
    
    KernelsCLI["kernels CLI tool<br/>download/upload commands"]
    
    LocalDev["Local Development<br/>importlib.import_module"]
    FallbackHub["Fallback to Hub<br/>kernels.load_kernel"]
    
    ServerUtils["server/utils/kernels.py<br/>load_kernel() function"]
    
    KernelsRepo --> KernelsCLI
    KernelsCLI --> LocalDev
    LocalDev --> ServerUtils
    
    KernelsCLI --> FallbackHub
    FallbackHub --> ServerUtils
```

The kernel loading system at [server/text_generation_server/utils/kernels.py:9-19]():
```python
def load_kernel(*, module: str, repo_id: str):
    """
    Load a kernel. First try to load it as the given module (e.g. for
    local development), falling back to a locked Hub kernel.
    """
    try:
        m = importlib.import_module(module)
        log_once(logger.info, f"Using local module for `{module}`")
        return m
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        return hf_load_kernel(repo_id=repo_id)
```

This allows:
1. **Local development:** Use locally built kernels during development
2. **Production:** Download pre-built, version-locked kernels from Hub
3. **CI/CD:** `kernels download .` at [Dockerfile:182]() downloads all required kernels

**Sources:** [server/text_generation_server/utils/kernels.py:1-23](), [Dockerfile:178-182]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) infrastructure for Text Generation Inference. The pipeline automates building, testing, and publishing Docker images for seven distinct hardware platforms, runs integration tests, and maintains documentation consistency. For information about local build systems using Nix or Cargo, see [Build Systems](#7.1). For information about integration test structure and fixtures, see [Testing Infrastructure](#7.3).

## Workflow Architecture

The CI/CD system consists of four primary GitHub Actions workflows that orchestrate different aspects of the build and test cycle:

### Primary Workflows

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "GitHub Actions Workflows"
        CIBUILD["ci_build.yaml<br/>Workflow Orchestrator"]
        BUILD["build.yaml<br/>Build & Push Job"]
        TESTS["tests.yaml<br/>Server Unit Tests"]
        AUTODOCS["autodocs.yaml<br/>Documentation Checks"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Triggers"
        PUSH["Push to main<br/>or tags"]
        PR["Pull Request"]
        MANUAL["Manual Dispatch"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Outputs"
        IMAGES["Docker Images<br/>7 Platforms"]
        TESTRESULTS["Test Results"]
        DOCS["Updated Docs"]
    end
    
    PUSH --> CIBUILD
    PR --> CIBUILD
    PR --> TESTS
    PR --> AUTODOCS
    MANUAL --> CIBUILD
    
    CIBUILD --> BUILD
    BUILD --> IMAGES
    BUILD --> TESTRESULTS
    TESTS --> TESTRESULTS
    AUTODOCS --> DOCS
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/ci_build.yaml:1-52](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:1-331](), [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:1-68](), [.github/workflows/autodocs.yaml:1-46]()

## Matrix Build Strategy

The `ci_build.yaml` workflow implements a matrix strategy to build TGI for seven hardware platforms in parallel:

| Hardware Platform | Dockerfile | Label Extension | Runner | Device Requests |
|------------------|------------|-----------------|--------|-----------------|
| cuda | `Dockerfile` | `` | aws-g6-12xl-plus-priv-cache | GPU (CUDA) |
| cuda-trtllm | `Dockerfile_trtllm` | `-trtllm` | ubuntu-latest | GPU (CUDA) |
| rocm | `Dockerfile_amd` | `-rocm` | ubuntu-latest | /dev/kfd, /dev/dri |
| intel-xpu | `Dockerfile_intel` | `-intel-xpu` | ubuntu-latest | XPU |
| intel-cpu | `Dockerfile_intel` | `-intel-cpu` | aws-highmemory-32-plus-priv | none |
| neuron | `Dockerfile.neuron` | `-neuron` | aws-inf2-8xlarge | /dev/neuron0 |
| gaudi | `Dockerfile_gaudi` | `-gaudi` | itac-bm-emr-gaudi3-dell-2gaudi | Gaudi |

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "ci_build.yaml Matrix"
        MATRIX["Matrix Strategy<br/>fail-fast: false"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parallel Build Jobs"
        CUDA["Build: cuda"]
        TRTLLM["Build: cuda-trtllm"]
        ROCM["Build: rocm"]
        IXPU["Build: intel-xpu"]
        ICPU["Build: intel-cpu"]
        NEURON["Build: neuron"]
        GAUDI["Build: gaudi"]
    end

    MATRIX --> IXPU

    ROCM --> ROCMIMG["ghcr.io/...-rocm"]
    IXPU --> IXPUIMG["ghcr.io/...-intel-xpu"]
    ICPU --> ICPUIMG["ghcr.io/...-intel-cpu"]
    NEURON --> NEURONIMG["ghcr.io/...-neuron"]
    GAUDI --> GAUDIIMG["ghcr.io/...-gaudi"]
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/ci_build.yaml:36-52](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:56-136]()

## Build and Push Workflow

The `build.yaml` workflow is invoked by `ci_build.yaml` for each hardware platform and performs the complete build, test, and publish cycle.

### Workflow Job Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CI as ci_build.yaml
    participant BP as build-and-push job
    participant Docker as Docker Buildx
    participant Registry as Container Registry
    participant Pre as precompile_neuron_models
    participant IT as integration_tests
    participant TRT as backend_trtllm_cxx_tests
    
    CI->>BP: Invoke with hardware parameter
    BP->>BP: Construct hardware variables
    BP->>BP: Extract TensorRT-LLM version
    BP->>BP: Setup Docker Buildx
    BP->>BP: Login to registries
    BP->>BP: Configure AWS credentials
    BP->>BP: Extract metadata (tags, labels)
    BP->>Docker: Build multi-stage image
    Docker->>Docker: cargo-chef (Rust dependencies)
    Docker->>Docker: Build Rust binaries
    Docker->>Docker: Build CUDA/ROCm kernels
    Docker->>Docker: Install Python dependencies
    Docker->>Docker: Assemble final image
    Docker->>Registry: Push image
    Registry-->>BP: Image reference
    BP->>BP: Output docker_image, runs_on, etc.
    
    alt Hardware is neuron
        BP->>Pre: Trigger precompilation
        Pre->>Pre: Export neuron models
        Pre-->>IT: Ready
    end
    
    BP->>IT: Trigger integration tests
    IT->>IT: Pull docker image
    IT->>IT: Run pytest suite
    IT-->>BP: Test results
    
    alt Hardware is cuda-trtllm
        BP->>TRT: Trigger C++ tests
        TRT->>TRT: Run tgi_trtllm_backend_tests
        TRT-->>BP: Test results
    end
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:21-331]()

### Key Build Steps

The `build-and-push` job performs these operations:

1. **Checkout and Setup** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:40-50]()
   - Checkout repository code
   - Inject slug/short variables for image naming
   - Configure sccache for Rust build caching

2. **Hardware Configuration** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:56-152]()
   - Constructs platform-specific variables based on `inputs.hardware`
   - Sets `DOCKERFILE`, `LABEL_EXTENSION`, `DOCKER_DEVICES`, `RUNS_ON`, `PLATFORM`, `TARGET`

3. **Container Registry Authentication** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:158-177]()
   - Authenticates to `registry.internal.huggingface.tech` (internal)
   - Authenticates to `ghcr.io` (GitHub Container Registry)
   - Authenticates to `docker.io` (Docker Hub)

4. **Image Metadata Generation** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:187-211]()
   - For PRs: tags as `sha-<commit>-<label_extension>`
   - For releases: tags as semver patterns `{{version}}`, `{{major}}.{{minor}}`, `latest`

5. **Docker Build and Push** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:212-235]()
   - Uses `docker/build-push-action@v4`
   - Employs S3-based build cache for layer reuse
   - Passes build args: `GIT_SHA`, `DOCKER_LABEL`, `PLATFORM`, `build_type`
   - Enables sccache for Rust compilation caching

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:21-235]()

## Docker Multi-Stage Build Process

### CUDA Backend Build Stages

The primary `Dockerfile` for CUDA backend uses a sophisticated multi-stage strategy to minimize final image size while building custom kernels:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Stage 1: Rust Build"
        CHEF["chef<br/>lukemathwalker/cargo-chef"]
        PLANNER["planner<br/>Generate recipe.json"]
        BUILDER["builder<br/>Compile Rust binaries"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 2: Python Environment"
        PYTORCH["pytorch-install<br/>nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel<br/>Install PyTorch 2.7"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 3: Kernel Builders"
        FLASH1["flash-att-builder<br/>Flash Attention v1"]
        FLASH2["flash-att-v2-builder<br/>Flash Attention v2"]
        EXLLAMA["exllama-kernels-builder"]
        EXLLAMAV2["exllamav2-kernels-builder"]
        AWQ["awq-kernels-builder"]
        CUSTOM["custom-kernels-builder"]
        MAMBA["mamba-builder"]
        FLASHINFER["flashinfer-builder"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Stage 4: Final Image"
        BASE["base<br/>nvidia/cuda:12.4.0-base"]
        FINAL["Final Runtime Image"]
    end
    
    CHEF --> PLANNER
    PLANNER --> BUILDER
    
    PYTORCH --> FLASH1
    PYTORCH --> FLASH2
    PYTORCH --> EXLLAMA
    PYTORCH --> EXLLAMAV2
    PYTORCH --> AWQ
    PYTORCH --> CUSTOM
    PYTORCH --> MAMBA
    PYTORCH --> FLASHINFER
    
    BUILDER --> FINAL
    PYTORCH --> FINAL
    FLASH1 --> FINAL
    FLASH2 --> FINAL
    EXLLAMA --> FINAL
    EXLLAMAV2 --> FINAL
    AWQ --> FINAL
    CUSTOM --> FINAL
    MAMBA --> FINAL
    FLASHINFER --> FINAL
    BASE --> FINAL
```

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-251]()

### Detailed Stage Breakdown

#### Rust Builder Stages [Dockerfile:1-43]()

1. **Chef Stage**: Base image with `cargo-chef` for Rust dependency caching
2. **Planner Stage**: Analyzes `Cargo.toml` and generates `recipe.json`
3. **Builder Stage**: 
   - Installs protobuf compiler [Dockerfile:23-27]()
   - Cooks dependencies from recipe (cached layer) [Dockerfile:30]()
   - Compiles all Rust binaries (router, launcher, benchmark) [Dockerfile:43]()

#### Python and Kernel Stages [Dockerfile:45-209]()

1. **pytorch-install**: Installs PyTorch 2.7 with CUDA 12.4 [Dockerfile:47-70]()
2. **kernel-builder**: Base for building custom kernels [Dockerfile:73-81]()
3. **flash-att-builder**: Builds Flash Attention v1 [Dockerfile:83-90]()
4. **flash-att-v2-builder**: Builds Flash Attention v2 CUDA kernels [Dockerfile:92-100]()
5. **exllama-kernels-builder**: ExLlama quantization kernels [Dockerfile:103-107]()
6. **exllamav2-kernels-builder**: ExLlama v2 kernels [Dockerfile:110-115]()
7. **awq-kernels-builder**: AWQ quantization kernels [Dockerfile:118-122]()
8. **custom-kernels-builder**: Custom CUDA kernels (GPT-NeoX, BLOOM) [Dockerfile:125-129]()
9. **mamba-builder**: Mamba SSM kernels [Dockerfile:132-135]()
10. **flashinfer-builder**: FlashInfer paged attention kernels [Dockerfile:138-141]()

#### Final Assembly Stage [Dockerfile:144-251]()

The base image copies artifacts from all kernel builders:
- Installs Python server with dependencies [Dockerfile:174-188]()
- Copies compiled Rust binaries [Dockerfile:227-231]()
- Copies kernel libraries from all builder stages [Dockerfile:191-209]()
- Sets environment variables [Dockerfile:147-149](), [Dockerfile:216](), [Dockerfile:248]()

**Sources:** [Dockerfile:1-251]()

## Platform-Specific Build Variations

### Intel Backend [Dockerfile_intel:1-223]()

The Intel backend supports both XPU (GPU) and CPU platforms using a shared base image with platform-specific final stages:

```mermaid
graph TB
    CHEF["chef<br/>cargo-chef"]
    PLANNER["planner"]
    BUILDER["builder<br/>Compile Rust"]
    
    XPU_BASE["xpu stage<br/>intel/oneapi-basekit:2025.1.3"]
    CPU_BASE["cpu stage<br/>ubuntu:22.04"]
    
    CHEF --> PLANNER
    PLANNER --> BUILDER
    
    XPU_BASE --> XPU_FINAL["XPU final<br/>Install PyTorch XPU<br/>Intel Extension"]
    CPU_BASE --> CPU_FINAL["CPU final<br/>Install PyTorch CPU<br/>OneCCL bindings"]
    
    BUILDER --> XPU_FINAL
    BUILDER --> CPU_FINAL
    
    FINAL["Final stage selection<br/>FROM ${PLATFORM}"]
    
    XPU_FINAL --> FINAL
    CPU_FINAL --> FINAL
```

Key differences:
- XPU uses Intel OneAPI base with IPEX 2.8.10+xpu [Dockerfile_intel:48-127]()
- CPU uses Intel MKL and OneCCL for distributed inference [Dockerfile_intel:130-215]()
- Both use `uv` for Python dependency management [Dockerfile_intel:108-112](), [Dockerfile_intel:204-207]()
- Platform selection via `ARG PLATFORM` and `FROM ${PLATFORM}` [Dockerfile_intel:216]()

**Sources:** [Dockerfile_intel:1-223]()

### AMD ROCm Backend [Dockerfile_amd:1-315]()

The AMD backend has the most complex build process due to building PyTorch from source:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Dependency Builds"
        BASE["base<br/>rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:6.3.1"]
        HIPBLASLT["build_hipblaslt<br/>Custom hipBLASLt"]
        RCCL["build_rccl<br/>Custom RCCL"]
        TRITON["build_triton<br/>Custom Triton"]
        AMDSMI["build_amdsmi<br/>AMD SMI"]
        PYTORCH["build_pytorch<br/>PyTorch + Vision + Flash Attn"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Kernel Builds"
        VLLM["vllm-builder"]
        CUSTOM["custom-kernels-builder"]
        EXLLAMA["exllama-kernels-builder"]
        EXLLAMAV2["exllamav2-kernels-builder"]
        MARLIN["marlin-kernels"]
        MOE["moe-kernels"]
    end
    
    BASE --> HIPBLASLT
    BASE --> RCCL
    BASE --> TRITON
    BASE --> AMDSMI
    BASE --> PYTORCH
    
    BASE --> VLLM
    BASE --> CUSTOM
    BASE --> EXLLAMA
    BASE --> EXLLAMAV2
    BASE --> MARLIN
    BASE --> MOE
    
    FINAL["final<br/>Assembly"]
    
    HIPBLASLT --> FINAL
    RCCL --> FINAL
    TRITON --> FINAL
    AMDSMI --> FINAL
    PYTORCH --> FINAL
    VLLM --> FINAL
    CUSTOM --> FINAL
    EXLLAMA --> FINAL
    EXLLAMAV2 --> FINAL
    MARLIN --> FINAL
    MOE --> FINAL
```

Notable build features:
- Builds hipBLASLt from source [Dockerfile_amd:97-116]()
- Builds custom RCCL [Dockerfile_amd:118-125]()
- Builds Triton from ROCm fork [Dockerfile_amd:127-135]()
- Builds PyTorch from source with AMD optimizations [Dockerfile_amd:142-166]()
- Uses `--mount=type=bind` to avoid copying large build artifacts [Dockerfile_amd:169-274]()

**Sources:** [Dockerfile_amd:1-315]()

## Integration Testing Pipeline

After images are built, the workflow executes platform-specific integration tests:

```mermaid
graph TB
    BUILD["build-and-push job<br/>Outputs: docker_image, runs_on"]
    
    NEURON_CHECK{"Hardware == neuron?"}
    PRECOMPILE["precompile_neuron_models<br/>Export models for Neuron"]
    
    SKIP_CHECK{"runs_on == ubuntu-latest?"}
    INTEGRATION["integration_tests job<br/>Run pytest suite"]
    
    TRTLLM_CHECK{"Hardware == cuda-trtllm?"}
    CPP_TESTS["backend_trtllm_cxx_tests<br/>Run C++ tests"]
    
    BUILD --> NEURON_CHECK
    NEURON_CHECK -->|Yes| PRECOMPILE
    NEURON_CHECK -->|No| SKIP_CHECK
    PRECOMPILE --> SKIP_CHECK
    
    SKIP_CHECK -->|No| INTEGRATION
    SKIP_CHECK -->|Yes| END["Skip tests<br/>No runner available"]
    
    BUILD --> TRTLLM_CHECK
    TRTLLM_CHECK -->|Yes| CPP_TESTS
    TRTLLM_CHECK -->|No| END2["Complete"]
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:250-331]()

### Integration Test Execution [.github/workflows/build.yaml:279-310]()

The `integration_tests` job:

1. **Setup**: Checkout code, install Python 3.11, install test dependencies [.github/workflows/build.yaml:290-300]()
2. **Environment Variables**:
   - `DOCKER_IMAGE`: Image reference from build job
   - `DOCKER_VOLUME`: Volume mount path (default: `/data`)
   - `DOCKER_DEVICES`: Hardware device paths
   - `PYTEST_FLAGS`: `--release` for main/tag builds
   - `HF_TOKEN`: Hugging Face API token for private models
3. **Execution**: Pulls image and runs pytest [.github/workflows/build.yaml:302-310]()

```bash
pytest -s -vv integration-tests ${PYTEST_FLAGS} ${EXTRA_PYTEST}
```

### Integration Test Infrastructure

The test infrastructure in `integration-tests/conftest.py` provides fixtures for both local and Docker-based testing:

#### Launcher Fixture [integration-tests/conftest.py:462-730]()

The `launcher` fixture returns either `local_launcher` or `docker_launcher` based on the `DOCKER_IMAGE` environment variable:

```python
if DOCKER_IMAGE is not None:
    return docker_launcher
return local_launcher
```

**Local Launcher** [integration-tests/conftest.py:465-563]():
- Spawns `text-generation-launcher` as subprocess
- Configures with random ports to avoid conflicts
- Captures stdout/stderr to temporary file
- Returns `ProcessLauncherHandle`

**Docker Launcher** [integration-tests/conftest.py:568-726]():
- Pulls specified `DOCKER_IMAGE`
- Configures device requests based on `DOCKER_DEVICES`
- Mounts `DOCKER_VOLUME` for model cache
- Returns `ContainerLauncherHandle`

#### Fixture Configuration [integration-tests/conftest.py:62-66]()

```python
DOCKER_IMAGE = os.getenv("DOCKER_IMAGE", None)
HF_TOKEN = os.getenv("HF_TOKEN", None)
DOCKER_VOLUME = os.getenv("DOCKER_VOLUME", "/data")
DOCKER_DEVICES = os.getenv("DOCKER_DEVICES")
```

**Sources:** [integration-tests/conftest.py:1-812](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:279-310]()

### Neuron Model Precompilation [.github/workflows/build.yaml:250-278]()

For AWS Neuron backend, models must be compiled before testing:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as precompile_neuron_models
    participant D as Docker
    participant S as export_models.py
    participant Hub as Hugging Face Hub
    
    W->>D: Pull docker image
    W->>S: Execute export script
    S->>Hub: Download model weights
    S->>S: Compile for Neuron
    S->>Hub: Upload compiled artifacts
    S-->>W: Compilation complete
    W->>W: Set fixture available flag
```

The job runs on the same Neuron hardware as tests [.github/workflows/build.yaml:256-257]() and exports models using `integration-tests/fixtures/neuron/export_models.py` [.github/workflows/build.yaml:272-278]().

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:250-278]()

### TensorRT-LLM C++ Tests [.github/workflows/build.yaml:312-331]()

For the TensorRT-LLM backend, additional C++ unit tests run inside the container:

```yaml
runs-on:
  group: aws-g6-12xl-plus-priv-cache
container:
  image: ${{ needs.build-and-push.outputs.docker_image }}
  options: --gpus all --shm-size=8g
steps:
  - name: Run C++/CUDA tests
    run: /usr/local/tgi/bin/tgi_trtllm_backend_tests
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:312-331]()

## Server Unit Tests

The `tests.yaml` workflow runs Python unit tests on every PR that modifies server code:

```mermaid

        KERNEL["Download kernels<br/>kernels download server"]
        PYTEST["Run pytest<br/>server/tests"]
        PRECOMMIT["Pre-commit checks<br/>Format, lint"]

    end

    SETUP --> INSTALL
    INSTALL --> KERNEL
    KERNEL --> PYTEST
    PYTEST --> PRECOMMIT
    PRECOMMIT --> RUST
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:1-68]()

### Test Execution Steps

1. **Path Filtering** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:5-13]()
   - Only runs when relevant files change: `.github/workflows/tests.yaml`, `server/**`, `proto/**`, `router/**`, `launcher/**`, `backends/**`, `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`

2. **Environment Setup** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:23-46]()
   - Uses AWS high-memory runner: `aws-highmemory-32-plus-priv`
   - Installs Python 3.11, Rust 1.85, and protoc
   - Cleans unused files to free disk space

3. **Python Installation** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:39-50]()
   ```bash
   make install-cpu
   kernels download server
   ```

4. **Test Execution** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:51-56]()
   ```bash
   pytest -s -vv server/tests
   ```

5. **Code Quality Checks** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:57-61]()
   ```bash
   pre-commit run --all-files
   ```

6. **Rust Tests** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:62-67]()
   ```bash
   cargo test
   cargo test --features google
   ```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:1-68]()

## Documentation Automation

The `autodocs.yaml` workflow ensures documentation stays synchronized with code changes:

```mermaid
graph TB
    PR["Pull Request Trigger"]
    
    subgraph "autodocs.yaml"
        CHECKOUT["Checkout code"]
        RUST["Install Rust toolchain"]
        PROTOC["Install protobuf compiler"]
        LAUNCHER["cargo install launcher"]
        ROUTER["cargo install router<br/>backends/v3"]
        NODE["Install Node.js 22"]
        PYTHON["Install Python 3.x"]
        REDOCLY["Install @redocly/cli"]
        CHECK["python update_doc.py --check"]
    end
    
    PR --> CHECKOUT
    CHECKOUT --> RUST
    RUST --> PROTOC
    PROTOC --> LAUNCHER
    LAUNCHER --> ROUTER
    ROUTER --> NODE
    NODE --> PYTHON
    PYTHON --> REDOCLY
    REDOCLY --> CHECK
    
    CHECK --> SUCCESS["Documentation matches"]
    CHECK --> FAIL["Diff found<br/>CI fails"]
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/autodocs.yaml:1-46]()

### Documentation Update Script

The `update_doc.py` script automates three documentation updates:

#### 1. CLI Documentation [update_doc.py:32-83]()

Generates `docs/source/reference/launcher.md` by:
- Executing `text-generation-launcher --help`
- Parsing the help output
- Formatting as structured markdown with code blocks
- In `--check` mode, fails if documentation differs

#### 2. Supported Models List [update_doc.py:85-124]()

Generates `docs/source/supported_models.md` by:
- Parsing `server/text_generation_server/models/__init__.py`
- Extracting the `ModelType` enum using AST
- Building a markdown list of supported models
- Annotating multimodal models

#### 3. OpenAPI Schema [update_doc.py:126-189]()

Generates `docs/openapi.json` by:
- Executing `text-generation-router print-schema`
- Parsing the JSON output
- Validating with `redocly lint`
- Checking for schema differences

```python
def get_openapi_schema():
    output = subprocess.check_output(["text-generation-router", "print-schema"])
    return json.loads(output)
```

**Sources:** [update_doc.py:1-204]()

## Build Caching Strategy

The CI/CD pipeline employs multiple caching strategies to accelerate builds:

### S3-Based Docker Layer Cache [.github/workflows/build.yaml:234-235]()

```yaml
cache-from: type=s3,region=us-east-1,bucket=...,name=text-generation-inference-cache${{ env.LABEL }},mode=max
cache-to: type=s3,region=us-east-1,bucket=...,name=text-generation-inference-cache${{ env.LABEL }},mode=max
```

Each hardware platform gets its own cache namespace via `LABEL` to avoid conflicts.

### Rust sccache [.github/workflows/build.yaml:44-49](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:227]()

Rust compilation uses GitHub Actions cache via sccache:

```yaml
- name: Inject required variables for sccache
  with:
    script: |
      core.exportVariable('ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL', ...);
      core.exportVariable('ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN', ...);

# Later in docker build:
build-args: |
  sccache_gha_enabled=on
secrets: |
  actions_results_url=${{ env.ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL }}
  actions_runtime_token=${{ env.ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN }}
```

### Cargo Chef [Dockerfile:1-43]()

The Rust builder stages use `cargo-chef` for incremental dependency compilation:

1. **Planner stage**: Generates `recipe.json` from `Cargo.toml` [Dockerfile:7-17]()
2. **Builder stage**: Cooks dependencies (cached) before copying source [Dockerfile:29-30]()

This ensures dependencies are only rebuilt when `Cargo.lock` changes, not on every code modification.

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:44-49](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:227](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:234-235](), [Dockerfile:1-43]()

## Image Tagging and Publication

### Tag Strategies

The workflow generates different tags based on the trigger event:

#### Pull Request Builds [.github/workflows/build.yaml:187-195]()

```yaml
images: |
  docker.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference-ci
tags: |
  type=raw,value=sha-${{ env.GITHUB_SHA_SHORT }}${{ env.LABEL_EXTENSION }}
```

Example: `docker.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference-ci:sha-abc1234-rocm`

#### Release Builds [.github/workflows/build.yaml:197-211]()

```yaml
images: |
  registry.internal.huggingface.tech/api-inference/community/text-generation-inference
  ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference
tags: |
  type=semver,pattern={{version}}${{ env.LABEL_EXTENSION }}
  type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}${{ env.LABEL_EXTENSION }}
  type=raw,value=latest${{ env.LABEL_EXTENSION }},enable=${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
  type=raw,value=sha-${{ env.GITHUB_SHA_SHORT }}${{ env.LABEL_EXTENSION }}
```

For a `v2.1.0` release with `cuda` backend, this generates:
- `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:2.1.0`
- `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:2.1`
- `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:latest`
- `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:sha-abc1234`

### Registry Authentication [.github/workflows/build.yaml:158-177]()

The workflow authenticates to three registries:

1. **Internal Hugging Face Registry** (non-PR only)
   - `registry.internal.huggingface.tech`
   - Used for production deployments

2. **GitHub Container Registry**
   - `ghcr.io`
   - Public releases

3. **Docker Hub**
   - `docker.io`
   - CI images for pull requests

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:158-211](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:236-249]()

## Concurrency Control

The workflows implement concurrency controls to prevent resource conflicts:

### Build Workflow Concurrency [.github/workflows/build.yaml:30-32]()

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-build-and-push-image-${{ inputs.hardware }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

This ensures that for a given hardware platform and PR, only one build runs at a time. New pushes cancel in-progress builds.

### Integration Test Concurrency [.github/workflows/build.yaml:251-253](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:280-282]()

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.job }}-${{ needs.build-and-push.outputs.label_extension }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Tests are grouped by job type and hardware platform, allowing parallel execution across different platforms while preventing duplicate tests for the same platform.

### Tests Workflow Concurrency [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:15-17]()

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:30-32](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:251-253](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:280-282](), [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:15-17]()

## Server Build Targets

The `server/Makefile` defines build targets used by both CI and local development:

### Key Makefile Targets

| Target | Purpose | Files |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `gen-server` | Compile protobuf definitions + install deps | [server/Makefile:15-23]() |
| `gen-server-raw` | Compile protobuf only (no deps) | [server/Makefile:25-30]() |
| `install-server` | Generate protos + sync Python packages | [server/Makefile:32-33]() |
| `install-cuda` | Full CUDA installation with kernels | [server/Makefile:39-42]() |
| `install-rocm` | Full ROCm installation | [server/Makefile:44]() |
| `unit-tests` | Run Python unit tests | [server/Makefile:9-13]() |
| `export-requirements` | Generate requirements*.txt files | [server/Makefile:46-50]() |

### Protobuf Generation [server/Makefile:25-30]()

The `gen-server-raw` target used in Docker builds:

```makefile
gen-server-raw:
	mkdir text_generation_server/pb || true
	python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I../proto/v3 --python_out=text_generation_server/pb \
		--grpc_python_out=text_generation_server/pb --mypy_out=text_generation_server/pb ../proto/v3/generate.proto
	find text_generation_server/pb/ -type f -name "*.py" -print0 -exec sed -i -e 's/^\(import.*pb2\)/from . \1/g' {} \;
	touch text_generation_server/pb/__init__.py
```

This generates Python gRPC stubs from `proto/v3/generate.proto` and fixes import statements.

**Sources:** [server/Makefile:1-51]()

## Environment Variables

The CI/CD system uses numerous environment variables for configuration:

### Build-Time Variables [.github/workflows/build.yaml:56-152]()

| Variable | Purpose | Set By |
|----------|---------|--------|
| `DOCKERFILE` | Dockerfile path for hardware | Hardware switch case |
| `LABEL_EXTENSION` | Image tag suffix (e.g., `-rocm`) | Hardware switch case |
| `DOCKER_DEVICES` | Device paths for containers | Hardware switch case |
| `RUNS_ON` | GitHub runner label | Hardware switch case |
| `PLATFORM` | Backend platform (xpu/cpu) | Hardware switch case |
| `TARGET` | Docker build target | Hardware switch case |
| `BUILD_TYPE` | `release` or `dev` | Tag detection |
| `EXTRA_PYTEST` | Platform-specific pytest filters | Hardware switch case |
| `GIT_SHA` | Git commit SHA | GitHub context |
| `DOCKER_LABEL` | Image label with SHA | Constructed |

### Test-Time Variables [integration-tests/conftest.py:62-66]()

| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `DOCKER_IMAGE` | Test image reference | None (use local) |
| `HF_TOKEN` | Hugging Face API token | None |
| `DOCKER_VOLUME` | Model cache mount | `/data` |
| `DOCKER_DEVICES` | Hardware devices | None |

### Runtime Variables [integration-tests/conftest.py:638-648]()

The launcher fixture sets:

```python
env = {
    "LOG_LEVEL": "info,text_generation_router=debug",
    "PREFILL_CHUNKING": "1",
}
if not use_flash_attention:
    env["USE_FLASH_ATTENTION"] = "false"
if attention is not None:
    env["ATTENTION"] = attention
if HF_TOKEN is not None:
    env["HF_TOKEN"] = HF_TOKEN
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:56-152](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:62-66](), [integration-tests/conftest.py:638-648]()

## Workflow Outputs and Job Dependencies

The `build-and-push` job outputs are consumed by downstream jobs:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "build-and-push Outputs"
        IMG["docker_image<br/>Image reference"]
        VOL["docker_volume<br/>Mount path"]
        DEV["docker_devices<br/>Device paths"]
        RUN["runs_on<br/>Runner label"]
        EXT["label_extension<br/>Image suffix"]
        PYTEST["extra_pytest<br/>Test filters"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Consumers"
        PRENEU["precompile_neuron_models"]
        INTEG["integration_tests"]
        TRTLLM["backend_trtllm_cxx_tests"]
    end
    
    IMG --> PRENEU
    IMG --> INTEG
    IMG --> TRTLLM
    
    VOL --> INTEG
    DEV --> INTEG
    RUN --> PRENEU
    RUN --> INTEG
    EXT --> PRENEU
    PYTEST --> INTEG
```

### Output Determination [.github/workflows/build.yaml:236-249]()

```bash
if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
  echo "docker_image=docker.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference-ci:sha-${{ env.GITHUB_SHA_SHORT}}${{ env.LABEL_EXTENSION }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  echo "docker_image=ghcr.io/huggingface/text-generation-inference:sha-${{ env.GITHUB_SHA_SHORT}}${{ env.LABEL_EXTENSION }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi
```

### Job Dependencies [.github/workflows/build.yaml:254-255](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:283](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:313]()

```yaml
precompile_neuron_models:
  needs: build-and-push

integration_tests:
  needs: [precompile_neuron_models, build-and-push]

backend_trtllm_cxx_tests:
  needs: build-and-push
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/build.yaml:21-331]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes TGI's testing infrastructure, including unit tests, integration tests, test fixtures, and the CI/CD pipeline that validates functionality across multiple hardware backends. For information about the build system itself, see [Build Systems](#7.1). For details on the CI/CD pipeline configuration, see [CI/CD Pipeline](#7.2).

The testing infrastructure encompasses:
- **Unit tests** for model implementations and core functionality
- **Integration tests** validating end-to-end request/response flows via Docker containers
- **Fixtures and utilities** providing test data, mock services, and response validation
- **CI/CD workflows** executing tests across seven hardware platforms (CUDA, TensorRT-LLM, ROCm, Intel XPU, Intel CPU, Neuron, Gaudi)

---

## Test Organization Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Test Directories"
        ServerTests["server/tests/<br/>Unit Tests"]
        IntegTests["integration-tests/<br/>Integration Tests"]

    end
    
    subgraph "Unit Test Modules"
        ModelTests["tests/models/<br/>test_bloom.py<br/>test_causal_lm.py<br/>test_seq2seq_lm.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Test Components"
        Conftest["conftest.py<br/>Fixtures & Config"]
        NeuronFix["fixtures/neuron/<br/>service.py<br/>export_models.py"]
        GaudiFix["fixtures/gaudi/<br/>service.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CI Workflows"
        TestsYAML[".github/workflows/tests.yaml<br/>Unit Tests"]
        BuildYAML[".github/workflows/build.yaml<br/>Build & Integration Tests"]
        CIBuildYAML[".github/workflows/ci_build.yaml<br/>Matrix Strategy"]
    end
    
    ServerTests --> ModelTests
    IntegTests --> Conftest
    IntegTests --> Fixtures
    Fixtures --> NeuronFix
    Fixtures --> GaudiFix
    
    TestsYAML -.->|Runs| ServerTests
    BuildYAML -.->|Runs| IntegTests
    CIBuildYAML -.->|Triggers| BuildYAML
```

**Sources:** [integration-tests/conftest.py:1-812](), [server/tests/models/test_bloom.py:1-364](), [.github/workflows/tests.yaml:1-68](), [.github/workflows/build.yaml:1-331]()
